nodes.body_text: pub const INPUT_SPAN: usize = SPLIT_FRAMES * HOP + PAD;

nodes.name: NET_COUNT
nodes.body_text: pub const NET_COUNT: usize = 4;

nodes.name: NET_VOCALS
nodes.body_text: pub const NET_VOCALS: usize = 0;

nodes.name: NET_DRUMS
nodes.body_text: pub const NET_DRUMS: usize = 1;

nodes.name: NET_BASS
nodes.body_text: pub const NET_BASS: usize = 2;

nodes.name: NET_OTHER
nodes.body_text: pub const NET_OTHER: usize = 3;

nodes.name: owned_start
nodes.body_text: pub fn owned_start(c: usize) -> usize { if c == 0 { 0 } else { c * STEP + MARGIN } }

nodes.name: owned_end
nodes.body_text: pub fn owned_end(c: usize) -> usize { (c + 1) * STEP + MARGIN }

nodes.name: chunk_containing
nodes.body_text: pub fn chunk_containing(frame: usize) -> usize { if frame < owned_end(0) { 0 } else { (frame - MARGIN) / STEP } }

nodes.name: chunk_count
nodes.body_text: pub fn chunk_count(frames: usize) -> usize { if frames == 0 { 0 } else { chunk_containing(frames - 1) + 1 } }

nodes.name: span_start
nodes.body_text: pub fn span_start(c: usize) -> i64 { if c == 0 { -(PAD as i64) } else { owned_start(c) as i64 - MARGIN as i64 - PAD as i64 } }

nodes.name: tests
nodes.body_text: mod tests { use super::*; #[test] fn derived_constants_match_the_mobile_header() { assert_eq!(SPEC_BINS, 2049); assert_eq!(PAD, 3072); assert_eq!(STEP, 520_192); assert_eq!(INPUT_SPAN, 527_360); } #[test] fn grid_tiles_the_timeline_without_gaps() { for c in 0..20 { assert_eq!(owned_end(c), owned_start(c + 1)); } for frame in [0, 1, 520_703, 520_704, 520_705, 3_000_000, 10_000_000] { let c = chunk_containing(frame); assert!(owned_start(c) <= frame && frame < owned_end(c), "frame {frame} chunk {c}"); } } #[test] fn owned_range_lies_inside_the_exact_region() { // The exact region of a chunk is the samples all 4 of whose frames are in it. for c in 0..5 { let span = span_start(c); let exact_lo = span + PAD as i64; let exact_hi = span + (SPLIT_FRAMES * HOP) as i64; assert!(exact_lo <= owned_start(c) as i64, "chunk {c} start"); assert!(owned_end(c) as i64 <= exact_hi, "chunk {c} end"); } } #[test] fn chunk_count_covers_the_track() { assert_eq!(chunk_count(0), 0); assert_eq!(chunk_count(1), 1); assert_eq!(chunk_count(owned_end(0)), 1); assert_eq!(chunk_count(owned_end(0) + 1), 2); let n = chunk_count(44_100 * 240); assert!(owned_end(n - 1) >= 44_100 * 240 && owned_end(n - 2) < 44_100 * 240); } }

nodes.body_text: fn grid_tiles_the_timeline_without_gaps() { for c in 0..20 { assert_eq!(owned_end(c), owned_start(c + 1)); } for frame in [0, 1, 520_703, 520_704, 520_705, 3_000_000, 10_000_000] { let c = chunk_containing(frame); assert!(owned_start(c) <= frame && frame < owned_end(c), "frame {frame} chunk {c}"); } }

nodes.name: owned_range_lies_inside_the_exact_region
nodes.body_text: fn owned_range_lies_inside_the_exact_region() { // The exact region of a chunk is the samples all 4 of whose frames are in it. for c in 0..5 { let span = span_start(c); let exact_lo = span + PAD as i64; let exact_hi = span + (SPLIT_FRAMES * HOP) as i64; assert!(exact_lo <= owned_start(c) as i64, "chunk {c} start"); assert!(owned_end(c) as i64 <= exact_hi, "chunk {c} end"); } }

nodes.name: MARKER
nodes.body_text: const MARKER: &str = "ready.json";

nodes.name: is_ready
nodes.body_text: pub fn is_ready(root: &Path, manifest: &Manifest) -> bool { let dir = root.join(&manifest.dir_name); let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join(MARKER)) else { return false }; let Ok(marker) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { return false }; manifest.files.iter().all(|f| { marker["files"][&f.name] == f.sha256.as_str() && std::fs::metadata(dir.join(&f.name)).is_ok_and(|m| m.len() == f.size) }) }

nodes.name: model_dir
nodes.body_text: pub fn model_dir(root: &Path, manifest: &Manifest) -> PathBuf { root.join(&manifest.dir_name) }

nodes.name: download
nodes.body_text: pub fn download( root: &Path, manifest: &Manifest, progress: &dyn Fn(u64, u64), cancel: &AtomicBool, ) -> Result<(), StemError> { let dir = model_dir(root, manifest); std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(io)?; let total = manifest.total_bytes(); let mut done = 0u64; // A marker from an older/partial install must not outlive a re-download. let _ = std::fs::remove_file(dir.join(MARKER)); let client = reqwest::blocking::Client::builder() .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(20)) .timeout(Duration::from_secs(900)) .build() .map_err(|e| StemError::Network(e.to_string()))?; for f in &manifest.files { let target = dir.join(&f.name); if verified_on_disk(&target, f) { done += f.size; progress(done, total); continue; } let mut last_err = StemError::Network("no download URL".into()); let mut ok = false; for url in &f.urls { match fetch_verified(&client, url, &target, f, &mut |n| progress(done + n, total), cancel) { Ok(()) => { ok = true; break; } Err(StemError::Aborted) => return Err(StemError::Aborted), Err(e) => last_err = e, } } if !ok { return Err(last_err); } done += f.size; progress(done, total); } let files: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = manifest .files .iter() .map(|f| (f.name.clone(), serde_json::Value::String(f.sha256.clone()))) .collect(); std::fs::write(dir.join(MARKER), serde_json::json!({ "files": files }).to_string()).map_err(io) }

nodes.name: verified_on_disk
nodes.body_text: fn verified_on_disk(path: &Path, f: &RemoteFile) -> bool { std::fs::metadata(path).is_ok_and(|m| m.len() == f.size) && hash_file(path).is_ok_and(|h| h == f.sha256) }

nodes.name: hash_file
nodes.body_text: pub(crate) fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<String> { let mut file = std::fs::File::open(path)?; let mut hasher = Sha256::new(); let mut buf = vec![0u8; 1 << 16]; loop { let n = file.read(&mut buf)?; if n == 0 { break; } hasher.update(&buf[..n]); } Ok(hex(&hasher.finalize())) }

nodes.name: hex
nodes.body_text: fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String { bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect() }

nodes.name: fetch_verified
nodes.body_text: pub(crate) fn fetch_verified( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str, target: &Path, f: &RemoteFile, on_bytes: &mut dyn FnMut(u64), cancel: &AtomicBool, ) -> Result<(), StemError> { let part = PathBuf::from(format!("{}.part", target.display())); let result = (|| { let mut resp = client .get(url) .send() .and_then(|r| r.error_for_status()) .map_err(|e| StemError::Network(e.to_string()))?; let mut out = std::fs::File::create(&part).map_err(io)?; let mut hasher = Sha256::new(); let mut buf = vec![0u8; 1 << 16]; let mut got = 0u64; loop { if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) { return Err(StemError::Aborted); } let n = resp.read(&mut buf).map_err(|e| StemError::Network(e.to_string()))?; if n == 0 { break; } got += n as u64; if got > f.size { return Err(StemError::Network(format!("{url} sent more than the expected {} bytes", f.size))); } hasher.update(&buf[..n]); out.write_all(&buf[..n]).map_err(io)?; on_bytes(got); } out.flush().map_err(io)?; drop(out); let digest = hex(&hasher.finalize()); if got != f.size || digest != f.sha256 { return Err(StemError::Network(format!( "{} failed its integrity check (got {got} bytes, sha256 {digest})", f.name ))); } std::fs::rename(&part, target).map_err(io) })(); if result.is_err() { let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&part); } result }

nodes.name: fill_store
nodes.body_text: pub fn fill_store( runner: &mut dyn NetRunner, store: &StemStore, cancel: &AtomicBool, mut on_chunk: impl FnMut(usize, usize), ) -> Result<(), StemError> { let mut scratch = ChunkScratch::new(); while let Some(c) = store.next_missing() { if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) { return Err(StemError::Aborted); } let out = chunk::separate_chunk(runner, &mut scratch, store.mix(), c)?; if !store.publish(c, out) { return Err(StemError::Engine(format!("chunk {c} could not be stored"))); } on_chunk(store.ready_count(), store.chunk_total()); } Ok(()) }

nodes.name: fill
nodes.body_text: pub fn fill( &self, store: &StemStore, cancel: &AtomicBool, on_chunk: impl FnMut(usize, usize), ) -> Result<(), StemError> { if !self.available() { return Err(StemError::Unavailable); } let mut guard = self .nets .lock() .map_err(|_| StemError::Engine("separator lock poisoned".into()))?; if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) { return Err(StemError::Aborted); } if guard.is_none() { if let Some(root) = &self.runtime_root { if !runtime::is_ready(root) { return Err(StemError::Unavailable); } runtime::activate(root)?; } *guard = Some(OrtNets::load(&self.model_dir)?); } let nets = guard.as_mut().expect("just loaded"); fill_store(nets, store, cancel, on_chunk) }

nodes.name: soft_masks

nodes.body_text: pub fn soft_masks(vocals: &mut [f32], drums: &mut [f32], bass: &[f32], other: &[f32]) { debug_assert!(vocals.len() == drums.len() && vocals.len() == bass.len() && vocals.len() == other.len()); for i in 0..vocals.len() { let sum = vocals[i] * vocals[i] + drums[i] * drums[i] + bass[i] * bass[i]; let total = sum + other[i] * other[i] + TOTAL_EPS; vocals[i] = (vocals[i] * vocals[i] + NUMERATOR_EPS) / total; drums[i] = (drums[i] * drums[i] + NUMERATOR_EPS) / total; } }

nodes.body_text: fn four_masks_sum_to_one() { let v0 = [0.3f32, 0.0, 2.0, 1e-6]; let d0 = [0.1f32, 0.0, 0.5, 4.0]; let b0 = [0.8f32, 0.0, 0.1, 0.0]; let o0 = [0.2f32, 0.0, 0.7, 1e-3]; let (mut v, mut d) = (v0, d0); soft_masks(&mut v, &mut d, &b0, &o0); for i in 0..4 { // masks of bass/other by the same formula let total = v0[i].powi(2) + d0[i].powi(2) + b0[i].powi(2) + o0[i].powi(2) + TOTAL_EPS; let mb = (b0[i].powi(2) + NUMERATOR_EPS) / total; let mo = (o0[i].powi(2) + NUMERATOR_EPS) / total; assert!((v[i] + d[i] + mb + mo - 1.0).abs() < 1e-5, "bin {i}"); } }

nodes.name: row_means_average_each_row

nodes.body_text: fn load_inner(dir: &Path) -> Result<Self, StemError> { let threads = intra_threads(); let mut sessions = Vec::with_capacity(NET_COUNT); for file in NET_FILES { let session = Session::builder() .and_then(|b| b.with_optimization_level(GraphOptimizationLevel::Level2)) .and_then(|b| b.with_intra_threads(threads)) .and_then(|b| b.with_inter_threads(1)) .and_then(|b| b.with_memory_pattern(false)) .and_then(|b| b.with_config_entry("session.intra_op.allow_spinning", "0")) .and_then(|b| { b.with_execution_providers([CPUExecutionProvider::default() .with_arena_allocator(false) .build()]) }) .and_then(|b| b.commit_from_file(dir.join(file))) .map_err(ort_err)?; sessions.push(session); } Ok(Self { sessions }) }

nodes.body_text: fn run(&mut self, net: usize, mag: &[f32], out: &mut [f32]) -> Result<(), StemError> { debug_assert_eq!(mag.len(), TENSOR_LEN); let session = self .sessions .get_mut(net) .ok_or_else(|| StemError::Engine(format!("no net {net}")))?; let input = Tensor::from_array(([2usize, 1, SPLIT_FRAMES, NET_BINS], mag.to_vec())).map_err(ort_err)?; let outputs = session.run(ort::inputs!["x" => input]).map_err(ort_err)?; let (_, data) = outputs["y"].try_extract_tensor::<f32>().map_err(ort_err)?; if data.len() != out.len() { return Err(StemError::Engine(format!( "net {net} returned {} values, expected {}", data.len(), out.len() ))); } out.copy_from_slice(data); Ok(()) }

nodes.body_text: pub fn install(root: &Path, progress: &dyn Fn(u64, u64), cancel: &AtomicBool) -> Result<(), StemError> { let Some(spec) = spec() else { return Err(StemError::Unavailable); }; if is_ready(root) { return Ok(()); } let manifest = Manifest { dir_name: format!("runtime-dl-{ORT_VERSION}"), files: vec![RemoteFile { name: spec.asset.to_string(), size: spec.size, sha256: spec.sha256.to_string(), urls: vec![format!( "https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/download/v{ORT_VERSION}/{}", spec.asset )], }], }; download::download(root, &manifest, progress, cancel)?; let dl_dir = download::model_dir(root, &manifest); let archive = dl_dir.join(spec.asset); let dest_dir = root.join("runtime"); std::fs::create_dir_all(&dest_dir).map_err(io)?; let part = dest_dir.join(format!("{}.part", spec.lib_name)); extract(&archive, spec.archive, spec.member, &part)?; std::fs::rename(&part, dest_dir.join(spec.lib_name)).map_err(io)?; let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(dl_dir); Ok(()) }

nodes.name: extract
nodes.signature: fn extract(archive: &Path, kind: Archive, member: &str, out: &Path) -> Result<(), StemError>
nodes.body_text: fn extract(archive: &Path, kind: Archive, member: &str, out: &Path) -> Result<(), StemError> { let file = std::fs::File::open(archive).map_err(io)?; match kind { Archive::TarGz => { let mut tar = tar::Archive::new(flate2::read::GzDecoder::new(file)); for entry in tar.entries().map_err(io)? { let mut entry = entry.map_err(io)?; let path = entry.path().map_err(io)?.to_path_buf(); if below_top_dir(&path) == Some(member) && entry.header().entry_type().is_file() { let mut dst = std::fs::File::create(out).map_err(io)?; std::io::copy(&mut entry, &mut dst).map_err(io)?; return Ok(()); } } } Archive::Zip => { let mut zip = zip::ZipArchive::new(file).map_err(io)?; for i in 0..zip.len() { let mut entry = zip.by_index(i).map_err(io)?; let name = entry.name().to_string(); if below_top_dir(Path::new(&name)) == Some(member) && entry.is_file() { let mut dst = std::fs::File::create(out).map_err(io)?; let mut buf = Vec::new(); entry.read_to_end(&mut buf).map_err(io)?; std::io::Write::write_all(&mut dst, &buf).map_err(io)?; return Ok(()); } } } } Err(StemError::Io(format!("{member} not found in the ONNX Runtime archive"))) }

nodes.name: OLA_GAIN
nodes.body_text: pub const OLA_GAIN: f32 = 1.5;

nodes.name: periodic_hann
nodes.body_text: pub fn periodic_hann() -> Vec<f32> { (0..NFFT) .map(|n| (0.5 - 0.5 * (std::f64::consts::TAU * n as f64 / NFFT as f64).cos()) as f32) .collect() }

nodes.name: Stft
nodes.body_text: pub struct Stft { window: Vec<f32>, fwd: Arc<dyn RealToComplex<f32>>, inv: Arc<dyn ComplexToReal<f32>>, frame: Vec<f32>, fwd_scratch: Vec<Complex32>, inv_scratch: Vec<Complex32>, inv_spec: Vec<Complex32>, }

nodes.name: default
nodes.body_text: fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }

nodes.name: new
nodes.body_text: pub fn new() -> Self { let mut planner = RealFftPlanner::<f32>::new(); let fwd = planner.plan_fft_forward(NFFT); let inv = planner.plan_fft_inverse(NFFT); Self { window: periodic_hann(), frame: vec![0.0; NFFT], fwd_scratch: fwd.make_scratch_vec(), inv_scratch: inv.make_scratch_vec(), inv_spec: vec![Complex32::new(0.0, 0.0); SPEC_BINS], fwd, inv, } }

nodes.name: window
nodes.body_text: pub fn window(&self) -> &[f32] { &self.window }

nodes.name: forward
nodes.signature: pub fn forward(&mut self, samples: &[f32], spec: &mut [Complex32])
nodes.body_text: pub fn forward(&mut self, samples: &[f32], spec: &mut [Complex32]) { debug_assert_eq!(samples.len(), NFFT); debug_assert_eq!(spec.len(), SPEC_BINS); for ((f, &s), &w) in self.frame.iter_mut().zip(samples).zip(&self.window) { *f = s * w; } self.fwd .process_with_scratch(&mut self.frame, spec, &mut self.fwd_scratch) .expect("fft sizes are fixed"); }

nodes.name: inverse
nodes.signature: pub fn inverse(&mut self, spec: &[Complex32], out: &mut [f32])
nodes.body_text: pub fn inverse(&mut self, spec: &[Complex32], out: &mut [f32]) { debug_assert_eq!(spec.len(), SPEC_BINS); debug_assert_eq!(out.len(), NFFT); self.inv_spec.copy_from_slice(spec); // A real signal's DC and Nyquist bins are real. self.inv_spec[0].im = 0.0; self.inv_spec[SPEC_BINS - 1].im = 0.0; self.inv .process_with_scratch(&mut self.inv_spec, out, &mut self.inv_scratch) .expect("fft sizes are fixed"); let scale = 1.0 / NFFT as f32; for (o, &w) in out.iter_mut().zip(&self.window) { *o *= scale * w; } }

nodes.name: tests
nodes.body_text: mod tests { use super::*; use crate::config::HOP; #[test] fn window_is_periodic_not_symmetric() { let w = periodic_hann(); assert_eq!(w[0], 0.0); // Periodic: peak is exactly 1 at N/2 and the window is NOT symmetric // about its midpoint sample index (N-1)/2. assert!((w[NFFT / 2] - 1.0).abs() < 1e-7); assert!((w[1] - w[NFFT - 1]).abs() < 1e-7, "w[n] == w[N-n]"); assert!(w[NFFT - 1] > 0.0 && w[NFFT - 1] < 1e-5); // numpy: np.hanning(N+1)[:-1][1] let expect = 0.5 - 0.5 * (std::f64::consts::TAU / NFFT as f64).cos(); assert!((f64::from(w[1]) - expect).abs() < 1e-9); } #[test] fn squared_windows_overlap_add_to_the_ola_gain() { let w = periodic_hann(); for n in 0..HOP { let s: f32 = (0..NFFT / HOP).map(|k| w[n + k * HOP].powi(2)).sum(); assert!((s - OLA_GAIN).abs() < 1e-5, "n={n} sum={s}"); } } #[test] fn forward_inverse_overlap_add_reconstructs_the_signal() { let mut stft = Stft::new(); let total = NFFT + HOP * 12; let x: Vec<f32> = (0..total) .map(|i| (i as f32 * 0.01).sin() * 0.5 + (i as f32 * 0.37).cos() * 0.2) .collect(); let mut acc = vec![0.0f32; total]; let mut spec = vec![Complex32::new(0.0, 0.0); SPEC_BINS]; let mut frame = vec![0.0f32; NFFT]; let mut at = 0; while at + NFFT <= total { stft.forward(&x[at..at + NFFT], &mut spec); stft.inverse(&spec, &mut frame); for (a, f) in acc[at..at + NFFT].iter_mut().zip(&frame) { *a += f; } at += HOP; } // Fully covered region: [NFFT - HOP, total - (NFFT - HOP)). for i in (NFFT - HOP)..(total - (NFFT - HOP)) { let y = acc[i] / OLA_GAIN; assert!((y - x[i]).abs() < 1e-4, "i={i} y={y} x={}", x[i]); } } }

nodes.name: new
nodes.body_text: pub fn new(mix: Vec<f32>) -> Arc<Self> { let n = chunk_count(mix.len() / 2); Arc::new(Self { chunks: (0..n).map(|_| OnceLock::new()).collect(), mix, ready: AtomicUsize::new(0), wanted: AtomicUsize::new(0), }) }

nodes.name: mix
nodes.body_text: pub fn mix(&self) -> &[f32] { &self.mix }

nodes.name: frames
nodes.body_text: pub fn frames(&self) -> usize { self.mix.len() / 2 }

nodes.name: chunk_total
nodes.body_text: pub fn chunk_total(&self) -> usize { self.chunks.len() }

nodes.name: ready_count
nodes.body_text: pub fn ready_count(&self) -> usize { self.ready.load(Ordering::Acquire) }

nodes.name: is_complete
nodes.body_text: pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool { self.ready_count() == self.chunks.len() }

nodes.name: is_ready
nodes.signature: pub fn is_ready(&self, c: usize) -> bool
nodes.body_text: pub fn is_ready(&self, c: usize) -> bool { self.chunks.get(c).is_some_and(|s| s.get().is_some()) }

nodes.name: publish
nodes.signature: pub fn publish(&self, c: usize, out: ChunkOut) -> bool
nodes.body_text: pub fn publish(&self, c: usize, out: ChunkOut) -> bool { let Some(slot) = self.chunks.get(c) else { return false }; let want = (owned_end(c).min(self.frames()) - owned_start(c)) * 2; if out.vocals.len() != want || out.drums.len() != want { return false; } if slot.set(out).is_ok() { self.ready.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Release); true } else { false } }

nodes.name: set_wanted
nodes.body_text: pub fn set_wanted(&self, frame: usize) { self.wanted.store(frame.min(self.frames()), Ordering::Relaxed); }

nodes.name: wanted
nodes.body_text: pub fn wanted(&self) -> usize { self.wanted.load(Ordering::Relaxed) }

nodes.name: next_missing
nodes.body_text: pub fn next_missing(&self) -> Option<usize> { let n = self.chunks.len(); if n == 0 { return None; } let from = chunk_containing(self.wanted().min(self.frames().saturating_sub(1))); (0..n).map(|i| (from + i) % n).find(|&c| !self.is_ready(c)) }

nodes.name: run_at
nodes.signature: pub fn run_at(&self, frame: usize) -> Option<Run<'_>>
nodes.body_text: pub fn run_at(&self, frame: usize) -> Option<Run<'_>> { if frame >= self.frames() { return None; } let c = chunk_containing(frame); let out = self.chunks.get(c)?.get()?; let offset = frame - owned_start(c); Some(Run { from: frame, vocals: &out.vocals[offset * 2..], drums: &out.drums[offset * 2..], }) }

nodes.name: fill_from
nodes.signature: pub fn fill_from(&self, vocals: &[f32], drums: &[f32]) -> bool
nodes.body_text: pub fn fill_from(&self, vocals: &[f32], drums: &[f32]) -> bool { if vocals.len() != self.mix.len() || drums.len() != self.mix.len() { return false; } for c in 0..self.chunks.len() { let lo = owned_start(c) * 2; let hi = owned_end(c).min(self.frames()) * 2; self.publish( c, ChunkOut { vocals: vocals[lo..hi].to_vec(), drums: drums[lo..hi].to_vec(), }, ); } true }

nodes.name: assemble
nodes.body_text: pub fn assemble(&self) -> Option<(Vec<f32>, Vec<f32>)> { if !self.is_complete() { return None; } let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(self.mix.len()); let mut d = Vec::with_capacity(self.mix.len()); for slot in &self.chunks { let c = slot.get()?; v.extend_from_slice(&c.vocals); d.extend_from_slice(&c.drums); } Some((v, d)) }

nodes.body_text: mod tests { use super::*; use crate::config::STEP; fn out(c: usize, frames: usize, value: f32) -> ChunkOut { let n = (owned_end(c).min(frames) - owned_start(c)) * 2; ChunkOut { vocals: vec![value; n], drums: vec![-value; n] } } #[test] fn publishes_and_serves_runs() { let frames = STEP * 2; let store = StemStore::new(vec![0.0; frames * 2]); assert_eq!(store.chunk_total(), 2); assert!(store.run_at(10).is_none(), "nothing ready yet"); assert!(store.publish(0, out(0, frames, 0.5))); assert!(!store.publish(0, out(0, frames, 0.5)), "no double publish"); let run = store.run_at(100).unwrap(); assert_eq!(run.vocals[0], 0.5); assert_eq!(run.drums[0], -0.5); assert_eq!(run.vocals.len(), (owned_end(0) - 100) * 2); assert!(store.run_at(owned_end(0)).is_none(), "next chunk not ready"); } #[test] fn wrong_length_is_refused() { let store = StemStore::new(vec![0.0; 2000]); assert!(!store.publish(0, ChunkOut { vocals: vec![0.0; 10], drums: vec![0.0; 10] })); assert_eq!(store.ready_count(), 0); } #[test] fn worker_follows_the_playhead_then_wraps() { let frames = STEP * 5; let store = StemStore::new(vec![0.0; frames * 2]); let n = store.chunk_total(); store.set_wanted(owned_start(3) + 10); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(3)); store.publish(3, out(3, frames, 0.1)); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(4)); store.publish(4, out(4, frames, 0.1)); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(5 % n), "then onward to the end of the track"); // the listener seeks back: the worker jumps there. store.set_wanted(0); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(0)); for c in 0..n { store.publish(c, out(c, frames, 0.1)); } assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), None); assert!(store.is_complete()); } #[test] fn fill_from_cache_round_trips_through_assemble() { let frames = STEP + 40_000; let mix: Vec<f32> = (0..frames * 2).map(|i| i as f32).collect(); let store = StemStore::new(mix); let v: Vec<f32> = (0..frames * 2).map(|i| i as f32 * 0.5).collect(); let d: Vec<f32> = (0..frames * 2).map(|i| -(i as f32)).collect(); assert!(store.fill_from(&v, &d)); let (v2, d2) = store.assemble().unwrap(); assert_eq!(v, v2); assert_eq!(d, d2); assert!(!store.fill_from(&v[..10], &d[..10]), "wrong length refused"); } }

nodes.name: out
nodes.signature: fn out(c: usize, frames: usize, value: f32) -> ChunkOut
nodes.body_text: fn out(c: usize, frames: usize, value: f32) -> ChunkOut { let n = (owned_end(c).min(frames) - owned_start(c)) * 2; ChunkOut { vocals: vec![value; n], drums: vec![-value; n] } }

nodes.name: publishes_and_serves_runs
nodes.body_text: fn publishes_and_serves_runs() { let frames = STEP * 2; let store = StemStore::new(vec![0.0; frames * 2]); assert_eq!(store.chunk_total(), 2); assert!(store.run_at(10).is_none(), "nothing ready yet"); assert!(store.publish(0, out(0, frames, 0.5))); assert!(!store.publish(0, out(0, frames, 0.5)), "no double publish"); let run = store.run_at(100).unwrap(); assert_eq!(run.vocals[0], 0.5); assert_eq!(run.drums[0], -0.5); assert_eq!(run.vocals.len(), (owned_end(0) - 100) * 2); assert!(store.run_at(owned_end(0)).is_none(), "next chunk not ready"); }

nodes.name: wrong_length_is_refused
nodes.body_text: fn wrong_length_is_refused() { let store = StemStore::new(vec![0.0; 2000]); assert!(!store.publish(0, ChunkOut { vocals: vec![0.0; 10], drums: vec![0.0; 10] })); assert_eq!(store.ready_count(), 0); }

nodes.name: worker_follows_the_playhead_then_wraps
nodes.body_text: fn worker_follows_the_playhead_then_wraps() { let frames = STEP * 5; let store = StemStore::new(vec![0.0; frames * 2]); let n = store.chunk_total(); store.set_wanted(owned_start(3) + 10); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(3)); store.publish(3, out(3, frames, 0.1)); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(4)); store.publish(4, out(4, frames, 0.1)); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(5 % n), "then onward to the end of the track"); // the listener seeks back: the worker jumps there. store.set_wanted(0); assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), Some(0)); for c in 0..n { store.publish(c, out(c, frames, 0.1)); } assert_eq!(store.next_missing(), None); assert!(store.is_complete()); }

nodes.name: fill_from_cache_round_trips_through_assemble
nodes.body_text: fn fill_from_cache_round_trips_through_assemble() { let frames = STEP + 40_000; let mix: Vec<f32> = (0..frames * 2).map(|i| i as f32).collect(); let store = StemStore::new(mix); let v: Vec<f32> = (0..frames * 2).map(|i| i as f32 * 0.5).collect(); let d: Vec<f32> = (0..frames * 2).map(|i| -(i as f32)).collect(); assert!(store.fill_from(&v, &d)); let (v2, d2) = store.assemble().unwrap(); assert_eq!(v, v2); assert_eq!(d, d2); assert!(!store.fill_from(&v[..10], &d[..10]), "wrong length refused"); }

nodes.name: read_f32
nodes.body_text: fn read_f32(path: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<f32> { std::fs::read(path) .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e}", path.display())) .chunks_exact(4) .map(|b| f32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]])) .collect() }

nodes.name: sdr_db
nodes.body_text: fn sdr_db(r: &[f32], x: &[f32]) -> f64 { let sig: f64 = r.iter().map(|&v| f64::from(v).powi(2)).sum(); let err: f64 = r.iter().zip(x).map(|(&a, &b)| (f64::from(a) - f64::from(b)).powi(2)).sum(); 10.0 * (sig / err.max(1e-30)).log10() }

nodes.name: max_abs
nodes.body_text: fn max_abs(r: &[f32], x: &[f32]) -> f32 { r.iter().zip(x).map(|(a, b)| (a - b).abs()).fold(0.0, f32::max) }

nodes.name: parity_with_the_mobile_cpp_engine
nodes.body_text: fn parity_with_the_mobile_cpp_engine() { let mix = read_f32(&env_path("HM_STEMS_PARITY_INPUT")); let dir = env_path("HM_STEMS_PARITY_DIR"); let mut nets = OrtNets::load(&env_path("HM_STEMS_MODEL_DIR")).expect("load nets"); let mut scratch = ChunkScratch::new(); let mut compared = 0; for c in 0..8 { let v_ref = dir.join(format!("chunk{c}.vocals.f32")); if !v_ref.exists() { continue; } let d_ref = dir.join(format!("chunk{c}.drums.f32")); let out = separate_chunk(&mut nets, &mut scratch, &mix, c).expect("separate"); let (rv, rd) = (read_f32(&v_ref), read_f32(&d_ref)); assert_eq!(out.vocals.len(), rv.len(), "chunk {c} length"); let (sv, sd) = (sdr_db(&rv, &out.vocals), sdr_db(&rd, &out.drums)); let (ev, ed) = (max_abs(&rv, &out.vocals), max_abs(&rd, &out.drums)); let energy: f64 = rv.iter().chain(&rd).map(|&v| f64::from(v).powi(2)).sum(); println!( "chunk {c}: frames {} vocals SDR {sv:.1} dB (max err {ev:.2e}) drums SDR {sd:.1} dB (max err {ed:.2e}) ref vocals+drums energy {energy:.1}", rv.len() / 2 ); assert!(energy > 1.0, "reference is near silent: the test would prove nothing"); assert!(sv > 40.0 && sd > 40.0, "chunk {c} below the 40 dB parity bar"); compared += 1; } assert!(compared >= 2, "expected at least two reference chunks in {}", dir.display()); }

nodes.name: real_nets_partition_the_mix_and_report_speed
nodes.body_text: fn real_nets_partition_the_mix_and_report_speed() { let mix = read_f32(&env_path("HM_STEMS_PARITY_INPUT")); let frames = mix.len() / 2; let store = StemStore::new(mix.clone()); let sep = hm_stems::Separator::new(env_path("HM_STEMS_MODEL_DIR"), std::env::temp_dir()); let t0 = Instant::now(); let mut first = None; sep.fill(&store, &AtomicBool::new(false), |ready, _| { first.get_or_insert(t0.elapsed()); eprintln!(" chunk {ready}/{} at {:.2}s", store.chunk_total(), t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64()); }) .expect("fill"); let took = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64(); let secs = frames as f64 / 44_100.0; println!( "separated {secs:.1} s of audio in {took:.2} s (incl. model load) = {:.1}x real time; first chunk after {:.2} s", secs / took, first.unwrap().as_secs_f64() ); let (v, d) = store.assemble().expect("complete"); assert_eq!(v.len(), mix.len()); // Physical sanity: vocals + drums never exceed the mix's energy (the other // two masks take their share), and both are non-trivial. let e = |x: &[f32]| x.iter().map(|&s| f64::from(s).powi(2)).sum::<f64>(); let (em, ev, ed) = (e(&mix), e(&v), e(&d)); println!("energy: mix {em:.1} vocals {ev:.1} drums {ed:.1}"); assert!(ev > 0.0 && ed > 0.0 && ev + ed <= em * 1.05, "stems must partition, not add, energy"); // chunk seams: no jump at the boundary between chunk 0 and 1. let b = owned_start(1) * 2; let jump = (v[b] - v[b - 2]).abs(); let typical = (b - 2000..b).step_by(2).map(|i| (v[i + 2] - v[i]).abs()).fold(0.0, f32::max); println!("seam jump {jump:.5} vs local max step {typical:.5}"); assert!(jump <= typical * 2.0 + 1e-3, "audible seam at the chunk boundary"); let _ = owned_end(0); }

nodes.name: a_stale_ort_dylib_path_does_not_count_as_a_runtime
nodes.body_text: fn a_stale_ort_dylib_path_does_not_count_as_a_runtime() { let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("hm_stems_stale_env_{}", std::process::id())); let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root); std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap(); std::env::set_var("ORT_DYLIB_PATH", root.join("libonnxruntime.dylib")); if runtime::lib_path(&root).is_some() { // Nothing installed: the app must offer the download, not try to load. assert!(!runtime::is_ready(&root)); assert!(runtime::download_bytes(&root) > 0); // Installed under runtime/: that one is used. let lib = runtime::lib_path(&root).unwrap(); std::fs::create_dir_all(lib.parent().unwrap()).unwrap(); std::fs::write(&lib, b"lib").unwrap(); assert!(runtime::is_ready(&root)); assert_eq!(runtime::download_bytes(&root), 0); } // A developer override that exists still wins. let dev = root.join("dev-libonnxruntime"); std::fs::write(&dev, b"lib").unwrap(); std::env::set_var("ORT_DYLIB_PATH", &dev); let empty = root.join("empty-root"); assert!(runtime::is_ready(&empty)); let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(root); }

let playlist = Playlist::new(&projectm); if !preset_dir.is_empty() { playlist.add_dir(Path::new(&preset_dir)); } // Show the app's selected preset on open (else a first one to start with). match &initial_preset { Some(name) => projectm.load_preset_file(&preset_path(&preset_dir, name), false), None => playlist.next(), } // --- stdin reader (background thread → latest PCM + pending preset) --------- let pcm: Arc<Mutex<Vec<f32>>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())); nodes.name: REQUIRED_ANY
nodes.body_text: const REQUIRED_ANY: &[&[&str]] = &[ &["SAPISID", "__Secure-3PAPISID"], &["SID", "__Secure-1PSID", "__Secure-3PSID"], ];

nodes.name: YtCookie
nodes.body_text: pub struct YtCookie { pub name: String, pub value: String, pub domain: String, pub path: String, /// Unix seconds. `None` is a session cookie. pub expires: Option<i64>, pub secure: bool, pub http_only: bool, }

nodes.name: header
nodes.body_text: pub fn header(cookies: &[YtCookie]) -> String { let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new(); cookies .iter() .filter(|c| seen.insert(c.name.as_str())) .map(|c| format!("{}={}", c.name, c.value)) .collect::<Vec<_>>() .join("; ") }

is_signed_in
nodes.body_text: pub fn is_signed_in(cookies: &[YtCookie]) -> bool { REQUIRED_ANY.iter().all(|group| { group .iter() .any(|want| cookies.iter().any(|c| c.name == *want && !c.value.is_empty())) }) }

nodes.signature: pub fn prune_expired(cookies: Vec<YtCookie>, now: i64) -> Vec<YtCookie>
nodes.body_text: pub fn prune_expired(cookies: Vec<YtCookie>, now: i64) -> Vec<YtCookie> { cookies .into_iter() .filter(|c| c.expires.is_none_or(|e| e > now)) .collect() }

nodes.name: now_secs
nodes.body_text: pub fn now_secs() -> i64 { std::time::SystemTime::now() .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH) .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64) .unwrap_or(0) }

nodes.name: CHUNK_UTF16_UNITS
nodes.body_text: const CHUNK_UTF16_UNITS: usize = 1024;

nodes.name: service
nodes.body_text: fn service() -> String { match std::env::var("HM_KEYCHAIN_NAMESPACE") { Ok(ns) if !ns.is_empty() => format!("{SERVICE}.{ns}"), _ => SERVICE.to_string(), } }

nodes.name: entry_at
nodes.body_text: fn entry_at(account: &str) -> Result<keyring::Entry, String> { keyring::Entry::new(&service(), account).map_err(|e| format!("keychain unavailable: {e}")) }

nodes.name: chunk_account
nodes.body_text: fn chunk_account(base: &str, i: usize) -> String { format!("{base}-{i}") }

nodes.name: split_chunks
nodes.body_text: fn split_chunks(s: &str, max_units: usize) -> Vec<String> { let mut out = Vec::new(); let mut current = String::new(); let mut units = 0usize; for ch in s.chars() { let width = ch.len_utf16(); if units + width > max_units && !current.is_empty() { out.push(std::mem::take(&mut current)); units = 0; } current.push(ch); units += width; } if !current.is_empty() || out.is_empty() { out.push(current); } out }

nodes.name: save_at
nodes.body_text: fn save_at(account: &str, cookies: &[YtCookie]) -> Result<(), String> { let json = serde_json::to_string(cookies).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; let chunks = split_chunks(&json, CHUNK_UTF16_UNITS); for (i, chunk) in chunks.iter().enumerate() { entry_at(&chunk_account(account, i))? .set_password(chunk) .map_err(|e| format!("could not save credentials: {e}"))?; } // Drop leftover tail chunks from a previously longer jar — load reads until // the first missing index, so a stale tail would corrupt the reassembly. let mut i = chunks.len(); loop { match entry_at(&chunk_account(account, i))?.delete_credential() { Ok(()) => i += 1, Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => break, Err(e) => return Err(format!("could not clear stale credentials: {e}")), } } // And the pre-chunking single entry, which load would otherwise still see // as a (stale) fallback. match entry_at(account)?.delete_credential() { Ok(()) | Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => Ok(()), Err(e) => Err(format!("could not clear legacy credentials: {e}")), } }

nodes.name: load_at
nodes.body_text: fn load_at(account: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<YtCookie>>, String> { let mut json = String::new(); let mut i = 0usize; loop { match entry_at(&chunk_account(account, i))?.get_password() { Ok(chunk) => { json.push_str(&chunk); i += 1; } Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => break, Err(e) => return Err(format!("could not read credentials: {e}")), } } if i == 0 { // No chunked entries: fall back to the pre-chunking single entry so a // session saved by an older build survives the upgrade (the next save // migrates it to chunks and removes this one). match entry_at(account)?.get_password() { Ok(single) => json = single, Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => return Ok(None), Err(e) => return Err(format!("could not read credentials: {e}")), } } serde_json::from_str(&json) .map(Some) .map_err(|e| format!("stored credentials are corrupt: {e}")) }

nodes.name: clear_at
nodes.body_text: fn clear_at(account: &str) -> Result<(), String> { match entry_at(account)?.delete_credential() { Ok(()) | Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => {} Err(e) => return Err(format!("could not clear credentials: {e}")), } let mut i = 0usize; loop { match entry_at(&chunk_account(account, i))?.delete_credential() { Ok(()) => i += 1, Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => return Ok(()), Err(e) => return Err(format!("could not clear credentials: {e}")), } } }

nodes.name: save
nodes.body_text: pub fn save(cookies: &[YtCookie]) -> Result<(), String> { save_at(ACCOUNT, cookies) }

nodes.name: load
nodes.body_text: pub fn load() -> Result<Option<Vec<YtCookie>>, String> { load_at(ACCOUNT) }

nodes.name: clear
nodes.body_text: pub fn clear() -> Result<(), String> { clear_at(ACCOUNT) }

nodes.name: new
nodes.body_text: pub fn new(cookies: &[YtCookie]) -> Result<Self, String> { let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!( "hm-ytm-cookies-{}-{}.txt", std::process::id(), now_secs() )); let mut file = std::fs::File::create(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; // Narrow the mode before writing, so the contents are never briefly // world-readable. #[cfg(unix)] { use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt; file.set_permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600)) .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; } file.write_all(netscape(cookies).as_bytes()) .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; file.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; Ok(Self { path }) }

nodes.name: keychain_round_trips
nodes.body_text: fn keychain_round_trips() { const TEST_ACCOUNT: &str = "ytmusic-cookies-selftest"; assert_ne!( TEST_ACCOUNT, ACCOUNT, "the self-test must not address the account a user's session lives in" ); // Big enough to need several chunks — the single-entry version of this // jar is exactly what Windows rejected in the field. let c: Vec<YtCookie> = (0..25) .map(|i| cookie(&format!("COOKIE_{i}"), &"v".repeat(120))) .collect(); assert!( serde_json::to_string(&c).unwrap().encode_utf16().count() > 2560, "the round-trip jar must exceed the Windows blob cap to prove chunking" ); save_at(TEST_ACCOUNT, &c).expect("save to keychain"); let loaded = load_at(TEST_ACCOUNT) .expect("load from keychain") .expect("entry present"); assert_eq!(loaded, c); // A shorter save must retire the now-surplus tail chunks, or the next // load would reassemble new-head + stale-tail garbage. let shorter = vec![cookie("SAPISID", "x"), cookie("SID", "y")]; save_at(TEST_ACCOUNT, &shorter).expect("shorter save"); assert_eq!( load_at(TEST_ACCOUNT).expect("load shorter").expect("present"), shorter ); clear_at(TEST_ACCOUNT).expect("clear keychain"); assert!(load_at(TEST_ACCOUNT).expect("load after clear").is_none()); // Clearing a missing entry must be a no-op, not an error — sign-out // shouldn't fail just because there was nothing stored. clear_at(TEST_ACCOUNT).expect("clear is idempotent"); }

nodes.body_text: pub struct ExploreItem { pub kind: ExploreKind, /// What to open, read according to [`ExploreItem::kind`]: /// /// * [`ExploreKind::Album`] — the `MPREb…` browse id. /// * [`ExploreKind::Playlist`] — the **`VL`-prefixed** browse id. /// `GetPlaylistTracksQuery` sends this verbatim as `browseId`, so the bare /// `PL…` form answers HTTP 400. See [`playlist_browse_id`]. /// * [`ExploreKind::Artist`] — the `UC…` channel id. /// * [`ExploreKind::Song`] / [`ExploreKind::Video`] — the video id. These are /// rows rather than cards: they name a thing to play, not a page to open. pub id: String, pub title: String, /// The subtitle runs joined as YouTube wrote them ("Album • A Pass • 2019"). /// /// Deliberately not split into artist/year by run index: fixed-index reads of /// this exact field are what broke the library listing (`"Made for "` parsed /// as an author). Joining is honest and cannot misattribute. pub subtitle: Option<String>, pub thumbnail: Option<String>, /// The runs that link to an artist page, joined — so a collaboration reads /// "Dave, Tems" rather than whichever half sat at the index we picked. /// /// `None` where the row credits someone without linking them: a co-credit /// with no single channel to point at ("Tyga & Blxst") has no artist run at /// all, and inventing one from the byline's text is how that becomes wrong /// rather than absent. #[serde(default)] pub artist: Option<String>, /// The run that links to an album page, wherever the surface put it. #[serde(default)] pub album: Option<String>, /// Filled for rows that state a running time. Songs on a genre page don't — /// they state a view count instead — so this stays `None` rather than /// borrowing a number that isn't one. #[serde(default)] pub duration_secs: Option<f64>, /// Whether there's real footage, on the same terms as [`crate::YtTrack`]. #[serde(default)] pub has_video: bool, }

nodes.name: ExploreKind
nodes.body_text: pub enum ExploreKind { Playlist, Album, Artist, Song, Video, }

nodes.name: ExploreShelf
nodes.body_text: pub struct ExploreShelf { pub title: String, pub items: Vec<ExploreItem>, }

nodes.name: parse_page
nodes.body_text: pub fn parse_page(json: &Value) -> Vec<ExploreShelf> { let mut shelves = Vec::new(); collect_shelves(json, &mut shelves); shelves }

nodes.name: collect_shelves
nodes.body_text: fn collect_shelves(v: &Value, out: &mut Vec<ExploreShelf>) { match v { Value::Object(o) => { // Shelves don't nest, so a hit ends this subtree. if let Some(shelf) = o.get("musicCarouselShelfRenderer") { push_shelf(carousel_title(shelf), shelf.pointer("/contents"), out); return; } if let Some(shelf) = o.get("musicShelfRenderer") { push_shelf(shelf_title(shelf), shelf.pointer("/contents"), out); return; } if let Some(shelf) = o.get("musicCardShelfRenderer") { if let Some(parsed) = parse_card_shelf(shelf) { out.push(parsed); } return; } for val in o.values() { collect_shelves(val, out); } } Value::Array(a) => a.iter().for_each(|i| collect_shelves(i, out)), _ => {} } }

nodes.name: push_shelf
nodes.signature: fn push_shelf(title: Option<String>, contents: Option<&Value>, out: &mut Vec<ExploreShelf>)
nodes.body_text: fn push_shelf(title: Option<String>, contents: Option<&Value>, out: &mut Vec<ExploreShelf>) { let Some(title) = title else { return }; let items = parse_items(contents); if !items.is_empty() { out.push(ExploreShelf { title, items }); } }

nodes.name: carousel_title
nodes.body_text: fn carousel_title(shelf: &Value) -> Option<String> { shelf .pointer("/header/musicCarouselShelfBasicHeaderRenderer/title/runs/0/text") .and_then(Value::as_str) .map(str::to_string) }

nodes.name: shelf_title
nodes.body_text: fn shelf_title(shelf: &Value) -> Option<String> { shelf .pointer("/title/runs/0/text") .and_then(Value::as_str) .map(str::to_string) }

nodes.name: parse_card_shelf
nodes.body_text: fn parse_card_shelf(shelf: &Value) -> Option<ExploreShelf> { let mut items = Vec::new(); if let Some(card) = parse_card(shelf) { items.push(card); } items.extend(parse_items(shelf.pointer("/contents"))); (!items.is_empty()).then(|| ExploreShelf { title: TOP_RESULT.to_string(), items, }) }

nodes.name: parse_card
nodes.body_text: fn parse_card(card: &Value) -> Option<ExploreItem> { let endpoint = card .pointer("/onTap") .or_else(|| card.pointer("/title/runs/0/navigationEndpoint"))?; let subtitle_runs = card.pointer("/subtitle/runs"); open( endpoint, card.pointer("/title/runs/0/text").and_then(Value::as_str)?, join_runs(subtitle_runs), best_thumbnail(card.pointer("/thumbnail/musicThumbnailRenderer/thumbnail/thumbnails")), std::slice::from_ref(&subtitle_runs).iter().flatten().copied(), ) }

nodes.name: parse_items
nodes.body_text: fn parse_items(contents: Option<&Value>) -> Vec<ExploreItem> { contents .and_then(Value::as_array) .map(|items| items.iter().filter_map(parse_content).collect()) .unwrap_or_default() }

nodes.name: parse_content
nodes.body_text: fn parse_content(v: &Value) -> Option<ExploreItem> { if let Some(card) = v.pointer("/musicTwoRowItemRenderer") { return parse_item(card); } parse_row(v.pointer("/musicResponsiveListItemRenderer")?) }

nodes.name: parse_item
nodes.body_text: fn parse_item(card: &Value) -> Option<ExploreItem> { // Cards state their destination twice — on the item and on the title's first // run — and the two agree wherever both exist. The item is the reliable one: // a music-video card carries a watch endpoint there and nothing at all on // the title run. let endpoint = card .pointer("/navigationEndpoint") .or_else(|| card.pointer("/title/runs/0/navigationEndpoint"))?; let subtitle_runs = card.pointer("/subtitle/runs"); open( endpoint, card.pointer("/title/runs/0/text").and_then(Value::as_str)?, join_runs(subtitle_runs), best_thumbnail(card.pointer("/thumbnailRenderer/musicThumbnailRenderer/thumbnail/thumbnails")), std::slice::from_ref(&subtitle_runs).iter().flatten().copied(), ) }

nodes.name: open
nodes.body_text: fn open<'a>( endpoint: &Value, title: &str, subtitle: Option<String>, thumbnail: Option<String>, byline: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Value> + Clone, ) -> Option<ExploreItem> { if let Some(browse) = endpoint.pointer("/browseEndpoint") { let id = browse.pointer("/browseId").and_then(Value::as_str)?; let kind = classify(id, browse.pointer(PAGE_TYPE).and_then(Value::as_str))?; return Some(ExploreItem { kind, id: match kind { ExploreKind::Playlist => playlist_browse_id(id), _ => id.to_string(), }, title: title.to_string(), subtitle, thumbnail, artist: linked_runs(byline.clone(), ARTIST_PAGE), album: linked_runs(byline, ALBUM_PAGE), duration_secs: None, has_video: false, }); } // A watch endpoint names something to play rather than a page to open. let watch = endpoint.pointer("/watchEndpoint")?; let video_id = watch.pointer("/videoId").and_then(Value::as_str)?; let video_type = watch.pointer(CARD_VIDEO_TYPE).and_then(Value::as_str); is_music(video_type).then(|| ExploreItem { kind: kind_of(video_type), id: video_id.to_string(), title: title.to_string(), subtitle, thumbnail, artist: linked_runs(byline.clone(), ARTIST_PAGE), album: linked_runs(byline.clone(), ALBUM_PAGE), duration_secs: duration_of(byline), has_video: has_video(video_type), }) }

nodes.name: parse_row
nodes.body_text: fn parse_row(row: &Value) -> Option<ExploreItem> { let Some(video_id) = row .pointer("/playlistItemData/videoId") .and_then(Value::as_str) else { // No video id: a row that names a page rather than a track. let subtitle_runs = row.pointer("/subtitle/runs"); return open( row.pointer("/navigationEndpoint")?, &flex_text(row, 0)?, flex_text(row, 1).or_else(|| join_runs(subtitle_runs)), best_thumbnail(row.pointer("/thumbnail/musicThumbnailRenderer/thumbnail/thumbnails")), byline(row), ); }; let title = flex_text(row, 0)?; // A removed track keeps its row but not its identity. if title == "Song deleted" { return None; } let video_type = row.pointer(VIDEO_TYPE_PATH).and_then(Value::as_str); if !is_music(video_type) { return None; } Some(ExploreItem { kind: kind_of(video_type), id: video_id.to_string(), title, // Column 1 is what YouTube prints under the title on every surface, and // the columns after it vary (an album here, a play count there), so the // one column is the honest subtitle and the linked runs below carry the // rest. subtitle: flex_text(row, 1), thumbnail: best_thumbnail( row.pointer("/thumbnail/musicThumbnailRenderer/thumbnail/thumbnails"), ), artist: linked_runs(byline(row), ARTIST_PAGE), album: linked_runs(byline(row), ALBUM_PAGE), duration_secs: duration_of(byline(row)).or_else(|| fixed_duration(row)), has_video: has_video(video_type), }) }

nodes.name: byline
nodes.body_text: fn byline(row: &Value) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Value> + Clone { (1..) .map_while(move |col| { row.pointer(&format!( "/flexColumns/{col}/musicResponsiveListItemFlexColumnRenderer/text/runs" )) }) }

nodes.name: linked_runs
nodes.signature: fn linked_runs<'a>(byline: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Value>, page_type: &str) -> Option<String>
nodes.body_text: fn linked_runs<'a>(byline: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Value>, page_type: &str) -> Option<String> { let names: Vec<&str> = byline .filter_map(Value::as_array) .flatten() .filter(|run| { run.pointer("/navigationEndpoint/browseEndpoint") .and_then(|b| b.pointer(PAGE_TYPE)) .and_then(Value::as_str) == Some(page_type) }) .filter_map(|run| run.pointer("/text").and_then(Value::as_str)) .filter(|t| !t.trim().is_empty()) .collect(); (!names.is_empty()).then(|| names.join(", ")) }

nodes.name: duration_of
nodes.signature: fn duration_of<'a>(byline: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Value>) -> Option<f64>
nodes.body_text: fn duration_of<'a>(byline: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Value>) -> Option<f64> { byline .filter_map(Value::as_array) .flatten() .filter_map(|run| run.pointer("/text").and_then(Value::as_str)) .filter(|text| text.contains(':')) .find_map(parse_duration) }

nodes.name: fixed_duration
nodes.body_text: fn fixed_duration(row: &Value) -> Option<f64> { let text = row.pointer("/fixedColumns/0/musicResponsiveListItemFixedColumnRenderer/text")?; join_runs(text.pointer("/runs")) .or_else(|| { text.pointer("/simpleText") .and_then(Value::as_str) .map(str::to_string) }) .as_deref() .and_then(parse_duration) }

nodes.name: kind_of
nodes.body_text: fn kind_of(video_type: Option<&str>) -> ExploreKind { if has_video(video_type) { ExploreKind::Video } else { ExploreKind::Song } }

nodes.name: classify
nodes.body_text: fn classify(browse_id: &str, page_type: Option<&str>) -> Option<ExploreKind> { match page_type { Some(ALBUM_PAGE) => Some(ExploreKind::Album), Some(PLAYLIST_PAGE) => Some(ExploreKind::Playlist), Some(ARTIST_PAGE) => Some(ExploreKind::Artist), Some(_) => None, None if browse_id.starts_with("MPREb") => Some(ExploreKind::Album), None if browse_id.starts_with("VL") => Some(ExploreKind::Playlist), None if browse_id.starts_with("UC") => Some(ExploreKind::Artist), None => None, } }

nodes.name: playlist_browse_id
nodes.body_text: fn playlist_browse_id(id: &str) -> String { if id.starts_with("VL") { id.to_string() } else { format!("VL{id}") } }

nodes.name: tests
nodes.body_text: mod tests { use super::*; use serde_json::json; fn thumb(url: &str, w: u64, h: u64) -> Value { json!({ "url": url, "width": w, "height": h }) } fn item(title: &str, browse_id: Option<&str>, subtitle: &[&str]) -> Value { let mut nav = json!({}); if let Some(id) = browse_id { nav = json!({ "browseEndpoint": { "browseId": id } }); } json!({ "musicTwoRowItemRenderer": { "title": { "runs": [{ "text": title, "navigationEndpoint": nav }] }, "subtitle": { "runs": subtitle.iter().map(|t| json!({ "text": t })).collect::<Vec<_>>() }, "thumbnailRenderer": { "musicThumbnailRenderer": { "thumbnail": { "thumbnails": [thumb("small.jpg", 60, 60), thumb("big.jpg", 544, 544)] }}} } }) } fn shelf(header: &str, items: Vec<Value>) -> Value { json!({ "musicCarouselShelfRenderer": { "header": { "musicCarouselShelfBasicHeaderRenderer": { "title": { "runs": [{ "text": header }] } }}, "contents": items } }) } fn page(shelves: Vec<Value>) -> Value { json!({ "contents": { "sectionListRenderer": { "contents": shelves } } }) } /// A run that links somewhere, which is how every reader here decides what a /// run means. fn linked(text: &str, browse_id: &str, page_type: &str) -> Value { json!({ "text": text, "navigationEndpoint": { "browseEndpoint": { "browseId": browse_id, "browseEndpointContextSupportedConfigs": { "browseEndpointContextMusicConfig": { "pageType": page_type } } }} }) } /// A list row, with its byline columns given as raw runs so each test can /// place the album wherever the surface it's imitating puts it. fn row(title: &str, video_id: &str, cols: Vec<Vec<Value>>, video_type: Option<&str>) -> Value { let mut flex = vec![json!({ "musicResponsiveListItemFlexColumnRenderer": { "text": { "runs": [{ "text": title }] } } })]; for runs in cols { flex.push(json!({ "musicResponsiveListItemFlexColumnRenderer": { "text": { "runs": runs } } })); } let mut r = json!({ "musicResponsiveListItemRenderer": { "playlistItemData": { "videoId": video_id }, "flexColumns": flex, "thumbnail": { "musicThumbnailRenderer": { "thumbnail": { "thumbnails": [thumb("small.jpg", 60, 60), thumb("big.jpg", 544, 544)] }}} } }); if let Some(t) = video_type { r["musicResponsiveListItemRenderer"]["overlay"] = json!({ "musicItemThumbnailOverlayRenderer": { "content": { "musicPlayButtonRenderer": { "playNavigationEndpoint": { "watchEndpoint": { "watchEndpointMusicSupportedConfigs": { "watchEndpointMusicConfig": { "musicVideoType": t } } } } } } } }); } r } #[test] fn reads_playlists_and_albums_from_their_shelves() { let json = page(vec![ shelf( "Featured playlists", vec![item("Owambe", Some("VLRDCLAK5uy_abc"), &["YouTube Music"])], ), shelf( "Albums", vec![item( "Miracles", Some("MPREb_MKmMXRbMBVr"), &["Album", " • ", "A Pass", " • ", "2019"], )], ), ]); let shelves = parse_page(&json); assert_eq!(shelves.len(), 2); assert_eq!(shelves[0].title, "Featured playlists"); assert_eq!(shelves[0].items[0].kind, ExploreKind::Playlist); // VL kept: browse sends this verbatim. assert_eq!(shelves[0].items[0].id, "VLRDCLAK5uy_abc"); assert_eq!(shelves[0].items[0].thumbnail.as_deref(), Some("big.jpg")); assert_eq!(shelves[1].items[0].kind, ExploreKind::Album); assert_eq!(shelves[1].items[0].id, "MPREb_MKmMXRbMBVr"); // Joined, not index-picked. assert_eq!( shelves[1].items[0].subtitle.as_deref(), Some("Album • A Pass • 2019") ); } /// The *Songs* shelf a genre page leads with: a carousel of list rows, not /// of cards. Which renderer a shelf holds is not a property of the shelf. #[test] fn reads_a_songs_carousel_of_list_rows() { let json = page(vec![shelf( "Songs", vec![row( "Raindance", "1qmrq6I_jHI", vec![ vec![ linked("Dave", "UC1", ARTIST_PAGE), json!({ "text": " & " }), linked("Tems", "UC2", ARTIST_PAGE), json!({ "text": " • " }), json!({ "text": "89M views" }), ], vec![linked("The Boy Who Played the Harp", "MPREb_x", ALBUM_PAGE)], ], Some("MUSIC_VIDEO_TYPE_ATV"), )], )]); let shelves = parse_page(&json); assert_eq!(shelves[0].title, "Songs"); let song = &shelves[0].items[0]; assert_eq!(song.kind, ExploreKind::Song); // A row's id is a video id — there's no browse id to have. assert_eq!(song.id, "1qmrq6I_jHI"); // Both credits, joined — not whichever one an index landed on. assert_eq!(song.artist.as_deref(), Some("Dave, Tems")); // Column 2 here, column 1 on a search row: found by its link either way. assert_eq!(song.album.as_deref(), Some("The Boy Who Played the Harp")); // A view count is not a running time. assert_eq!(song.duration_secs, None); assert!(!song.has_video); } /// The same reader on a search row, where the album sits one column earlier /// and column 2 is a play count instead. Nothing about the row's position /// may leak into what it means. #[test] fn reads_a_search_song_row_whose_album_sits_in_another_column() { let json = page(vec![json!({ "musicShelfRenderer": { "title": { "runs": [{ "text": "Songs" }] }, "contents": [row( "Common Person", "ZmZi1ZuPB9A", vec![ vec![ linked("Burna Boy", "UCr61", ARTIST_PAGE), json!({ "text": " • " }), linked("Love, Damin

nodes.name: reads_playlists_and_albums_from_their_shelves
nodes.body_text: fn reads_playlists_and_albums_from_their_shelves() { let json = page(vec![ shelf( "Featured playlists", vec![item("Owambe", Some("VLRDCLAK5uy_abc"), &["YouTube Music"])], ), shelf( "Albums", vec![item( "Miracles", Some("MPREb_MKmMXRbMBVr"), &["Album", " • ", "A Pass", " • ", "2019"], )], ), ]); let shelves = parse_page(&json); assert_eq!(shelves.len(), 2); assert_eq!(shelves[0].title, "Featured playlists"); assert_eq!(shelves[0].items[0].kind, ExploreKind::Playlist); // VL kept: browse sends this verbatim. assert_eq!(shelves[0].items[0].id, "VLRDCLAK5uy_abc"); assert_eq!(shelves[0].items[0].thumbnail.as_deref(), Some("big.jpg")); assert_eq!(shelves[1].items[0].kind, ExploreKind::Album); assert_eq!(shelves[1].items[0].id, "MPREb_MKmMXRbMBVr"); // Joined, not index-picked. assert_eq!( shelves[1].items[0].subtitle.as_deref(), Some("Album • A Pass • 2019") ); }

nodes.body_text: fn reads_a_songs_carousel_of_list_rows() { let json = page(vec![shelf( "Songs", vec![row( "Raindance", "1qmrq6I_jHI", vec![ vec![ linked("Dave", "UC1", ARTIST_PAGE), json!({ "text": " & " }), linked("Tems", "UC2", ARTIST_PAGE), json!({ "text": " • " }), json!({ "text": "89M views" }), ], vec![linked("The Boy Who Played the Harp", "MPREb_x", ALBUM_PAGE)], ], Some("MUSIC_VIDEO_TYPE_ATV"), )], )]); let shelves = parse_page(&json); assert_eq!(shelves[0].title, "Songs"); let song = &shelves[0].items[0]; assert_eq!(song.kind, ExploreKind::Song); // A row's id is a video id — there's no browse id to have. assert_eq!(song.id, "1qmrq6I_jHI"); // Both credits, joined — not whichever one an index landed on. assert_eq!(song.artist.as_deref(), Some("Dave, Tems")); // Column 2 here, column 1 on a search row: found by its link either way. assert_eq!(song.album.as_deref(), Some("The Boy Who Played the Harp")); // A view count is not a running time. assert_eq!(song.duration_secs, None); assert!(!song.has_video); }

nodes.name: reads_a_search_song_row_whose_album_sits_in_another_column
nodes.body_text: fn reads_a_search_song_row_whose_album_sits_in_another_column() { let json = page(vec![json!({ "musicShelfRenderer": { "title": { "runs": [{ "text": "Songs" }] }, "contents": [row( "Common Person", "ZmZi1ZuPB9A", vec![ vec![ linked("Burna Boy", "UCr61", ARTIST_PAGE), json!({ "text": " • " }), linked("Love, Damini", "MPREb_If75wr3HkMf", ALBUM_PAGE), json!({ "text": " • " }), json!({ "text": "3:31" }), ], vec![json!({ "text": "149M plays" })], ], Some("MUSIC_VIDEO_TYPE_ATV"), )] }})]); let song = &parse_page(&json)[0].items[0]; assert_eq!(song.artist.as_deref(), Some("Burna Boy")); assert_eq!(song.album.as_deref(), Some("Love, Damini")); assert_eq!(song.duration_secs, Some(211.0)); // The play count must not be mistaken for anything: it links nowhere. assert_eq!(song.subtitle.as_deref(), Some("Burna Boy • Love, Damini • 3:31")); }

nodes.body_text: fn reads_a_music_video_card_from_its_watch_endpoint() { let json = page(vec![shelf( "Music videos", vec![json!({ "musicTwoRowItemRenderer": { "title": { "runs": [{ "text": "Raindance" }] }, "subtitle": { "runs": [ linked("Dave", "UC1", ARTIST_PAGE), { "text": " • " }, { "text": "210M views" } ]}, "navigationEndpoint": { "watchEndpoint": { "videoId": "SOJpE1KMUbo", "watchEndpointMusicSupportedConfigs": { "watchEndpointMusicConfig": { "musicVideoType": "MUSIC_VIDEO_TYPE_OMV" } } }} }})], )]); let video = &parse_page(&json)[0].items[0]; assert_eq!(video.kind, ExploreKind::Video); assert_eq!(video.id, "SOJpE1KMUbo"); assert_eq!(video.artist.as_deref(), Some("Dave")); assert!(video.has_video); }

nodes.body_text: fn a_stated_page_type_beats_the_id_prefix() { assert_eq!(classify("UCabc", Some(ARTIST_PAGE)), Some(ExploreKind::Artist)); assert_eq!(classify("MPREb_x", Some(ALBUM_PAGE)), Some(ExploreKind::Album)); assert_eq!( classify("PL_no_prefix", Some(PLAYLIST_PAGE)), Some(ExploreKind::Playlist) ); assert_eq!(classify("UCabc", Some("MUSIC_PAGE_TYPE_PODCAST_SHOW")), None); assert_eq!(classify("UCabc", Some("MUSIC_PAGE_TYPE_USER_CHANNEL")), None); }

nodes.name: ClientIdentity
nodes.body_text: pub(crate) enum ClientIdentity { /// Apple Vision Pro. A single published identity rather than an app with a /// rolling version, so there is no version list to walk: when it is /// refused the second axis is the `visitorData`. VisionOs, /// Kept behind VISIONOS rather than deleted. Every version here is below /// 1.64, so it fails **loudly** — a refusal, not a gated url that plays a /// megabyte and stops — which costs one clean miss and leaves a second /// axis if VISIONOS is ever refused. Never add one at or above 1.64. AndroidVr(&'static str), }

nodes.name: NativeMiss
nodes.body_text: pub(crate) enum NativeMiss { /// Transport failure or a non-2xx status — includes timeouts. Http(String), /// The response wasn't the JSON shape expected at all. BadJson, /// `playabilityStatus.status != "OK"` — carries the status string. Unplayable(String), /// No itag 140 in `adaptiveFormats` at all. NoItag140, /// itag 140 exists but hides its url behind `signatureCipher` — the SABR /// canary: this client losing its plaintext-url exemption. Ciphered, }

nodes.name: fmt
nodes.body_text: fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result { match self { Self::Http(m) => write!(f, "http: {m}"), Self::BadJson => write!(f, "bad json"), Self::Unplayable(status) => write!(f, "unplayable: {status}"), Self::NoItag140 => write!(f, "no itag 140"), Self::Ciphered => write!(f, "ciphered"), } }

nodes.name: resolve_native
nodes.body_text: pub(crate) fn resolve_native( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, video_id: &str, ) -> Result<StreamTarget, NativeMiss> { let started = std::time::Instant::now(); let mut last = NativeMiss::Http("no identity tried".to_string()); for identity in IDENTITIES { match ask_presenting(client, video_id, *identity) { Ok(target) => return Ok(target), Err(miss) => last = miss, } // The floor is 5 seconds away; spending longer than that here to avoid // it is a loss even when the next identity would have worked. if started.elapsed() >= ROTATION_BUDGET { break; } } Err(last) }

nodes.name: ask_presenting
nodes.body_text: fn ask_presenting( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, video_id: &str, identity: ClientIdentity, ) -> Result<StreamTarget, NativeMiss> { let presented = visitor_data(); let json = player_once(client, video_id, identity, presented.as_deref())?; let miss = match parse_player_response(&json, identity) { Ok(target) => return Ok(target), Err(miss) => miss, }; if !matches!(miss, NativeMiss::Unplayable(_)) { return Err(miss); } let learned = visitor_data(); if learned.is_some() && learned != presented { let json = player_once(client, video_id, identity, learned.as_deref())?; return parse_player_response(&json, identity); } // Nothing new came back and we presented nothing, so there is no second // request to make that differs from the first. if presented.is_none() { return Err(miss); } set_visitor_data(None); let json = player_once(client, video_id, identity, None)?; parse_player_response(&json, identity) }

nodes.name: player_once
nodes.body_text: fn player_once( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, video_id: &str, identity: ClientIdentity, visitor: Option<&str>, ) -> Result<Value, NativeMiss> { let ua = identity.user_agent(); let mut context = identity.context(); if let Some(v) = visitor { context["visitorData"] = Value::String(v.to_string()); } let body = serde_json::json!({ "context": { "client": context }, "videoId": video_id, "cpn": cpn(), "contentCheckOk": true, "racyCheckOk": true, }); let mut req = client .post("https://youtubei.googleapis.com/youtubei/v1/player?prettyPrint=false") .header("User-Agent", ua.as_str()) .header("X-YouTube-Client-Name", identity.id()) .header("X-YouTube-Client-Version", identity.version()) .header("Content-Type", "application/json") .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3)); if let Some(v) = visitor { req = req.header("X-Goog-Visitor-Id", v); } let resp = req .json(&body) .send() .map_err(|e| NativeMiss::Http(e.to_string()))?; if !resp.status().is_success() { return Err(NativeMiss::Http(format!("status {}", resp.status()))); } let json: Value = resp.json().map_err(|_| NativeMiss::BadJson)?; harvest_visitor_data(&json); Ok(json) }

nodes.name: cpn
nodes.body_text: fn cpn() -> String { const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"; let mut n = std::time::SystemTime::now() .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH) .map(|d| d.as_nanos()) .unwrap_or(0); let mut out = String::with_capacity(16); for _ in 0..16 { out.push(ALPHABET[(n & 0x3f) as usize] as char); n >>= 6; } out }

nodes.name: parse_player_response
nodes.body_text: pub(crate) fn parse_player_response( json: &Value, identity: ClientIdentity, ) -> Result<StreamTarget, NativeMiss> { let status = json .pointer("/playabilityStatus/status") .and_then(Value::as_str) .ok_or(NativeMiss::BadJson)?; if status != "OK" { return Err(NativeMiss::Unplayable(status.to_string())); } let formats = json .pointer("/streamingData/adaptiveFormats") .and_then(Value::as_array) .ok_or(NativeMiss::BadJson)?; let m4a = formats .iter() .find(|f| f.pointer("/itag").and_then(Value::as_u64) == Some(140)) .ok_or(NativeMiss::NoItag140)?; let url = match m4a.pointer("/url").and_then(Value::as_str) { Some(u) => u, // A 140 that exists but hides its url behind a cipher is the SABR // canary — distinct from "no 140 at all" so the log shows the drift. None => return Err(NativeMiss::Ciphered), }; Ok(StreamTarget { url: url.to_string(), headers: vec![("User-Agent".into(), identity.user_agent())], ext: "m4a".into(), format_id: "140".into(), abr_kbps: m4a .pointer("/bitrate") .and_then(Value::as_u64) .and_then(|b| u32::try_from(b / 1000).ok()), expires_at: ytdlp::parse_expiry(url), }) }

codecs=\"opus\"", "url": "https://cdn/opus" }, { "itag": 140, "mimeType": "audio/mp4; codecs=\"mp4a.40.2\"", "bitrate": 130_000, "url": url }, { "itag": 136, "mimeType": "video/mp4", "url": "https://cdn/video" } ] } }) } #[test] fn a_healthy_response_builds_the_exact_target() { let url = "https://rr3.googlevideo.com/videoplayback?expire=1790000000&c=ANDROID_VR&itag=140"; let t = parse_player_response(&player_ok(url), ClientIdentity::AndroidVr("1.62.20")).expect("itag 140 with a url must resolve"); assert_eq!(t.url, url); assert_eq!(t.ext, "m4a"); assert_eq!(t.format_id, "140"); assert_eq!(t.expires_at, Some(1_790_000_000)); assert_eq!(t.abr_kbps, Some(130)); // The media GET must present the same client the URL was minted for. assert_eq!( t.headers, vec![("User-Agent".to_string(), android_vr_ua("1.62.20"))] ); } /// The decoder pin: Opus must be unrepresentable — 140 or nothing. #[test] fn opus_alone_is_a_miss_never_a_target() { let mut v = player_ok("https://cdn/x"); v["streamingData"]["adaptiveFormats"] .as_array_mut() .unwrap() .retain(|f| f["itag"] != 140); let f = &mut v["streamingData"]["adaptiveFormats"][1]; f.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("url"); f["signatureCipher"] = serde_json::json!("s=abc&sp=sig&url=https%3A%2F%2F..."); assert!(matches!(parse_player_response(&v, ClientIdentity::AndroidVr("1.62.20")), Err(NativeMiss::Ciphered))); } #[test] fn a_non_ok_playability_carries_its_status() { let mut v = player_ok("unused"); v["playabilityStatus"] = serde_json::json!({ "status": "UNPLAYABLE", "reason": "made for kids" }); match parse_player_response(&v, ClientIdentity::AndroidVr("1.62.20")) { Err(NativeMiss::Unplayable(s)) => assert_eq!(s, "UNPLAYABLE"), other => panic!("expected Unplayable, got {other:?}"), } } /// `1.64.16` -> 164016, so versions compare as numbers rather than strings /// (where "1.9" would sort above "1.64"). fn ordinal(version: &str) -> u32 { let mut parts = version.split('.').map(|p| p.parse::<u32>().unwrap()); parts.next().unwrap() * 1_000_000 + parts.next().unwrap() * 1_000 + parts.next().unwrap() } /// The 2026-08-18 outage, and the one thing that must never regress. /// /// From 1.64 upward YouTube hands ANDROID_VR a proof-of-origin gated url: /// it resolves `OK`, it serves a bounded slice, and it 403s the single /// open-ended GET a player opens with. ANDROID_VR is refused on *both* sides of the /// 1.64 wall now — bot-checked below it, gated at and above it — so it /// cannot lead. Asking it first costs the user two refusals per track /// before anything that plays is even tried. #[test] fn visionos_is_asked_first() { assert_eq!(IDENTITIES.first(), Some(&ClientIdentity::VisionOs)); } /// Every field was measured rather than guessed: an identity YouTube /// cannot place is answered exactly like a bot. #[test] fn the_visionos_identity_is_the_one_that_was_measured() { let ctx = ClientIdentity::VisionOs.context(); assert_eq!(ctx["clientName"], "VISIONOS"); assert_eq!(ctx["clientVersion"], "1.02"); assert_eq!(ctx["deviceMake"], "Apple"); assert_eq!(ctx["deviceModel"], "RealityDevice17,1"); assert_eq!(ctx["osName"], "visionOS"); assert_eq!(ClientIdentity::VisionOs.id(), "101"); // Not an Android client: sending an Android field marks it as forged. assert!(ctx.get("androidSdkVersion").is_none()); } /// The UA travels with the url to the media GET, so it must be the one /// VISIONOS presented — not an Oculus UA left over from the old client. #[test] fn a_visionos_target_carries_the_visionos_user_agent() { let t = parse_player_response(&player_ok("https://cdn/x"), ClientIdentity::VisionOs) .expect("itag 140 with a url must resolve"); assert_eq!( t.headers, vec![("User-Agent".to_string(), VISIONOS_UA.to_string())] ); assert!(!VISIONOS_UA.contains("oculus")); } /// Comparing `VISIONOS_UA` to itself proves not

nodes.name: YtMusicState
nodes.body_text: pub struct YtMusicState { /// Cached API handle. Rebuilt whenever the cookies change; `None` when /// signed out or not yet built. client: tokio::sync::Mutex<Option<Arc<YtMusic<BrowserToken>>>>, /// The session, mirrored in memory so `stream_target` (sync, on the decode /// thread) doesn't touch the keychain per resolve — that can block on a /// user prompt, which would stall audio. /// /// Read lazily, and *never* during app setup: see [`SessionStore`]. The /// residual risk is that the decode thread is the first caller and pays for /// the read — but that path only reaches here after the native resolve has /// missed, i.e. on its way to a yt-dlp process start, and in practice the /// account is asked about far earlier by whichever view mounts first. session: RwLock<Session>, /// Where [`Self::session`] is read from, and what a sign-out clears. session_store: SessionStore, /// Whether the session is worth trying *first* when resolving a stream. /// /// Starts true and flips to whatever last worked. Where accounts exist that /// YouTube serves no playable format to, every track otherwise paid for a /// doomed yt-dlp spawn before the one that works — seconds, in front of the /// play button. Both attempts always remain available, so a private track /// still resolves; this only decides the order. session_first: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool, /// Resolved stream urls, kept until the CDN's own `expire=` says not to. /// /// A resolve is a yt-dlp process start — a Python interpreter and extractor /// import before a single byte moves — and measures ~5s. That cost landed /// between two tracks, where it *is* the gap the listener hears. The urls are /// good for ~6 hours, so paying it more than once a track is pure waste. /// /// Keyed by video id. Bounded by pruning the already-expired on write: an /// entry is only useful while live, so what makes one stale is also what /// makes it collectable and no separate eviction policy is needed. resolved: RwLock<std::collections::HashMap<String, ytdlp::StreamTarget>>, /// Disk-restored urls, quarantined until probed. /// /// A restart often means a network change, and googlevideo urls are /// IP-bound — so nothing in here may be served without one cheap probe /// first (see `live_or_probed_target`). Same-session entries never pass /// through this map and keep their unprobed ~µs hits. restored: TargetCache, /// Bumped whenever what a snapshot would contain changes — `remember_target`, /// a probe dropping a restored entry, and `forget()` (a dead url must leave /// the on-disk snapshot too). The disk saver polls it to skip writes when /// nothing moved. Restore doesn't bump: that state came FROM the file. cache_generation: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64, /// Resolved *video* urls, on the same terms as [`Self::resolved`]. /// /// A separate map because the same video id resolves to two different urls — /// the m4a the engine decodes, and the video-only rendition the picture /// shows. One map keyed by id would have them evict and answer for each /// other. /// /// This one is arguably the more important of the two: the audio url is /// prefetched a track ahead, but the video url is resolved on demand, so its /// cold cost lands *while the user is watching the spinner*. resolved_video: RwLock<std::collections::HashMap<String, ytdlp::StreamTarget>>, /// Where yt-dlp lives, once found. /// /// `detect()` stats every entry on `PATH` and ran on every resolve. Only a /// hit is remembered: a miss has to stay cheap to retry, or installing /// yt-dlp wouldn't take effect until a restart. yt_dlp_bin: RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>, /// Session tally for the native InnerTube fast path — how often a POST /// and a probe replaced a yt-dlp spawn, versus how often it fell through. /// Read by nothing yet but `native_miss`'s own log line; exists so a /// future status surface doesn't need a second counting scheme bolted on. native_hits: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64, native_misses: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64, }

nodes.body_text: fn probe_ok(target: &ytdlp::StreamTarget) -> bool { matches!(probe(target), ProbeVerdict::Serves) }

nodes.name: ProbeVerdict
nodes.body_text: enum ProbeVerdict { /// It served the whole-file request. This url plays. Serves, /// It answered with a status that will not change on its own — the /// proof-of-origin gate (403), or a url that is simply gone. Nothing is /// retrievable here; only a different url can help. Refused, /// Anything else: transport failure, timeout, offline, or a CDN saying /// "not now" (429, 5xx). Says nothing about the url itself. Inconclusive, }

nodes.name: probe
nodes.body_text: fn probe(target: &ytdlp::StreamTarget) -> ProbeVerdict { let mut req = probe_client().get(&target.url).header("Range", "bytes=0-"); for (k, v) in &target.headers { req = req.header(k.as_str(), v.as_str()); } match req.send() { Ok(r) => { let s = r.status(); if s == reqwest::StatusCode::OK || s == reqwest::StatusCode::PARTIAL_CONTENT { ProbeVerdict::Serves } else if matches!( s, reqwest::StatusCode::FORBIDDEN | reqwest::StatusCode::NOT_FOUND | reqwest::StatusCode::GONE ) { ProbeVerdict::Refused } else { ProbeVerdict::Inconclusive } } Err(_) => ProbeVerdict::Inconclusive, } }

nodes.name: remember_in
nodes.body_text: fn remember_in(cache: &TargetCache, video_id: &str, target: &ytdlp::StreamTarget) { // Nothing to reason about without a deadline, and a url we can't date is // one we can't safely re-serve. if target.expires_at.is_none() { return; } let Some(now) = now_secs() else { return }; let Ok(mut cache) = cache.write() else { return; }; cache.retain(|_, t| is_fresh(t, now)); cache.insert(video_id.to_string(), target.clone()); }

nodes.name: sign_in
nodes.signature: pub async fn sign_in(&self, captured: Vec<YtCookie>) -> Result<(), String>
nodes.body_text: pub async fn sign_in(&self, captured: Vec<YtCookie>) -> Result<(), String> { let live = cookies::prune_expired(captured, cookies::now_secs()); if !cookies::is_signed_in(&live) { return Err("Sign-in didn't complete — no YouTube session cookies were found.".into()); } cookies::save(&live)?; *self.session.write().unwrap() = Session::Read(Some(live)); // A new session earns a fresh chance at going first. self.session_first .store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed); // Force a rebuild so the next call uses the new session. *self.client.lock().await = None; // Prove the cookies actually work now, rather than failing later behind // an empty playlist list. self.client().await.map(|_| ()) }

nodes.name: sign_out
nodes.signature: pub async fn sign_out(&self) -> Result<(), String>
nodes.body_text: pub async fn sign_out(&self) -> Result<(), String> { (self.session_store.clear)()?; *self.session.write().unwrap() = Session::Read(None); self.session_first .store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed); *self.client.lock().await = None; Ok(()) }

nodes.name: cookies_snapshot
nodes.body_text: fn cookies_snapshot(&self) -> Option<Vec<YtCookie>> { if let Session::Read(jar) = &*self.session.read().unwrap() { return jar.clone(); } let mut slot = self.session.write().unwrap(); if let Session::Read(jar) = &*slot { // Someone else settled it while we waited for the lock. return jar.clone(); } let jar = match (self.session_store.read)() { Ok(Some(stored)) => { let live = cookies::prune_expired(stored, cookies::now_secs()); cookies::is_signed_in(&live).then_some(live) } Ok(None) | Err(_) => None, }; *slot = Session::Read(jar.clone()); jar }

ExploreKind::Song | ExploreKind::Video => Ok(vec![track_of(item)]), // An artist isn't a track list; its top songs are the closest thing // to one, and they're what YouTube's own play button uses. ExploreKind::Artist => self.artist_tracks(item).await, } }

nodes.signature: async fn artist_tracks(&self, item: &ExploreItem) -> Result<Vec<YtTrack>, String>
nodes.body_text: async fn artist_tracks(&self, item: &ExploreItem) -> Result<Vec<YtTrack>, String> { let shelves = self.artist_page(&item.id).await?; Ok(shelves .iter() .flat_map(|shelf| &shelf.items) .filter(|i| matches!(i.kind, ExploreKind::Song | ExploreKind::Video)) .map(|song| YtTrack { // The artist's own name stands in where a row didn't link a // credit: on their page, an unlinked credit is them. artist: song.artist.clone().or_else(|| Some(item.title.clone())), playlist_id: item.id.clone(), playlist_title: item.title.clone(), ..track_of(song) }) .collect()) }

nodes.name: album_tracks
nodes.signature: async fn album_tracks(&self, album_id: &str, fallback_title: &str) -> Result<Vec<YtTrack>, String>
nodes.body_text: async fn album_tracks(&self, album_id: &str, fallback_title: &str) -> Result<Vec<YtTrack>, String> { let yt = self.client().await?; let album = yt .get_album(AlbumID::from_raw(album_id)) .await .map_err(|e| format!("Could not load \"{fallback_title}\": {e}"))?; let artist = join_artists(&album.artists); let cover = best_thumbnail(&album.thumbnails); Ok(album .tracks .into_iter() .map(|t| YtTrack { video_id: t.video_id.get_raw().to_string(), title: t.title, artist: artist.clone(), album: (!album.title.is_empty()).then(|| album.title.clone()), duration_secs: parse_duration(&t.duration), thumbnail: cover.clone(), playlist_id: album_id.to_string(), playlist_title: album.title.clone(), // `get_album` doesn't report per-track availability; a track that // turns out to be blocked fails at resolve time like any other. is_available: true, // Album tracks are songs — YouTube renders them as a still, so // there's nothing to watch. It also doesn't report a video type // here, and claiming footage we haven't seen would show an // enabled toggle that produces a photograph. has_video: false, }) .collect()) }

nodes.name: all_tracks
nodes.signature: pub async fn all_tracks(&self) -> Result<(Vec<YtPlaylist>, Vec<YtTrack>), String>
nodes.body_text: pub async fn all_tracks(&self) -> Result<(Vec<YtPlaylist>, Vec<YtTrack>), String> { let yt = self.client().await?; let playlists = self.playlists().await?; let sem = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(PLAYLIST_FETCH_CONCURRENCY)); let mut set = tokio::task::JoinSet::new(); for pl in playlists.clone() { let yt = yt.clone(); let sem = sem.clone(); set.spawn(async move { let _permit = sem.acquire().await.ok()?; fetch_tracks(&yt, &pl).await.ok() }); } let mut tracks = Vec::new(); while let Some(res) = set.join_next().await { if let Ok(Some(mut got)) = res { tracks.append(&mut got); } } Ok((playlists, tracks)) }

nodes.name: live_or_probed_target
nodes.body_text: fn live_or_probed_target(&self, video_id: &str) -> Option<ytdlp::StreamTarget> { if let Some(t) = self.cached_target(video_id) { return Some(t); } let quarantined = self.restored.write().ok()?.remove(video_id)?; if probe_ok(&quarantined) { // remember_target() also bumps the generation — promotion doesn't // change the snapshot union, but the bump is harmless (one spare // write). self.remember_target(video_id, &quarantined); return Some(quarantined); } // Dead on arrival (new network, revoked url): the union changed, so // the saver must write the shrunken truth. self.cache_generation .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed); None }
