nodes.name: build_menu
nodes.body_text: fn build_menu(app: &AppHandle, model: &TrayModel) -> tauri::Result<Menu<tauri::Wry>> { let menu = Menu::new(app)?; let sep = || PredefinedMenuItem::separator(app); let equalizer_mode = model.mode == "equalizer"; // Status line + transport. let status = if equalizer_mode { "Equalizing system audio".to_string() } else { match &model.now_playing { Some(title) => format!("♪ {}", ellipsize(title, 48)), None => "Nothing playing".to_string(), } }; menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "status", status, false, None::<&str>)?)?; if !equalizer_mode { let play_label = if model.playing { "Pause" } else { "Play" }; menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "play_pause", play_label, model.can_control, None::<&str>)?)?; menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "next", "Next", model.can_control, None::<&str>)?)?; menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "prev", "Previous", model.can_control, None::<&str>)?)?; } menu.append(&sep()?)?; // Mode, power, tuning. menu.append(&CheckMenuItem::with_id(app, "mode:player", "Player mode", true, !equalizer_mode, None::<&str>)?)?; menu.append(&CheckMenuItem::with_id( app, "mode:equalizer", "Equalizer mode", model.mode_supported, equalizer_mode, None::<&str>, )?)?; menu.append(&CheckMenuItem::with_id(app, "power", "Enhancement on", true, model.power, None::<&str>)?)?; let presets = Submenu::with_id(app, "presets", "Equalizer preset", true)?; for p in &model.presets { presets.append(&CheckMenuItem::with_id(app, format!("preset:{}", p.id), &p.name, true, p.active, None::<&str>)?)?; } if !model.presets.is_empty() { presets.append(&sep()?)?; } presets.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "presets:open", "Open Equalizer…", true, None::<&str>)?)?; menu.append(&presets)?; let effects = Submenu::with_id(app, "effects", "Effects", !model.effects.is_empty())?; for fx in &model.effects { effects.append(&CheckMenuItem::with_id(app, format!("fx:{}", fx.id), &fx.label, fx.enabled, fx.on, None::<&str>)?)?; } menu.append(&effects)?; if let Some(running) = model.visualizer { menu.append(&CheckMenuItem::with_id(app, "visualizer", "Fullscreen visualizer", true, running, None::<&str>)?)?; } menu.append(&sep()?)?; // Navigation. let go = Submenu::with_id(app, "go", "Go to", !model.routes.is_empty())?; for r in &model.routes { go.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, format!("go:{}", r.id), &r.label, true, None::<&str>)?)?; } menu.append(&go)?; menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "settings", "Settings…", true, Some("CmdOrCtrl+,"))?)?; menu.append(&sep()?)?; // App. if let Some(version) = &model.update_version { menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id( app, "update_restart", format!("Restart to update ({version})"), true, None::<&str>, )?)?; } menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "show", "Show HypeMuzik", true, None::<&str>)?)?; menu.append(&MenuItem::with_id(app, "quit", "Quit HypeMuzik", true, None::<&str>)?)?; Ok(menu) }

nodes.name: start
nodes.body_text: pub fn start() -> Option<TvProxy> { let server = Server::http("127.0.0.1:0").ok()?; let port = server.server_addr().to_ip()?.port(); let client = Arc::new( reqwest::blocking::Client::builder() // Fail fast on dead/geo-blocked hosts (→ the error card, not a long // hang), but allow a slow live segment to finish downloading. .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(6)) .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20)) // Low-latency forwarding + reuse warm keep-alive connections across // the manifest → variant → segment chain (avoids re-doing DNS/TLS). .tcp_nodelay(true) .pool_max_idle_per_host(8) .build() .ok()?, ); std::thread::Builder::new() .name("hm-tv-proxy".into()) .spawn(move || { for request in server.incoming_requests() { let client = Arc::clone(&client); // Detached per-request thread: concurrent segment fetches. std::thread::spawn(move || handle(&client, port, request)); } }) .ok()?; Some(TvProxy { port }) }

nodes.name: handle
nodes.signature: fn handle(client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, port: u16, request: tiny_http::Request)
nodes.body_text: fn handle(client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, port: u16, request: tiny_http::Request) { let raw = request.url().to_string(); let (path, query) = raw.split_once('?').unwrap_or((raw.as_str(), "")); let params = parse_query(query); let Some(upstream) = params.get("u") else { respond(request, 400, "text/plain", b"missing url".to_vec(), None); return; }; let ua = params.get("ua").map(String::as_str); let referer = params.get("r").map(String::as_str); match path { "/hls" => serve_playlist(client, port, upstream, ua, referer, request), "/seg" => serve_segment(client, upstream, ua, referer, request), "/video" => serve_video(client, upstream, ua, request), _ => respond(request, 404, "text/plain", b"not found".to_vec(), None), } }

nodes.name: VIDEO_BODY_TIMEOUT
nodes.body_text: const VIDEO_BODY_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10 * 60);

nodes.name: serve_video
nodes.body_text: fn serve_video( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, upstream: &str, ua: Option<&str>, request: tiny_http::Request, ) { let Some(total) = video_total_len(client, upstream, ua) else { respond(request, 502, "text/plain", b"upstream length unknown".to_vec(), None); return; }; let range = request .headers() .iter() .find(|h| h.field.equiv("Range")) .map(|h| h.value.as_str().to_string()); let framing = video_framing(range.as_deref(), total); let reader = ChunkedVideo { client: client.clone(), url: upstream.to_string(), ua: ua.map(str::to_string), next: framing.start, end: framing.end, buf: Vec::new(), buf_pos: 0, }; let content_len = framing.end - framing.start + 1; let mut response = Response::new( StatusCode(framing.status), Vec::new(), reader, Some(content_len as usize), None, ); for (name, value) in [ ("Content-Type", "video/mp4"), ("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"), ("Accept-Ranges", "bytes"), ("Cache-Control", "no-store"), ] { if let Ok(h) = Header::from_bytes(name.as_bytes(), value.as_bytes()) { response.add_header(h); } } if let Some(cr) = framing.content_range.as_deref() { if let Ok(h) = Header::from_bytes(b"Content-Range".as_ref(), cr.as_bytes()) { response.add_header(h); } } let _ = request.respond(response); }

nodes.name: VIDEO_CHUNK
nodes.body_text: const VIDEO_CHUNK: u64 = 1 << 20;

nodes.name: VideoFraming
nodes.body_text: struct VideoFraming { status: u16, start: u64, /// Inclusive last byte. end: u64, content_range: Option<String>, }

nodes.name: video_framing
nodes.signature: fn video_framing(client_range: Option<&str>, total: u64) -> VideoFraming
nodes.body_text: fn video_framing(client_range: Option<&str>, total: u64) -> VideoFraming { let last = total.saturating_sub(1); match parse_byte_range(client_range) { // No Range: the element is owed a 200 over the whole file. None => VideoFraming { status: 200, start: 0, end: last, content_range: None }, // A Range: a 206 from `start`, clamped to what exists. Some((start, end_opt)) => { let start = start.min(last); let end = end_opt.unwrap_or(last).min(last); VideoFraming { status: 206, start, end, content_range: Some(format!("bytes {start}-{end}/{total}")), } } } }

nodes.name: parse_byte_range
nodes.body_text: fn parse_byte_range(header: Option<&str>) -> Option<(u64, Option<u64>)> { let spec = header?.trim().strip_prefix("bytes=")?; if spec.contains(',') { return None; // multi-range: can't be one contiguous body } let (a, b) = spec.split_once('-')?; let start: u64 = a.trim().parse().ok()?; let end = match b.trim() { "" => None, s => Some(s.parse().ok()?), }; Some((start, end)) }

nodes.name: video_total_len
nodes.body_text: fn video_total_len( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str, ua: Option<&str>, ) -> Option<u64> { if let Some(n) = parse_clen(url) { return Some(n); } let mut req = client .get(url) .timeout(VIDEO_BODY_TIMEOUT) .header(reqwest::header::RANGE, "bytes=0-0"); if let Some(ua) = ua { req = req.header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, ua); } let resp = req.send().ok()?; let cr = resp.headers().get(reqwest::header::CONTENT_RANGE)?.to_str().ok()?; total_from_content_range(cr) }

nodes.name: parse_clen
nodes.body_text: fn parse_clen(url: &str) -> Option<u64> { url.split(['?', '&']) .find_map(|kv| kv.strip_prefix("clen=")) .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()) }

nodes.name: total_from_content_range
nodes.body_text: fn total_from_content_range(cr: &str) -> Option<u64> { cr.rsplit('/').next()?.trim().parse().ok() }

nodes.name: next_chunk
nodes.signature: fn next_chunk(next: u64, end: u64, chunk: u64) -> Option<(u64, u64)>
nodes.body_text: fn next_chunk(next: u64, end: u64, chunk: u64) -> Option<(u64, u64)> { if next > end { return None; } Some((next, (next + chunk - 1).min(end))) }

nodes.name: ChunkedVideo
nodes.body_text: struct ChunkedVideo { client: reqwest::blocking::Client, url: String, ua: Option<String>, next: u64, end: u64, buf: Vec<u8>, buf_pos: usize, }

nodes.name: read
nodes.body_text: fn read(&mut self, out: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> { if self.buf_pos >= self.buf.len() { let Some((lo, hi)) = next_chunk(self.next, self.end, VIDEO_CHUNK) else { return Ok(0); // whole requested span delivered }; let mut req = self .client .get(&self.url) .timeout(VIDEO_BODY_TIMEOUT) .header(reqwest::header::RANGE, format!("bytes={lo}-{hi}")); if let Some(ua) = &self.ua { req = req.header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, ua); } let resp = req.send().map_err(std::io::Error::other)?; if !resp.status().is_success() { return Err(std::io::Error::other(format!( "upstream chunk {lo}-{hi} -> {}", resp.status() ))); } self.buf = resp .bytes() .map_err(std::io::Error::other)? .to_vec(); self.buf_pos = 0; self.next = hi + 1; if self.buf.is_empty() { return Ok(0); } } let n = (self.buf.len() - self.buf_pos).min(out.len()); out[..n].copy_from_slice(&self.buf[self.buf_pos..self.buf_pos + n]); self.buf_pos += n; Ok(n) }

nodes.name: serve_playlist
nodes.body_text:
fn serve_playlist( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, port: u16, upstream: &str, ua: Option<&str>, referer: Option<&str>, request: tiny_http::Request, ) { let Some(body) = fetch_text(client, upstream, ua, referer) else { respond(request, 502, "text/plain", b"upstream fetch failed".to_vec(), None); return; }; let base = Url::parse(upstream).ok(); let mut out = String::with_capacity(body.len() + 256); for line in body.lines() { let trimmed = line.trim(); if trimmed.is_empty() { out.push('
'); continue; } if trimmed.starts_with('#') { out.push_str(&rewrite_tag_uri(trimmed, base.as_ref(), port, ua, referer)); out.push('
'); } else { // A media segment or a child (variant) playlist URI. let abs = resolve(base.as_ref(), trimmed); out.push_str(&proxied(port, &abs, ua, referer)); out.push('
'); } } respond( request, 200, "application/vnd.apple.mpegurl", out.into_bytes(), Some(upstream), ); }

nodes.name: serve_segment
nodes.body_text: fn serve_segment( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, upstream: &str, ua: Option<&str>, referer: Option<&str>, request: tiny_http::Request, ) { let mut req = client.get(upstream); if let Some(ua) = ua { req = req.header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, ua); } if let Some(r) = referer { req = req.header(reqwest::header::REFERER, r); } let Ok(resp) = req.send() else { respond(request, 502, "text/plain", b"upstream fetch failed".to_vec(), None); return; }; let status = resp.status().as_u16(); let content_type = resp .headers() .get(reqwest::header::CONTENT_TYPE) .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()) .unwrap_or("application/octet-stream") .to_string(); let len = resp.content_length().map(|l| l as usize); let headers: Vec<Header> = [ ("Content-Type", content_type.as_str()), ("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"), ("Cache-Control", "no-store"), ] .iter() .filter_map(|(n, v)| Header::from_bytes(n.as_bytes(), v.as_bytes()).ok()) .collect(); // `resp` implements `Read`; tiny_http pulls bytes from it and writes them to // the socket as they come (chunked when the length is unknown). let response = Response::new(StatusCode(status), headers, resp, len, None); let _ = request.respond(response); }

nodes.name: rewrite_tag_uri
nodes.body_text: fn rewrite_tag_uri( line: &str, base: Option<&Url>, port: u16, ua: Option<&str>, referer: Option<&str>, ) -> String { let Some(start) = line.find("URI=\"") else { return line.to_string(); }; let val_start = start + 5; let Some(end_rel) = line[val_start..].find('"') else { return line.to_string(); }; let end = val_start + end_rel; let abs = resolve(base, &line[val_start..end]); format!("{}{}{}", &line[..val_start], proxied(port, &abs, ua, referer), &line[end..]) }

nodes.name: proxied
nodes.signature: fn proxied(port: u16, abs_url: &str, ua: Option<&str>, referer: Option<&str>) -> String
nodes.body_text: fn proxied(port: u16, abs_url: &str, ua: Option<&str>, referer: Option<&str>) -> String { let path = if is_playlist(abs_url) { "hls" } else { "seg" }; let mut out = format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/{path}?u={}", enc(abs_url)); if let Some(ua) = ua { out.push_str(&format!("&ua={}", enc(ua))); } if let Some(r) = referer { out.push_str(&format!("&r={}", enc(r))); } out }

nodes.name: is_playlist
nodes.body_text: fn is_playlist(u: &str) -> bool { let path = u.split(['?', '#']).next().unwrap_or(u); path.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".m3u8") }

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.body_text: fn resolve(base: Option<&Url>, uri: &str) -> String { if uri.starts_with("http://") || uri.starts_with("https://") { return uri.to_string(); } base.and_then(|b| b.join(uri).ok()) .map(|u| u.to_string()) .unwrap_or_else(|| uri.to_string()) }

nodes.name: fetch_text
nodes.body_text: fn fetch_text( client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str, ua: Option<&str>, referer: Option<&str>, ) -> Option<String> { let mut req = client.get(url); if let Some(ua) = ua { req = req.header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, ua); } if let Some(r) = referer { req = req.header(reqwest::header::REFERER, r); } let resp = req.send().ok()?; if !resp.status().is_success() { return None; } resp.text().ok() }

nodes.name: respond
nodes.body_text: fn respond( request: tiny_http::Request, status: u16, content_type: &str, body: Vec<u8>, _upstream: Option<&str>, ) { let mut response = Response::from_data(body).with_status_code(status); for (name, value) in [ ("Content-Type", content_type), ("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"), ("Cache-Control", "no-store"), ] { if let Ok(header) = Header::from_bytes(name.as_bytes(), value.as_bytes()) { response.add_header(header); } } let _ = request.respond(response); }

nodes.name: enc
nodes.body_text: fn enc(s: &str) -> String { url::form_urlencoded::byte_serialize(s.as_bytes()).collect() }

nodes.name: parse_query
nodes.body_text: fn parse_query(query: &str) -> HashMap<String, String> { url::form_urlencoded::parse(query.as_bytes()) .into_owned() .collect() }

nodes.name: log
nodes.body_text: fn log(msg: &str) { eprintln!("[updater] {msg}"); }

nodes.name: FIRST_CHECK_DELAY
nodes.body_text: const FIRST_CHECK_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(90);

nodes.name: CHECK_INTERVAL
nodes.body_text: const CHECK_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(6 * 60 * 60);

nodes.name: EVENT
nodes.body_text: pub const EVENT: &str = "updater://status";

nodes.name: Status
nodes.body_text: pub enum Status { /// Nothing known yet, or the last check found nothing. #[default] Idle, Checking, /// Downloading, with progress when the server sent a length. `total` is /// `None` for a chunked response — the bar has to degrade to indeterminate /// rather than pretend. /// `version` is what is coming, so the UI can name it before it is ready. Downloading { version: String, received: u64, total: Option<u64> }, /// Downloaded, verified, and waiting for the app to quit. Ready { version: String, notes: Option<String> }, /// The last attempt failed. Held for the UI; the next tick retries. Failed { message: String }, }

nodes.name: Staged
nodes.body_text: struct Staged { update: Update, bytes: Vec<u8>, }

nodes.name: UpdaterState
nodes.body_text: pub struct UpdaterState { status: Mutex<Status>, staged: Mutex<Option<Staged>>, }

nodes.name: set_status
nodes.signature: fn set_status<R: Runtime>(&self, app: &AppHandle<R>, next: Status)
nodes.body_text: fn set_status<R: Runtime>(&self, app: &AppHandle<R>, next: Status) { if let Ok(mut guard) = self.status.lock() { if *guard == next { return; // don't spam the UI with identical frames } *guard = next.clone(); } let _ = app.emit(EVENT, next); }

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.body_text: fn snapshot(&self) -> Status { self.status.lock().map(|s| s.clone()).unwrap_or_default() }

nodes.name: has_staged
nodes.body_text: pub fn has_staged(&self) -> bool { self.staged.lock().map(|s| s.is_some()).unwrap_or(false) }

nodes.name: updater_status
nodes.signature: pub fn updater_status(state: State<'_, UpdaterState>) -> Status
nodes.body_text: pub fn updater_status(state: State<'_, UpdaterState>) -> Status { state.snapshot() }

nodes.name: updater_check_now
nodes.signature: pub async fn updater_check_now(app: AppHandle) -> Result<(), IpcError>
nodes.body_text: pub async fn updater_check_now(app: AppHandle) -> Result<(), IpcError> { check_and_stage(&app).await; Ok(()) }

nodes.name: updater_restart_now
nodes.signature: pub async fn updater_restart_now(app: AppHandle) -> Result<(), IpcError>
nodes.body_text: pub async fn updater_restart_now(app: AppHandle) -> Result<(), IpcError> { install_staged(&app).map_err(|e| IpcError::new("updater", e))?; // Only reached where `install` returns (macOS/Linux); on Windows the // installer has already exited the process. `restart` diverges. app.restart(); }

nodes.name: spawn_cadence
nodes.body_text: pub fn spawn_cadence(app: AppHandle) { tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move { tokio::time::sleep(FIRST_CHECK_DELAY).await; loop { // Once something is staged there is nothing left to look for — the // install happens at quit, and checking again would only discard a // download we already paid for. if !app.state::<UpdaterState>().has_staged() { check_and_stage(&app).await; } tokio::time::sleep(CHECK_INTERVAL).await; } }); }

nodes.name: check_and_stage
nodes.body_text: async fn check_and_stage(app: &AppHandle) { let state = app.state::<UpdaterState>(); state.set_status(app, Status::Checking); let updater = match app.updater() { Ok(u) => u, Err(e) => { state.set_status(app, Status::Failed { message: e.to_string() }); return; } }; let update = match updater.check().await { // No update. Back to idle — this is the overwhelmingly common outcome // and must never look like an error. Ok(None) => { state.set_status(app, Status::Idle); return; } Ok(Some(u)) => u, Err(e) => { // Offline, endpoint down, or an unparseable manifest. Logged, not // surfaced loudly: a failed check is not the user's problem. log(&format!("updater: check failed: {e}")); state.set_status(app, Status::Failed { message: e.to_string() }); return; } }; let version = update.version.clone(); let notes = update.body.clone(); log(&format!("updater: {version} available, downloading")); let mut received: u64 = 0; let downloaded = update .download( |chunk, total| { received += chunk as u64; app.state::<UpdaterState>().set_status( app, Status::Downloading { version: version.clone(), received, total }, ); }, || {}, ) .await; match downloaded { Ok(bytes) => { log(&format!("updater: {version} staged ({} bytes)", bytes.len())); if let Ok(mut slot) = state.staged.lock() { *slot = Some(Staged { update, bytes }); } state.set_status(app, Status::Ready { version, notes }); } Err(e) => { // Unresumable: the partial download is gone. The next tick starts over. log(&format!("updater: download failed: {e}")); state.set_status(app, Status::Failed { message: e.to_string() }); } } }

nodes.name: stage_teardown
nodes.body_text: fn stage_teardown<R: Runtime>(app: &AppHandle<R>) { if let Some(engine) = app.try_state::<hm_audio::AudioEngine>() { // Mirrors `stop_system_audio`: Linux/Windows own a self-contained EQ // session to drop, while macOS's routing lives in the playing source, so // stopping the engine is what releases the tap and its aggregate device. #[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "windows"))] engine.stop_system_eq(); #[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "windows")))] engine.stop(); } // Known gap, stated rather than hidden: the settings autosave runs on a 2s // debounce and there is no flush hook, so up to two seconds of very recent // changes are still only in memory here and are lost. Everything older is // already on disk. Not worth a plumbing change to close. }

nodes.name: install_staged
nodes.body_text: fn install_staged<R: Runtime>(app: &AppHandle<R>) -> Result<bool, String> { let state = app.state::<UpdaterState>(); let staged = match state.staged.lock() { Ok(mut slot) => slot.take(), Err(_) => None, }; let Some(Staged { update, bytes }) = staged else { return Ok(false); }; log(&format!("updater: installing {}", update.version)); stage_teardown(app); update.install(bytes).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; Ok(true) }

nodes.name: install_on_exit
nodes.body_text: pub fn install_on_exit<R: Runtime>(app: &AppHandle<R>) { match install_staged(app) { Ok(true) => log("updater: installed on exit"), Ok(false) => {} Err(e) => log(&format!("updater: install on exit failed: {e}")), } }

nodes.name: YtLibraryCache

nodes.name: new
nodes.body_text: pub fn new(path: PathBuf) -> Self { Self { inner: OnceLock::new(), path, } }

nodes.name: cell
nodes.body_text: fn cell(&self) -> &Mutex<Option<CachedLibrary>> { self.inner.get_or_init(|| { let loaded = std::fs::File::open(&self.path) .ok() .and_then(|f| serde_json::from_reader(std::io::BufReader::new(f)).ok()); Mutex::new(loaded) }) }

nodes.name: warm
nodes.body_text: pub fn warm(&self) { let _ = self.cell(); }

nodes.name: get
nodes.body_text: pub fn get(&self) -> Option<CachedLibrary> { self.cell().lock().expect("yt cache poisoned").clone() }

nodes.name: put
nodes.body_text: pub fn put(&self, lib: CachedLibrary) { { let mut slot = self.cell().lock().expect("yt cache poisoned"); *slot = Some(lib); } self.write(); }

nodes.name: clear
nodes.body_text: pub fn clear(&self) { { let mut slot = self.cell().lock().expect("yt cache poisoned"); *slot = None; } let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&self.path); }

nodes.name: write
nodes.body_text: fn write(&self) { let slot = self.cell().lock().expect("yt cache poisoned"); let Some(lib) = slot.as_ref() else { return }; let Ok(json) = serde_json::to_string(lib) else { return; }; let tmp = self.path.with_extension("json.tmp"); if std::fs::write(&tmp, json).is_ok() { let _ = std::fs::rename(&tmp, &self.path); } }

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.body_text: struct Settings { /// Where downloads land. `None` means "use the default" — stored as absent /// rather than resolved, so a user who never chose a folder follows the OS /// music dir if it changes, instead of being pinned to wherever they first /// launched. #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] download_dir: Option<String>, }

nodes.name: YtSettings
nodes.body_text: pub struct YtSettings { inner: Mutex<Settings>, path: PathBuf, /// The OS music dir, resolved at startup (Tauri's path API needs the app /// handle, which commands shouldn't have to thread through for this). default_dir: PathBuf, }

nodes.name: load
nodes.signature: pub fn load(path: PathBuf, default_dir: PathBuf) -> Self
nodes.body_text: pub fn load(path: PathBuf, default_dir: PathBuf) -> Self { let inner = std::fs::read_to_string(&path) .ok() .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok()) .unwrap_or_default(); Self { inner: Mutex::new(inner), path, default_dir, } }

nodes.name: download_dir
nodes.body_text: pub fn download_dir(&self) -> PathBuf { self.inner .lock() .expect("yt settings poisoned") .download_dir .as_ref() .map(PathBuf::from) .unwrap_or_else(|| self.default_dir.join("HypeMuzik")) }

nodes.name: set_download_dir
nodes.body_text: pub fn set_download_dir(&self, dir: Option<String>) { { let mut s = self.inner.lock().expect("yt settings poisoned"); s.download_dir = dir.filter(|d| !d.trim().is_empty()); } self.write(); }

nodes.name: write
nodes.body_text: fn write(&self) { let s = self.inner.lock().expect("yt settings poisoned"); let Ok(json) = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&*s) else { return; }; let tmp = self.path.with_extension("json.tmp"); if std::fs::write(&tmp, json).is_ok() { let _ = std::fs::rename(&tmp, &self.path); } }

Surface it — and copy it to the clipboard — so the user can finish. useEffect(() => { let unlisten: UnlistenFn | undefined; let cancelled = false; void listen("system-eq-setup-manual", (e) => { const command = e.payload; void navigator.clipboard?.writeText(command).catch(() => {}); toast.info(`System-wide EQ needs a component. It NEVER returns a sign-in screen or a "trial ended" screen — * gating for Advanced DSP / stems / cloud happens per-feature via * `<PremiumGate>` / `requirePremium`, not here. Offline on first launch still * opens the app (core needs no network); the bootstrap retries on the next * focus or periodic refresh. */

function SessionGate({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { const status = useAccountStore((s) => s.status); const loading = useAccountStore((s) => s.loading); const refresh = useAccountStore((s) => s.refresh); const bootstrapAnonymous = useAccountStore((s) => s.bootstrapAnonymous); const refreshEntitlement = useEntitlementStore((s) => s.refresh); const appInfo = useUiStore((s) => s.appInfo); // Initial + periodic re-check (a claimed email / Supporter status can // change server-side while running). useEffect(() => { void refresh(); const t = setInterval(() => void refresh(), REFRESH_MS); return () => clearInterval(t); }, [refresh]); // Ensure a session always exists. Fires whenever we learn there isn't // one — first launch (no local tokens), a dead refresh token that got // cleared, or right after the user signs out — so the app is never stuck // sessionless. Idempotent server-side (same install id → same user), and // guarded here so an offline stretch doesn't fire this on every re-render. const bootstrapping = useRef(false); useEffect(() => { if (!status || status.authenticated || bootstrapping.current) return; bootstrapping.current = true; void bootstrapAnonymous().finally(() => { bootstrapping.current = false; }); }, [status, bootstrapAnonymous]); // Entitlements follow the session: fetch as soon as we're authenticated, // and on the periodic/focus refreshes below. useEffect(() => { if (status?.authenticated) void refreshEntitlement(); }, [status?.authenticated, refreshEntitlement]); // Re-check everything whenever the app regains focus / becomes visible. // The interval above is suspended while the machine sleeps, so without this // a claimed-email / Supporter change (or a first-launch offline bootstrap) // could sit stale until the next 5-min tick. Throttled so rapid focus // changes don't spam the server; the single-flight token refresh makes // frequent re-checks safe. const lastActiveRefresh = useRef(Date.now()); useEffect(() => { const onActive = () => { if (document.visibilityState !== "visible") return; const now = Date.now(); if (now - lastActiveRefresh.current < 30_000) return; lastActiveRefresh.current = now; void refresh(); void refreshEntitlement(); }; window.addEventListener("focus", onActive); document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", onActive); return () => { window.removeEventListener("focus", onActive); document.removeEventListener("visibilitychange", onActive); }; }, [refresh, refreshEntitlement]); // Heartbeats while a session exists (anonymous sessions are "authenticated" // too, so usage is counted from the very first launch). const authed = status?.authenticated ?? false; useEffect(() => { if (!authed) return; const version = appInfo?.version ?? "dev"; const platform = detectPlatform(); void accountHeartbeat(platform, version); const t = setInterval( () => void accountHeartbeat(platform, version), HEARTBEAT_MS, ); return () => clearInterval(t); }, [authed, appInfo]); // Only ever a brief spinner for the very first bootstrap — never a wall. if (loading && !status) { return (
); } return <>{children}; }

nodes.body_text: function detectPlatform(): string { if (typeof navigator === "undefined") return "desktop"; const ua = navigator.userAgent.toLowerCase(); if (ua.includes("mac")) return "macos"; if (ua.includes("win")) return "windows"; if (ua.includes("linux")) return "linux"; return "desktop"; }

nodes.name: bridge.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Inbound frames → the player. `cmd`s run one at a time and are acked when * accepted; `rpc`s answer as soon as their lookup finishes; `welcome` and * `devices` feed the device list (and, v1.2, the remote session and the * claim/yield rules, with `state`, `ack` and `error`); `pong` feeds the hub clock and the hub's * `viz_sub` starts or stops the visualiser stream (v1.1). */ import { CommandQueue, executeCommand, type PlayerPort } from "./commands"; import { decodeFrame, type AckError, type DeviceInfo, type Frame, type PlayerState } from "./protocol"; import type { QueueUidTracker } from "./queueUids"; import { executeRpc, type RpcPort } from "./rpc"; /** `{t, id}` of a frame that didn't decode, so it can still be answered. */

nodes.name: BridgeDeps
nodes.body_text: interface BridgeDeps { player: PlayerPort; rpc: RpcPort; uids: QueueUidTracker; send(frame: Frame): Promise<void>; onDevices?(devices: DeviceInfo[], activeDeviceId: string | null): void; /** The hub's clock at `welcome` (a first guess before any `pong`). */ onWelcome?(serverTime: number): void; /** `welcome` in full: the devices, who is active and every online player's * latest state (v1.2: this app can be a remote). Runs before `onDevices`. */ onWelcomeStates?( devices: DeviceInfo[], activeDeviceId: string | null, states: Record<string, PlayerState>, ): void; /** Another player's state (v1.2). */ onState?(deviceId: string | undefined, state: PlayerState): void; /** The answer to a `cmd` this app sent as a remote (v1.2). */ onAck?(id: string, ok: boolean, error?: AckError): void; /** `error` from the hub (v1.2: `not_a_player` ends a claim). */ onError?(code: string, message: string): void; onPong?(id: string, serverTime: number): void; /** The hub's subscriber count went 0 → 1 (`true`) or 1 → 0 (`false`). */ onVizSub?(on: boolean): void; }

nodes.name: idOf
nodes.signature: function idOf(raw: unknown): { t: unknown; id: string } | null
nodes.body_text: function idOf(raw: unknown): { t: unknown; id: string } | null { if (typeof raw !== "object" || raw === null) return null; const { t, id } = raw as { t?: unknown; id?: unknown }; return typeof id === "string" ? { t, id } : null; }

nodes.name: createInboundHandler
nodes.body_text: function createInboundHandler(deps: BridgeDeps): (raw: unknown) => void { const commands = new CommandQueue(); const send = (frame: Frame) => deps.send(frame).catch(() => {}); return (raw) => { const frame = decodeFrame(raw); if (!frame) { // Rust already validated it, so this is a version skew between the two // halves; answer rather than leave the controller waiting for a timeout. const head = idOf(raw); if (head?.t === "cmd") void send({ t: "ack", id: head.id, ok: false, error: "unsupported" }); if (head?.t === "rpc") { void send({ t: "rpc_result", id: head.id, ok: false, error: "unsupported" }); } return; } switch (frame.t) { case "cmd": { const { id, cmd } = frame; void commands.run(async () => { const outcome = await executeCommand(cmd, deps.player, deps.uids); await send( outcome.ok ? { t: "ack", id, ok: true } : { t: "ack", id, ok: false, error: outcome.error }, ); }); return; } case "rpc": { const { id, method, params } = frame; void executeRpc(method, params, deps.rpc).then((outcome) => send( outcome.ok ? { t: "rpc_result", id, ok: true, result: outcome.result } : { t: "rpc_result", id, ok: false, error: outcome.error }, ), ); return; } case "welcome": deps.onWelcome?.(frame.serverTime); deps.onWelcomeStates?.(frame.devices, frame.activeDeviceId, frame.states); deps.onDevices?.(frame.devices, frame.activeDeviceId); return; case "devices": deps.onDevices?.(frame.devices, frame.activeDeviceId); return; case "state": deps.onState?.(frame.deviceId, frame.state); return; case "ack": deps.onAck?.(frame.id, frame.ok, frame.error); return; case "error": deps.onError?.(frame.code, frame.message); return; case "pong": deps.onPong?.(frame.id, frame.serverTime); return; case "viz_sub": deps.onVizSub?.(frame.on); return; default: return; } }; }

expect(port.enqueue).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2); }); }); describe("pause / resume are explicit, never toggles", () => { it("pause pauses only a playing track", async () => { const playing = fakePort({ playing: true, paused: false }); await run({ type: "pause" }, playing.port); expect(playing.port.pause).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); const paused = fakePort({ playing: true, paused: true }); expect(await run({ type: "pause" }, paused.port)).toEqual({ ok: true }); expect(paused.port.pause).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); const idle = fakePort(); await run({ type: "pause" }, idle.port); expect(idle.port.pause).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); it("resume un-pauses a paused track and leaves a playing one alone", async () => { const paused = fakePort({ playing: true, paused: true }); await run({ type: "resume" }, paused.port); expect(paused.port.resume).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); const playing = fakePort({ playing: true, paused: false }); expect(await run({ type: "resume" }, playing.port)).toEqual({ ok: true }); expect(playing.port.resume).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); expect(playing.port.jumpTo).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); it("resume when stopped replays the track the queue ended on", async () => { const { port } = fakePort({ playing: false, queue: [ytItem("a"), ytItem("b")], order: [0, 1], orderPos: 1 }); expect(await run({ type: "resume" }, port)).toEqual({ ok: true }); expect(port.jumpTo).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1); }); it("resume with an empty queue is nothing_playable", async () => { const { port } = fakePort(); expect(await run({ type: "resume" }, port)).toEqual({ ok: false, error: "nothing_playable" }); expect(port.jumpTo).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); }); describe("seek", () => { it("converts ms to seconds and clamps negatives to 0", async () => { const { port } = fakePort(); await run({ type: "seek", positionMs: 90_250 }, port); expect(port.seek).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(90.25); await run({ type: "seek", positionMs: -5 }, port); expect(port.seek).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(0); }); it("is unsupported on a source that cannot seek", async () => { const { port } = fakePort({ seekable: false }); expect(await run({ type: "seek", positionMs: 1000 }, port)).toEqual({ ok: false, error: "unsupported", }); expect(port.jumpTo).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1); }); it("an unknown uid fails without jumping", async () => { const queue = [ytItem("a")]; const { port } = fakePort({ playing: true, queue, order: [0], orderPos: 0 }); expect(await run({ type: "jump", uid: "nope" }, port)).toEqual({ ok: false, error: "failed" }); expect(port.jumpTo).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); }); describe("simple transport", () => { it("volume is clamped to 0..1", async () => { const { port } = fakePort(); await run({ type: "volume", value: 1.7 }, port); await run({ type: "volume", value: -0.3 }, port); await run({ type: "volume", value: 0.4 }, port); expect(port.setVolume.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0])).toEqual([1, 0, 0.4]); await run({ type: "next" }, port); await run({ type: "prev" }, port); await run({ type: "stop" }, port); expect(port.setShuffle.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0])).toEqual([true, false]); expect(port.setRepeat).toHaveBeenCalledWith("one"); expect(port.next).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); expect(port.prev).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); expect(port.stop).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); }); }); describe("CommandQueue", () => { it("runs tasks strictly in arrival order, even when an earlier one is slow", async () => { const q = new CommandQueue(); const log: string[] = []; const slow = q.run(async () => { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 20)); log.push("play"); }); const fast = q.run(async () => { log.push("pause"); }); await Promise.all([slow, fast]); nodes.name: commands.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Remote commands → the app's own player. * * Every command is mapped onto the same engine-store actions the UI uses, so * a remote `play` rides exactly the streaming/gapless/radio stack a click * does. Two rules from the contract shape everything here: * * - **Explicit states, never toggles.** `pause` while paused, `shuffle on` * while on: no-ops, never flips. Two controllers racing can't invert state. * - **Never navigate.** Nothing here opens a view or steals focus; the app's * UI simply follows the store like it does for the OS media keys. * * The ack goes out once the command is *accepted* (queued/applied), not when * audio starts; the next `state` shows the outcome. */ import { localItem, ytmusicItem, type QueueItem } from "@/stores/engine"; import type { LibraryTrack, YtTrack } from "@/lib/types"; import type { AckError, Command, RepeatMode, TrackRef } from "./protocol"; import type { QueueUidTracker } from "./queueUids"; import { msToSecs, ytRefToTrack } from "./refs"; /** What the executor needs to see of the player. */ /** The player, as far as remote commands are concerned. The real one is * `enginePlayerPort()` over the engine store; tests use a fake. */ const OK: AckOutcome = { ok: true }; /** A ref as a queue item this desktop can play, or null to skip it: another * device's `local` track, a path that isn't in the library, or an `other` * ref (which belongs in `state` only). */ /** Resolve `refs`, dropping what can't play here, and re-base `index` onto * what's left: the requested item if it survived, else the next playable * one after it, else the closest one before it. */ /** Execute one command. Never throws: a failure is an ack. */ /** * Runs commands one at a time, in arrival order. A `play` that waits on the * library must not be overtaken by the `pause` sent right after it. */

nodes.name: PlayerSnapshot
nodes.body_text: interface PlayerSnapshot { playing: boolean; paused: boolean; seekable: boolean; queue: readonly QueueItem[]; order: readonly number[]; orderPos: number; }

nodes.name: PlayerPort
nodes.body_text: interface PlayerPort { /** This desktop's Connect device id (its install id). */ deviceId(): string; /** A track from this device's library by path, or null if it isn't there. */ findLocal(path: string): Promise<LibraryTrack | null>; snapshot(): PlayerSnapshot; playItems(items: QueueItem[], index: number): void; /** Play `seed` and let YT Music's radio grow the queue behind it — what * tapping a search result in the app does. */ playRadio(seed: YtTrack): void; /** Seek to `secs` once the track that was just started can seek. */ startAt(secs: number): void; enqueue(items: QueueItem[], mode: "next" | "end"): void; pause(): void; resume(): void; jumpTo(orderPos: number): void; next(): void; prev(): void; seek(secs: number): void; stop(): Promise<void>; setVolume(value: number): void; setShuffle(on: boolean): void; setRepeat(mode: RepeatMode): void; }

nodes.name: AckOutcome
nodes.signature: type AckOutcome = { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: AckError };
nodes.body_text: type AckOutcome = { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: AckError };

nodes.name: refuse
nodes.body_text: refuse = (error: AckError): AckOutcome => ({ ok: false, error })

nodes.name: playable
nodes.signature: async function playable(ref: TrackRef, port: PlayerPort): Promise<QueueItem | null>
nodes.body_text: async function playable(ref: TrackRef, port: PlayerPort): Promise<QueueItem | null> { switch (ref.src) { case "yt": return ytmusicItem(ytRefToTrack(ref)); case "local": { if (ref.deviceId !== port.deviceId()) return null; const track = await port.findLocal(ref.id); return track ? localItem(track) : null; } case "other": return null; } }

nodes.name: resolvePlayable
nodes.signature: async function resolvePlayable( refs: readonly TrackRef[], index: number, port: PlayerPort, ): Promise<{ items: QueueItem[]; start: number }>
nodes.body_text: async function resolvePlayable( refs: readonly TrackRef[], index: number, port: PlayerPort, ): Promise<{ items: QueueItem[]; start: number }> { const resolved = await Promise.all(refs.map((r) => playable(r, port))); const items: QueueItem[] = []; let start = -1; let before = -1; resolved.forEach((item, i) => { if (!item) return; if (i >= index && start < 0) start = items.length; if (i < index) before = items.length; items.push(item); }); if (start < 0) start = Math.max(0, before); return { items, start }; }

nodes.name: executeCommand
nodes.signature: async function executeCommand( cmd: Command, port: PlayerPort, uids: QueueUidTracker, ): Promise<AckOutcome>
nodes.body_text: async function executeCommand( cmd: Command, port: PlayerPort, uids: QueueUidTracker, ): Promise<AckOutcome> { try { return await execute(cmd, port, uids); } catch { return refuse("failed"); } }

nodes.name: execute
nodes.signature: async function execute(cmd: Command, port: PlayerPort, uids: QueueUidTracker): Promise<AckOutcome>
nodes.body_text: async function execute(cmd: Command, port: PlayerPort, uids: QueueUidTracker): Promise<AckOutcome> { switch (cmd.type) { case "play": { const { items, start } = await resolvePlayable(cmd.items, cmd.index, port); const first = items[start]; if (!first) return refuse("nothing_playable"); if (cmd.radio && first.ytTrack) { // One tapped result: it plays, its radio fills in behind it. port.playRadio(first.ytTrack); } else { port.playItems(items, start); } const at = msToSecs(cmd.positionMs); if (at !== null && at > 0) port.startAt(at); return OK; } case "enqueue": { const { items } = await resolvePlayable(cmd.items, 0, port); if (items.length === 0) return refuse("nothing_playable"); port.enqueue(items, cmd.mode); return OK; } case "pause": { const s = port.snapshot(); if (s.playing && !s.paused) port.pause(); return OK; } case "resume": { const s = port.snapshot(); if (s.playing) { if (s.paused) port.resume(); return OK; } // Ended or stopped: replay the track the queue is parked on, if any. if (s.orderPos >= 0 && s.orderPos < s.order.length) { port.jumpTo(s.orderPos); return OK; } return refuse("nothing_playable"); } case "stop": await port.stop(); return OK; case "next": port.next(); return OK; case "prev": port.prev(); return OK; case "seek": { if (!port.snapshot().seekable) return refuse("unsupported"); port.seek(Math.max(0, cmd.positionMs) / 1000); return OK; } case "jump": { const s = port.snapshot(); const qi = uids.uidsFor(s.queue).indexOf(cmd.uid); const pos = qi < 0 ? -1 : s.order.indexOf(qi); if (pos < 0) return refuse("failed"); port.jumpTo(pos); return OK; } case "volume": port.setVolume(Math.min(1, Math.max(0, cmd.value))); return OK; case "shuffle": port.setShuffle(cmd.on); return OK; case "repeat": port.setRepeat(cmd.mode); return OK; } }

nodes.name: CommandQueue
nodes.body_text: class CommandQueue { private tail: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve(); run(task: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> { const next = this.tail.then(task, task); this.tail = next.catch(() => {}); return next; } }

nodes.body_text: /** Pure display helpers for the Hype Connect card. */ import type { ConnectStatus } from "@/lib/ipc"; import type { DeviceInfo } from "./protocol"; const PLATFORMS: Record<string, string> = { macos: "macOS", windows: "Windows", linux: "Linux", android: "Android", ios: "iOS", }; /** "Chrome on macOS" is already the name a browser links under; players get * their platform appended. */ /** "483920" → "483 920", the way it's read aloud. */ /** Seconds until `iso`, never negative. */

nodes.name: Tone
nodes.body_text: type Tone = "ok" | "busy" | "warn" | "off";

nodes.name: ConnectionView
nodes.body_text: interface ConnectionView { tone: Tone; title: string; detail: string; /** Offer "Reconnect" (the client stopped and won't retry on its own). */ canReconnect: boolean; }

nodes.name: describeConnection
nodes.body_text: function describeConnection(status: ConnectStatus | null): ConnectionView { const view = (tone: Tone, title: string, detail: string, canReconnect = false) => ({ tone, title, detail, canReconnect, }); if (!status) return view("busy", "Starting…", "Checking Hype Connect."); if (!status.enabled) { return view("off", "Off", "Turn on to play music on this desktop from a browser."); } const c = status.connection; if (!c) return view("busy", "Starting…", "Opening the connection."); switch (c.state) { case "connected": return view( "ok", "Ready", "Pick this desktop in Hype Muzik on the web and the music plays here.", ); case "connecting": return view("busy", "Connecting…", "Reaching the Hype Connect service."); case "waiting": { const secs = Math.max(1, Math.round(c.retryInMs / 1000)); return view("warn", `Reconnecting in ${secs}s`, c.reason); } case "no_session": return view("busy", "Waiting for your account…", "Hype Connect starts once you're signed in."); case "stopped": switch (c.reason) { case "unlinked": return view( "warn", "Unlinked", "This desktop was removed from your devices. Reconnect to add it back.", true, ); case "replaced": return view( "warn", "In use elsewhere", "Another copy of Hype Muzik on this computer took over Hype Connect.", true, ); case "tls_unavailable": return view("warn", "Can't secure the connection", "Hype Connect couldn't set up TLS.", true); case "shutdown": return view("off", "Stopped", "Hype Connect isn't running.", true); } } }

nodes.name: deviceSubtitle
nodes.signature: function deviceSubtitle(d: DeviceInfo, now: number): string
nodes.body_text: function deviceSubtitle(d: DeviceInfo, now: number): string { const parts = [platformLabel(d.platform)]; parts.push(d.online ? "Online" : lastSeen(d.lastSeenAt, now)); return parts.filter(Boolean).join(" · "); }

nodes.name: lastSeen
nodes.signature: function lastSeen(iso: string, now: number): string
nodes.body_text: function lastSeen(iso: string, now: number): string { const at = Date.parse(iso); if (!Number.isFinite(at)) return "Offline"; const mins = Math.floor((now - at) / 60_000); if (mins < 1) return "Seen just now"; if (mins < 60) return `Seen ${mins} min ago`; const hours = Math.floor(mins / 60); if (hours < 24) return `Seen ${hours} h ago`; return `Seen ${Math.floor(hours / 24)} d ago`; }

nodes.name: formatCode
nodes.body_text: function formatCode(code: string): string { return code.length === 6 ? `${code.slice(0, 3)} ${code.slice(3)}` : code; }

nodes.name: secondsUntil
nodes.signature: function secondsUntil(iso: string, now: number): number
nodes.body_text: function secondsUntil(iso: string, now: number): number { const at = Date.parse(iso); return Number.isFinite(at) ? Math.max(0, Math.ceil((at - now) / 1000)) : 0; }

nodes.body_text: import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"; import { CLOCK_INTERVAL_MS, CLOCK_WINDOW, ClockSync, HubClock, MAX_ROUND_TRIP_MS, } from "./hubClock"; describe("HubClock", () => { it("measures offset = serverTime - (sent + received) / 2", () => { const c = new HubClock(); // Hub clock is 5000 ms ahead; the pong took 100 ms, answered mid-flight. expect(c.addSample(1000, 1100, 1050 + 5000)).toBe(true); expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(5000); expect(c.roundTripMs).toBe(100); }); it("is unknown before any sample, and nowMs() is then the local clock", () => { const c = new HubClock(() => 123_456); expect(c.offsetMs).toBeNull(); expect(c.roundTripMs).toBeNull(); expect(c.isMeasured).toBe(false); expect(c.nowMs()).toBe(123_456); }); it("nowMs() is local time plus the offset", () => { let local = 10_000; const c = new HubClock(() => local); c.addSample(0, 40, 20 + 700); expect(c.nowMs()).toBe(10_700); local += 250; expect(c.nowMs()).toBe(10_950); }); it("trusts the fastest round trip, not the newest", () => { const c = new HubClock(); c.addSample(0, 400, 200 + 1000); // slow: offset 1000, rtt 400 c.addSample(1000, 1040, 1020 + 1300); // fast: offset 1300, rtt 40 c.addSample(2000, 2300, 2150 + 900); // slow again expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(1300); expect(c.roundTripMs).toBe(40); }); it("on a tie, the newest sample wins", () => { const c = new HubClock(); c.addSample(0, 50, 25 + 100); c.addSample(100, 150, 125 + 200); expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(200); }); it("lets an old good sample age out after the window, so the offset can follow a drifting clock", () => { const c = new HubClock(); c.addSample(0, 10, 5 + 1000); // the best ever, offset 1000 for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { c.addSample(i * 1000, i * 1000 + 100, i * 1000 + 50 + 2000); // offset 2000, rtt 100 } expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(2000); }); it("compares the last five samples by default, every ten seconds", () => { expect(CLOCK_WINDOW).toBe(5); expect(CLOCK_INTERVAL_MS).toBe(10_000); }); it("keeps exactly the last `window` samples", () => { const c = new HubClock(() => 0, 2); c.addSample(0, 10, 5 + 111); // rtt 10, will be pushed out c.addSample(0, 20, 10 + 222); c.addSample(0, 30, 15 + 333); expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(222); // 111 gone, fastest of the last two }); it("rejects a negative or absurd round trip, and non-finite input", () => { const c = new HubClock(); expect(c.addSample(1000, 900, 5000)).toBe(false); // clock stepped back expect(c.addSample(0, MAX_ROUND_TRIP_MS + 1, 5000)).toBe(false); expect(c.addSample(0, Number.NaN, 5000)).toBe(false); expect(c.addSample(0, 10, Number.NaN)).toBe(false); expect(c.offsetMs).toBeNull(); expect(c.addSample(0, MAX_ROUND_TRIP_MS, 5000)).toBe(true); }); it("uses the welcome's time only until a real sample arrives", () => { const c = new HubClock(() => 0); c.seedFromWelcome(9_000, 8_000); expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(1000); expect(c.isMeasured, "a seed is not a measurement").toBe(false); c.seedFromWelcome(99_000, 8_000); // only the first seed counts expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(1000); c.addSample(0, 20, 10 + 400); expect(c.offsetMs).toBe(400); expect(c.isMeasured).toBe(true); }); it("clear() forgets samples and seed", () => { const c = new HubClock(); c.seedFromWelcome(2, 1); c.addSample(0, 10, 100); c.clear(); expect(c.offsetMs).toBeNull(); }); }); describe("ClockSync", () => { it("pings at once on start, then on every interval tick", () => { const t = sync(); t.s.start(); expect(t.sent).toHaveLength(1); t.fire(); t.fire(); expect(t.sent).toHaveLength(3); expect(new Set(t.sent).size, "ids are unique").toBe(3); }); it("turns a pong into a sample against the time the ping left", () => { const t = sync(); t.s.start(); t.advance(80); t.s.onPong(t.sent[0]!, 1_000_040 + 700); // hub is 700 ahead expect(t.clock.offsetMs).toBe(700); expect(t.clock.roundTripMs).toBe(80); }); it("ignores a pong it never asked for, and a repeated one", () => { const t = sync(); t.s.start(); t.s.onPong("someone-else", 5); expect(t.clock.isMeasured).toBe(false); t.advance(10); t.s.onPong(t.sent[0]!, 1_000_005 + 1); t.advance(500); t.s.onPong(t.sent[0]!, 9_999_999); expect(t.clock.offsetMs).toBe(1); }); it("stop() cancels the timer and forgets in-flight pings, but keeps the measured offset", () => { const t = sync(); t.s.start(); t.advance(20); t.s.onPong(t.sent[0]!, 1_000_010 + 50); t.fire(); const inFlight = t.sent[1]!; t.s.stop(); expect(t.cleared).toEqual(["timer"]); t.s.onPong(inFlight, 0); expect(t.clock.offsetMs).toBe(50); }); it("start() again (a new welcome) replaces the timer instead of stacking one", () => { const t = sync(); nodes.name: hubClock.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * This desktop's view of the hub's clock (§3.7), done in TypeScript: the * `ping`/`pong` frames already cross the IPC boundary, and everything that * needs hub time (a viz frame's `heardAt`) lives here too. * * # One sample * * `ping` leaves at local time `sent`; `pong` returns at `received` carrying the * hub's `serverTime`. The hub answered somewhere in between; assuming the * middle, the hub clock read `serverTime` when ours read `(sent + received) / 2`: * * offset = serverTime - (sent + received) / 2 * * That assumption errs by at most half the round trip, so the best sample is * the one with the *smallest* round trip. {@link HubClock} keeps the last * {@link CLOCK_WINDOW} samples and trusts the fastest: one slow exchange can't * move the estimate, and a good old one ages out after five samples instead of * pinning the offset forever (clocks drift; users change them). * * {@link ClockSync} takes a sample on every `welcome` and every * {@link CLOCK_INTERVAL_MS} after. */ /** Samples compared. */ export const CLOCK_WINDOW = 5; /** Re-measure this often while connected. */ export const CLOCK_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000; /** A round trip longer than this measures nothing (a clock set mid-flight, a * pong that sat in a queue for ages). */ export const MAX_ROUND_TRIP_MS = 10_000; /** Pings the hub on connect and then periodically; feeds the pongs to a * {@link HubClock}. */

nodes.name: Sample
nodes.body_text: interface Sample { offsetMs: number; roundTripMs: number; }

nodes.name: HubClock
nodes.body_text: class HubClock { private samples: Sample[] = []; private seeded: number | null = null; constructor( private readonly localNow: () => number = () => Date.now(), private readonly window: number = CLOCK_WINDOW, ) {} /** Record one exchange. Returns `false` when it was unusable. */ addSample(sentMs: number, receivedMs: number, serverTimeMs: number): boolean { const roundTripMs = receivedMs - sentMs; if (!Number.isFinite(roundTripMs) || !Number.isFinite(serverTimeMs)) return false; if (roundTripMs < 0 || roundTripMs > MAX_ROUND_TRIP_MS) return false; this.samples.push({ offsetMs: Math.round(serverTimeMs - (sentMs + receivedMs) / 2), roundTripMs, }); while (this.samples.length > this.window) this.samples.shift(); return true; } /** A first guess from `welcome`, used only until a real sample arrives. The * hello→welcome trip includes token verification so it measures nothing, but * a clock off by that is better than one off by the whole offset. */ seedFromWelcome(serverTimeMs: number, receivedMs: number): void { if (this.seeded === null && Number.isFinite(serverTimeMs)) { this.seeded = Math.round(serverTimeMs - receivedMs); } } /** Hub time minus local time; `null` before any sample or seed. */ get offsetMs(): number | null { return this.best()?.offsetMs ?? this.seeded; } /** Whether a real ping/pong exchange has been measured (a seed isn't one). */ get isMeasured(): boolean { return this.samples.length > 0; } /** Round trip of the sample the offset comes from. */ get roundTripMs(): number | null { return this.best()?.roundTripMs ?? null; } /** The hub's epoch ms now. Before a measurement this is the local clock — * off by the offset, but never absent. */ nowMs(): number { return this.localNow() + (this.offsetMs ?? 0); } /** Forget everything (a new account / socket). */ clear(): void { this.samples = []; this.seeded = null; } /** The fastest kept sample; on a tie the newest. */ private best(): Sample | null { let best: Sample | null = null; for (const s of this.samples) { if (best === null || s.roundTripMs <= best.roundTripMs) best = s; } return best; } }

nodes.name: ClockSyncDeps
nodes.body_text: interface ClockSyncDeps { clock: HubClock; sendPing(id: string): Promise<void>; /** Local epoch ms. */ now(): number; setInterval(fn: () => void, ms: number): unknown; clearInterval(handle: unknown): void; }

nodes.name: ClockSync
nodes.body_text: class ClockSync { private pending = new Map<string, number>(); private timer: unknown = null; private counter = 0; constructor(private readonly deps: ClockSyncDeps) {} /** The socket came up (a `welcome` arrived): measure now, then every 10 s. */ start(): void { this.stop(); this.ping(); this.timer = this.deps.setInterval(() => this.ping(), CLOCK_INTERVAL_MS); } /** The socket is gone. The measured offset is kept — it describes the two * clocks, not the connection — but nothing is in flight any more. */ stop(): void { if (this.timer !== null) this.deps.clearInterval(this.timer); this.timer = null; this.pending.clear(); } /** A `pong` arrived. */ onPong(id: string, serverTime: number): void { const sent = this.pending.get(id); if (sent === undefined) return; this.pending.delete(id); this.deps.clock.addSample(sent, this.deps.now(), serverTime); } private ping(): void { const id = `clk-${(this.counter += 1)}`; // Only the freshest few can still be answered usefully. if (this.pending.size >= CLOCK_WINDOW) { const oldest = this.pending.keys().next().value; if (oldest !== undefined) this.pending.delete(oldest); } this.pending.set(id, this.deps.now()); this.deps.sendPing(id).catch(() => this.pending.delete(id)); } }

nodes.body_text: constructor(private readonly deps: ClockSyncDeps) {}

nodes.name: start
nodes.body_text: start(): void { this.stop(); this.ping(); this.timer = this.deps.setInterval(() => this.ping(), CLOCK_INTERVAL_MS); }

nodes.name: stop
nodes.body_text: stop(): void { if (this.timer !== null) this.deps.clearInterval(this.timer); this.timer = null; this.pending.clear(); }

nodes.name: onPong
nodes.body_text: onPong(id: string, serverTime: number): void { const sent = this.pending.get(id); if (sent === undefined) return; this.pending.delete(id); this.deps.clock.addSample(sent, this.deps.now(), serverTime); }

nodes.body_text: private ping(): void { const id = `clk-${(this.counter += 1)}`; // Only the freshest few can still be answered usefully. if (this.pending.size >= CLOCK_WINDOW) { const oldest = this.pending.keys().next().value; if (oldest !== undefined) this.pending.delete(oldest); } this.pending.set(id, this.deps.now()); this.deps.sendPing(id).catch(() => this.pending.delete(id)); }

it("sends a half-timed list unsynced rather than half-timed", () => { const out = lyricsToWire( track, parsed([ { timeMs: 1000, text: "timed", words: [{ timeMs: 1000, text: "timed" }] }, { timeMs: null, text: "untimed" }, ]), ); expect(out.synced).toBe(false); expect(out.lines.map((l) => l.startMs)).toEqual([null, null]); expect(out.lines.map((l) => l.words)).toEqual([null, null]); }); it("applies the LRC [offset:] the panel adds to its clock, never below 0", () => { const out = lyricsToWire( track, parsed( [ { timeMs: 100, text: "early", words: [{ timeMs: 100, text: "early" }], endMs: 1000 }, { timeMs: 1000, text: "later" }, ], { offsetMs: -300 }, ), ); expect(out.lines.map((l) => l.startMs)).toEqual([0, 700]); expect(out.lines[0]!.words).toEqual([{ startMs: 0, endMs: 700, text: "early" }]); const late = lyricsToWire(track, parsed([{ timeMs: 1000, text: "x" }], { offsetMs: 250 })); expect(late.lines[0]!.startMs).toBe(1250); }); it("does not shift unsynced lyrics by an offset", () => { const out = lyricsToWire(track, parsed([{ timeMs: null, text: "x" }], { offsetMs: 500 })); expect(out.lines[0]!.startMs).toBeNull(); expect(await answerLyrics(p)).toEqual(noLyrics(track)); expect(p.resolve).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); it("answers found:false after the window when the lookup is slow, and lets it finish", async () => { vi.useFakeTimers(); nodes.name: lyrics.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * The `lyrics` rpc (§3.8, v1.1): a browser shows the lyrics of whatever this * desktop is playing, so it asks, and the answer is what the Lyrics panel would * show — resolved by the same resolver and cache (`player/useLyrics.ts`), so * the two can't disagree. * * # The 10-second rule * * The hub gives an rpc 15 s. A lookup can outlast that (fingerprinting a * weakly-tagged file, a slow LRCLIB), so after {@link LYRICS_WINDOW_MS} the * answer is `found:false` *now* while the lookup carries on; the resolver * caches what it finds and the controller's next ask is served from there. * Answering late would only buy a `timeout` error. */ import type { LyricLine as AppLine, ParsedLyrics } from "@/lib/lrc"; import type { Lyrics, LyricLine, LyricWord, TrackRef } from "./protocol"; export const LYRICS_WINDOW_MS = 10_000; /** What is playing and what the lookup needs to find its lyrics. */ /** A line that isn't timed shows for ~4 s in the app's synced view when it has * no successor; the same fallback closes the last word. */ const LAST_LINE_MS = 4_000; /** * The wire form of `parsed` for `track`. * * * `synced` means *every* line has a start; a mixed list is sent unsynced * (nothing half-timed). * * Times are track time: the LRC `[offset:]` the Lyrics panel adds to its * clock (`position - offset >= start`) is applied here, so the controller * needs no knowledge of it. * * `words` only when the source really has word timing; each word ends where * the next begins, the last where its line does. * * `source` is `null`: the resolver hands back raw text without saying which * of sidecar / embedded / LRCLIB / backend produced it. */ /** Resolve to `null` after `ms` without cancelling `p`. */ /** Answer one `lyrics` rpc. Never throws and never waits past `windowMs`. */

nodes.body_text: interface LyricsPort { /** The track playing now, or `null` when idle. */ current(): LyricsTarget | null; /** The app's lyrics resolver (cache first); it keeps running if abandoned. */ resolve(target: LyricsTarget): Promise<ParsedLyrics | null>; }

nodes.name: lyricsToWire
nodes.signature: function lyricsToWire(track: TrackRef | null, parsed: ParsedLyrics | null): Lyrics
nodes.body_text: function lyricsToWire(track: TrackRef | null, parsed: ParsedLyrics | null): Lyrics { if (!parsed || !parsed.lines.some((l) => l.text.trim() !== "")) return noLyrics(track); const synced = parsed.synced && parsed.lines.every((l) => l.timeMs !== null); const shift = (ms: number): number => Math.max(0, Math.round(ms + (synced ? parsed.offsetMs : 0))); return { track, found: true, synced, source: null, lines: parsed.lines.map((line): LyricLine => { const start = synced && line.timeMs !== null ? shift(line.timeMs) : null; return { startMs: start, text: line.text.trim(), words: synced ? wordsToWire(line, shift) : null, }; }), }; }

nodes.name: shift
nodes.body_text: shift = (ms: number): number => Math.max(0, Math.round(ms + (synced ? parsed.offsetMs : 0)))

nodes.name: wordsToWire
nodes.signature: function wordsToWire(line: AppLine, shift: (ms: number) => number): LyricWord[] | null
nodes.body_text: function wordsToWire(line: AppLine, shift: (ms: number) => number): LyricWord[] | null { const words = line.words; if (!words || words.length === 0 || line.timeMs === null) return null; const lineEnd = line.endMs ?? line.timeMs + LAST_LINE_MS; return words.map((w, i) => { const startMs = shift(w.timeMs); const end = shift(words[i + 1]?.timeMs ?? lineEnd); return { startMs, endMs: Math.max(startMs, end), text: w.text }; }); }

nodes.name: withWindow
nodes.signature: function withWindow<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T | null>
nodes.body_text: function withWindow<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T | null> { return new Promise((resolve) => { const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(null), ms); p.then( (v) => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(v); }, () => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(null); }, ); }); }

nodes.name: answerLyrics
nodes.signature: async function answerLyrics( port: LyricsPort, windowMs: number = LYRICS_WINDOW_MS, ): Promise<Lyrics>
nodes.body_text: async function answerLyrics( port: LyricsPort, windowMs: number = LYRICS_WINDOW_MS, ): Promise<Lyrics> { const target = port.current(); if (!target) return noLyrics(null); if (target.title === null) return noLyrics(target.track); let lookup: Promise<ParsedLyrics | null>; try { lookup = port.resolve(target); } catch { return noLyrics(target.track); } return lyricsToWire(target.track, await withWindow(lookup, windowMs)); }

nodes.body_text: /** * The real `PlayerPort` / `RpcPort`: the engine store, the music library * store and the YouTube Music IPC — the same calls the app's own views make. */ import { ytmusicArtistPage, ytmusicExploreTracks, ytmusicSearch, ytmusicSearchSuggestions, ytmusicStatus, } from "@/lib/ipc"; import type { LibraryTrack } from "@/lib/types"; import { useEngineStore } from "@/stores/engine"; import { useLibraryStore } from "@/stores/library"; import { useMusicLibraryStore } from "@/stores/musicLibrary"; import { lookupLyrics } from "@/features/player/useLyrics"; import type { PlayerPort } from "./commands"; import type { LyricsPort } from "./lyrics"; import { queueItemToRef } from "./refs"; import type { RpcPort } from "./rpc"; import { activeQueueItem } from "./statePublisher"; /** The `getState`/`subscribe` half of a zustand store. */ /** Resolve once `done(state)` holds, or after `timeoutMs` either way. */ const LIBRARY_WAIT_MS = 6_000; /** The local library, loading it first if nothing has asked for it yet (the * Library view loads it lazily). Waits a bounded time: a huge first load * answers with what has streamed in so far rather than outlast the hub's * command/rpc timeout. */ /** Seek to `secs` once the track that is current *now* is actually playing * and seekable (a stream only becomes seekable once it's open). Gives up if * the track changes or nothing happens within `timeoutMs`. */ /** The Lyrics panel's own resolver and cache, aimed at the track playing now * (`useLyrics` keys it the same way, so a lookup done for one serves the other). */ const SIGNED_IN_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000; const SIGNED_OUT_TTL_MS = 15_000;

nodes.name: waitForStore

[t.track] : [])); }

nodes.signature: function seekWhenReady(store: StoreLike<SeekView>, secs: number, timeoutMs = 20_000): void
nodes.body_text: function seekWhenReady(store: StoreLike<SeekView>, secs: number, timeoutMs = 20_000): void { const track = store.getState().queueIndex; let finished = false; let unsubscribe = () => {}; const finish = () => { finished = true; clearTimeout(timer); unsubscribe(); }; const timer = setTimeout(finish, timeoutMs); const check = (s: SeekView) => { if (finished) return; if (s.queueIndex !== track) return finish(); // A first progress tick (position > 0) means the engine has the source // open; seeking before that can land on the previous track. if (s.playing && s.seekable && s.positionSecs > 0) { finish(); s.seek(secs); } }; unsubscribe = store.subscribe(check); check(store.getState()); }

nodes.name: unsubscribe
nodes.body_text: unsubscribe = () => {}

nodes.name: finish
nodes.body_text: finish = () => { finished = true; clearTimeout(timer); unsubscribe(); }

nodes.name: check
nodes.body_text: check = (s: SeekView) => { if (finished) return; if (s.queueIndex !== track) return finish(); // A first progress tick (position > 0) means the engine has the source // open; seeking before that can land on the previous track. if (s.playing && s.seekable && s.positionSecs > 0) { finish(); s.seek(secs); } }

"", t.artist, t.durationSecs, ), }; }

nodes.body_text: function appRpcPort(deviceId: () => string): RpcPort { // `ytmusic_status` shells out to yt-dlp, so its answer is cached — briefly // when signed out, so signing in is noticed almost at once. let known: { signedIn: boolean; at: number } | null = null; return { deviceId, ytSignedIn: async () => { const now = Date.now(); if (known && now - known.at < (known.signedIn ? SIGNED_IN_TTL_MS : SIGNED_OUT_TTL_MS)) { return known.signedIn; } const { signedIn } = await ytmusicStatus(); known = { signedIn, at: now }; return signedIn; }, forgetSignIn: () => { known = null; }, search: ytmusicSearch, suggest: ytmusicSearchSuggestions, exploreTracks: ytmusicExploreTracks, artistPage: ytmusicArtistPage, localTracks: localLibrary, lyrics: appLyricsPort(deviceId), }; }

nodes.name: protocol.test.ts
nodes.body_text: import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs"; import { join } from "node:path"; import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; import { decodeFrame } from "./protocol"; const DIR = join(process.cwd(), "connect-protocol", "fixtures"); const files = readdirSync(DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".json")); /** REST bodies aren't WebSocket frames. */ describe("fixtures", () => { it("finds the shared fixture set", () => { // 56 fixtures in the v1.1 contract, 6 of them REST bodies. expect(files.length).toBe(56); expect(files.filter(isFrameFixture).length).toBe(50); }); describe.each(files.filter(isFrameFixture))("%s", (file) => { it("decodes and round-trips to the same JSON", () => { const raw = read(file); const frame = decodeFrame(raw); expect(frame).not.toBeNull(); expect(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(frame))).toEqual(raw); }); }); }); describe("decodeFrame rejects what the contract forbids", () => { it("non-objects and unknown frame types", () => { expect(decodeFrame(null)).toBeNull(); expect(decodeFrame("x")).toBeNull(); expect(decodeFrame([])).toBeNull(); expect(decodeFrame({ t: "nope" })).toBeNull(); }); it("a cmd with an unknown command type", () => { const f = cmd(); f.cmd.type = "explode"; expect(decodeFrame(f)).toBeNull(); }); it("a track with an unknown src", () => { const f = cmd(); f.cmd.items[0].src = "spotify"; expect(decodeFrame(f)).toBeNull(); }); it("a cmd without an id", () => { const f = cmd(); delete f.id; expect(decodeFrame(f)).toBeNull(); }); it("a non-finite number where a number is required", () => { const f = cmd(); f.cmd.index = "0"; expect(decodeFrame(f)).toBeNull(); }); it("a repeat mode outside off/all/one", () => { const f = structuredClone(read("cmd.repeat.json")) as Record<string, any>; f.cmd.mode = "twice"; expect(decodeFrame(f)).toBeNull(); }); it("an ack with an unknown error code", () => { const f = structuredClone(read("ack.error.json")) as Record<string, any>; f.error = "kaboom"; expect(decodeFrame(f)).toBeNull(); }); }); describe("v1.1", () => { it("keeps the v1.1 caps and drops caps it doesn't know", () => { const hello = decodeFrame(read("hello.mobile.v11.json")); expect(hello).toMatchObject({ t: "hello", device: { caps: ["player", "yt", "local", "lyrics", "viz"] }, }); const welcome = clone("welcome.json"); welcome.devices[0].caps = ["player", "hologram", "viz", 7, null]; const w = decodeFrame(welcome); expect(w?.t === "welcome" && w.devices[0]?.caps).toEqual(["player", "viz"]); const devices = clone("devices.json"); devices.devices[0].caps = ["hologram"]; const decoded = decodeFrame(devices); expect(decoded?.t === "devices" && decoded.devices[0]?.caps).toEqual([]); }); it("still rejects a caps field that isn't a list", () => { const devices = clone("devices.json"); devices.devices[0].caps = "player"; expect(decodeFrame(devices)).toBeNull(); }); it("decodes the lyrics rpc", () => { expect(decodeFrame(read("rpc.lyrics.from.json"))).toMatchObject({ t: "rpc", method: "lyrics", params: {}, }); }); it("keeps a viz_sub's direction", () => { expect(decodeFrame(read("viz_sub.player.on.json"))).toEqual({ t: "viz_sub", on: true }); expect(decodeFrame(read("viz_sub.to.json"))).toMatchObject({ t: "viz_sub", on: true, to: expect.any(String) }); const bad = clone("viz_sub.player.on.json"); bad.on = "yes"; expect(decodeFrame(bad)).toBeNull(); }); it("rejects a viz frame that isn't exactly 32 numeric bands", () => { const short = clone("viz.player.json"); short.frame.bands.pop(); expect(decodeFrame(short)).toBeNull(); const long = clone("viz.player.json"); long.frame.bands.push(0.5); expect(decodeFrame(long)).toBeNull(); const text = clone("viz.player.json"); text.frame.bands[4] = "0.5"; expect(decodeFrame(text)).toBeNull(); const nolevel = clone("viz.player.json"); delete nolevel.frame.level; expect(decodeFrame(nolevel)).toBeNull(); }); });

nodes.name: protocol.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Hype Connect protocol v1 (+ v1.1: the `lyrics` rpc and the visualiser * stream) — the TypeScript side of * `hypemuzik-management/backend/docs/hype-connect.md`. * * Rust (`crates/hm-connect`) owns the socket and already validates every * frame it forwards, but the webview still decodes what crosses the IPC * boundary instead of casting it: `decodeFrame` returns a canonical object * (only the contract's keys, nullable fields kept as `null`, optional ones * omitted) or `null`. Every frame fixture round-trips through it in * `protocol.test.ts`. */ /** A track in one device's own library; the desktop's `id` is the file path. */ /** Cloud, phone-link, radio … — only ever in `state`, never in commands. */ /** One timed word of a lyric line (§3.8). */ /** The `lyrics` rpc result (§3.8, v1.1). */ /** Bands in a `viz` frame (§3.11). */ export const VIZ_BANDS = 32; /** What a player's audio looks like (§3.11). */ /* ------------------------------------------------------------- decoding */ /** A nullable field: must be a string or null (missing reads as null). */ /** Copy optional key `k` only when present. */ const DEVICE_KINDS = ["web", "mobile", "desktop"] as const; const CAPS = ["player", "yt", "local", "lyrics", "viz"] as const; const REPEAT = ["off", "all", "one"] as const; const ACK_ERRORS = [ "offline", "not_a_player", "nothing_playable", "unsupported", "failed", "timeout", ] as const; const RPC_ERRORS = ["offline", "unsupported", "not_signed_in", "failed", "timeout"] as const; const RPC_METHODS = ["search", "suggest", "open", "artist", "library", "lyrics"] as const; const ITEM_KINDS = ["song", "video", "album", "playlist", "artist"] as const; /** Receivers ignore caps they don't know (§3.1): an unknown one is dropped, * never a reason to reject the frame. */ /** Decode any frame, or `null` when it doesn't match the contract. */ /** Run a decoder, returning `null` instead of throwing on a mismatch. */

nodes.body_text: type Obj = Record<string, unknown>;

nodes.name: Invalid
nodes.body_text: class Invalid extends Error {}

nodes.name: fail
nodes.body_text: function fail(at: string): never { throw new Invalid(at); }

nodes.name: obj
nodes.signature: function obj(v: unknown, at: string): Obj
nodes.body_text: function obj(v: unknown, at: string): Obj { return typeof v === "object" && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v) ? (v as Obj) : fail(at); }

nodes.name: str
nodes.signature: function str(o: Obj, k: string): string
nodes.body_text: function str(o: Obj, k: string): string { const v = o[k]; return typeof v === "string" ? v : fail(k); }

nodes.body_text: function strOrNull(o: Obj, k: string): string | null { const v = o[k]; if (v === null || v === undefined) return null; return typeof v === "string" ? v : fail(k); }

nodes.signature: function num(o: Obj, k: string): number
nodes.body_text: function num(o: Obj, k: string): number { const v = o[k]; return typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : fail(k); }

nodes.name: numOrNull
nodes.signature: function numOrNull(o: Obj, k: string): number | null
nodes.body_text: function numOrNull(o: Obj, k: string): number | null { const v = o[k]; if (v === null || v === undefined) return null; return typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : fail(k); }

nodes.name: bool
nodes.signature: function bool(o: Obj, k: string): boolean
nodes.body_text: function bool(o: Obj, k: string): boolean { const v = o[k]; return typeof v === "boolean" ? v : fail(k); }

nodes.name: oneOf
nodes.signature: function oneOf<T extends string>(v: unknown, allowed: readonly T[], at: string): T
nodes.body_text: function oneOf<T extends string>(v: unknown, allowed: readonly T[], at: string): T { return typeof v === "string" && (allowed as readonly string[]).includes(v) ? (v as T) : fail(at); }

nodes.signature: function list<T>(v: unknown, at: string, each: (x: unknown) => T): T[]
nodes.body_text: function list<T>(v: unknown, at: string, each: (x: unknown) => T): T[] { return Array.isArray(v) ? v.map(each) : fail(at); }

nodes.name: opt
nodes.signature: function opt<T>(o: Obj, k: string, read: (o: Obj, k: string) => T): Partial<Record<string, T>>
nodes.body_text: function opt<T>(o: Obj, k: string, read: (o: Obj, k: string) => T): Partial<Record<string, T>> { return o[k] === undefined ? {} : { [k]: read(o, k) }; }

nodes.name: caps
nodes.body_text: function caps(v: unknown): Cap[] { return list(v, "caps", (c) => (CAPS as readonly unknown[]).includes(c) ? (c as Cap) : null).filter( (c): c is Cap => c !== null, ); }

nodes.name: decodeDeviceInfo
nodes.body_text: function decodeDeviceInfo(v: unknown): DeviceInfo { const o = obj(v, "device"); return { id: str(o, "id"), kind: oneOf(o.kind, DEVICE_KINDS, "kind"), name: str(o, "name"), platform: strOrNull(o, "platform"), appVersion: strOrNull(o, "appVersion"), caps: caps(o.caps), online: bool(o, "online"), lastSeenAt: str(o, "lastSeenAt"), }; }

nodes.name: decodeDeviceHello
nodes.body_text: function decodeDeviceHello(v: unknown): DeviceHello { const o = obj(v, "device"); return { id: str(o, "id"), kind: oneOf(o.kind, DEVICE_KINDS, "kind"), name: str(o, "name"), platform: str(o, "platform"), appVersion: str(o, "appVersion"), caps: caps(o.caps), }; }

nodes.name: decodeTrackRef
nodes.body_text: function decodeTrackRef(v: unknown): TrackRef { const o = obj(v, "track"); const common = { title: str(o, "title"), artist: strOrNull(o, "artist"), album: strOrNull(o, "album"), durationMs: numOrNull(o, "durationMs"), }; switch (o.src) { case "yt": return { src: "yt", videoId: str(o, "videoId"), ...common, artUrl: strOrNull(o, "artUrl") }; case "local": return { src: "local", deviceId: str(o, "deviceId"), id: str(o, "id"), ...common, artUrl: null }; case "other": return { src: "other", ...common, artUrl: strOrNull(o, "artUrl") }; default: return fail("src"); } }

nodes.name: decodeCommand
nodes.body_text: function decodeCommand(v: unknown): Command { const o = obj(v, "cmd"); const items = () => list(o.items, "items", decodeTrackRef); switch (o.type) { case "play": return { type: "play", items: items(), index: num(o, "index"), ...(opt(o, "positionMs", num) as { positionMs?: number }), ...(opt(o, "radio", bool) as { radio?: boolean }), }; case "enqueue": return { type: "enqueue", items: items(), mode: oneOf(o.mode, ["next", "end"] as const, "mode") }; case "pause": case "resume": case "stop": case "next": case "prev": return { type: o.type }; case "seek": return { type: "seek", positionMs: num(o, "positionMs") }; case "jump": return { type: "jump", uid: str(o, "uid") }; case "volume": return { type: "volume", value: num(o, "value") }; case "shuffle": return { type: "shuffle", on: bool(o, "on") }; case "repeat": return { type: "repeat", mode: oneOf(o.mode, REPEAT, "mode") }; default: return fail("type"); } }

nodes.name: items
nodes.body_text: items = () => list(o.items, "items", decodeTrackRef)

nodes.name: decodePlayerState
nodes.body_text: function decodePlayerState(v: unknown): PlayerState { const o = obj(v, "state"); return { seq: num(o, "seq"), track: o.track === null || o.track === undefined ? null : decodeTrackRef(o.track), playing: bool(o, "playing"), positionMs: num(o, "positionMs"), durationMs: numOrNull(o, "durationMs"), volume: num(o, "volume"), shuffle: bool(o, "shuffle"), repeat: oneOf(o.repeat, REPEAT, "repeat"), queue: list(o.queue, "queue", (q) => { const e = obj(q, "queue[]"); return { uid: str(e, "uid"), track: decodeTrackRef(e.track) }; }), ...(opt(o, "at", num) as { at?: number }), }; }

nodes.name: decodeItem
nodes.body_text: function decodeItem(v: unknown): Item { const o = obj(v, "item"); return { kind: oneOf(o.kind, ITEM_KINDS, "kind"), id: str(o, "id"), title: str(o, "title"), subtitle: strOrNull(o, "subtitle"), thumbnail: strOrNull(o, "thumbnail"), artist: strOrNull(o, "artist"), album: strOrNull(o, "album"), durationMs: numOrNull(o, "durationMs"), hasVideo: bool(o, "hasVideo"), }; }

nodes.name: decodeVizFrame
nodes.body_text: function decodeVizFrame(v: unknown): VizFrame { const o = obj(v, "frame"); const bands = list(o.bands, "bands", (b) => typeof b === "number" && Number.isFinite(b) ? b : fail("bands[]"), ); if (bands.length !== VIZ_BANDS) fail("bands"); return { heardAt: num(o, "heardAt"), positionMs: num(o, "positionMs"), bands, level: num(o, "level"), beat: num(o, "beat"), }; }

nodes.name: route
nodes.signature: function route(o: Obj): { to?: string; from?: string }
nodes.body_text: function route(o: Obj): { to?: string; from?: string } { return { ...(opt(o, "to", str) as { to?: string }), ...(opt(o, "from", str) as { from?: string }) }; }

nodes.name: decodeFrameStrict
