nodes.body_text: import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; import { BassBeat, type BassHit, MIN_STRENGTH } from "./bassBeat"; const DT = 1 / 30; /** Feed `dbs` one per frame; returns [frame index, hit] for every report. */ describe("BassBeat", () => { it("is quiet on a steady bass line", () => { expect(run(new BassBeat(), steady(-30, 120))).toEqual([]); }); it("fires on a sharp rise out of a settled level, on the frame it happens", () => { const hits = run(new BassBeat(), [...steady(-30, 30), -16, -16, -16]); expect(hits).toHaveLength(1); const [frame, hit] = hits[0]!; expect(frame).toBe(30); expect(hit.onset).toBe(true); expect(hit.strength).toBeGreaterThan(MIN_STRENGTH); expect(hit.strength).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1); expect(hit.gain).toBe(hit.strength); }); it("is silent through the warm-up after a reset (the baseline starts from nothing)", () => { expect(run(new BassBeat(), [-60, -20, -20, -20])).toEqual([]); }); it("ignores a rise that is slow, even if it climbs far", () => { const swell = Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) => -40 + i * 0.5); // +0.5 dB / frame expect(run(new BassBeat(), [...steady(-40, 20), ...swell])).toEqual([]); }); it("ignores a rise that stays under the absolute floor", () => { expect(run(new BassBeat(), [...steady(-75, 30), -62, -62])).toEqual([]); }); it("ignores a hit far quieter than the song's recent loudest bass", () => { // 30 dB of headroom below a loud passage: a 4 dB bump there is not a hit. const frames = [...steady(-10, 15), ...steady(-40, 30), -34, -34]; expect(run(new BassBeat(), frames).filter(([i]) => i >= 45)).toEqual([]); }); it("tops a hit up while its attack keeps rising, then reports nothing more", () => { // A loud passage first, so the hit is judged against a higher recent peak // (a hit that sets its own peak is already at full strength). const hits = run(new BassBeat(), [...steady(-20, 15), ...steady(-42, 40), -34, -30, -30, -30]); expect(hits[0]![1].onset).toBe(true); const top = hits.find(([, h]) => !h.onset); expect(top, "the rising second frame tops the hit up").toBeDefined(); expect(top![1].gain).toBeGreaterThan(0); expect(top![1].strength).toBeGreaterThan(hits[0]![1].strength); expect(hits).toHaveLength(2); }); it("does not fire twice inside the refractory period, even out of a deep notch", () => { // Hit, a deep notch (so the baseline falls and the second rise is huge), // then another rise 66 ms after the first. const frames = [...steady(-30, 30), -18, -45, -18, -18]; const onsets = run(new BassBeat(), frames).filter(([, h]) => h.onset); expect(onsets.map(([i]) => i)).toEqual([30]); }); it("fires again once the refractory period has passed", () => { const frames = [...steady(-30, 30), -18, ...steady(-45, 6), -18, -18]; const onsets = run(new BassBeat(), frames).filter(([, h]) => h.onset); expect(onsets.map(([i]) => i)).toEqual([30, 37]); }); it("does not re-arm on a hit's own tail (the baseline starts just under its peak)", () => { // After a hit the level settles a few dB lower and wobbles: not new hits. const frames = [...steady(-30, 30), -16, -19, -22, -19, -22, -19, -22, -19]; const onsets = run(new BassBeat(), frames).filter(([, h]) => h.onset); expect(onsets).toHaveLength(1); }); it("forgets the song on reset()", () => { const beat = new BassBeat(); run(beat, [...steady(-30, 30), -16]); beat.reset(); // Straight after a reset the same jump is inside the warm-up: no hit. expect(run(beat, [-30, -30, -16])).toEqual([]); // …and a settled level followed by a jump fires again. expect(run(beat, [...steady(-30, 30), -16]).filter(([, h]) => h.onset)).toHaveLength(1); }); it("survives junk input", () => { const beat = new BassBeat(); expect(beat.step(Number.NaN, DT)).toBeNull(); expect(beat.step(Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY, Number.NaN)).toBeNull(); expect(beat.step(-30, -1)).toBeNull(); }); });

nodes.name: run
nodes.signature: function run(beat: BassBeat, dbs: number[], dt = DT): Array<[number, BassHit]>
nodes.body_text: function run(beat: BassBeat, dbs: number[], dt = DT): Array<[number, BassHit]> { const out: Array<[number, BassHit]> = []; dbs.forEach((db, i) => { const hit = beat.step(db, dt); if (hit) out.push([i, hit]); }); return out; }

nodes.name: steady
nodes.body_text: steady = (db: number, n: number) => new Array<number>(n).fill(db)

nodes.name: bassBeat.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Bass-hit detection from the engine's spectrum: a kick, an 808, a log drum — * whatever lands in the low end with an attack. A port of the phone's * `BassBeat` (`hype/lib/visualizers/bass_beat.dart`) to a frame rate of ~30 Hz. * * # Why not `lib/beat.ts` * * `stepBeat` watches the whole mix's level and fires at 1.45x its running * average. A mastered song barely moves its full-band level between kicks, so * on the phone that detector answered only 21-53% of the bass hits (and pulsed * on snares and vocal stabs). This listens to the band below ~150 Hz only, in * decibels, where "a hit" is a rise of a few dB whatever the loudness. * * # How a hit is told from everything else * * - **It rises sharply** — at least {@link FAST_RISE_DB} over the lowest of the * last {@link FAST_FRAMES} frames. * - **It clears where the bass was** — at least {@link RISE_DB} over a baseline * trailing the level by ~{@link BASE_TAU} s (a kick's tail cancelling the * bassline recovers fast but only back to the baseline). * - **It is loud for this song** — within {@link GATE_DB} of the loudest bass * of the last few seconds, and above an absolute floor. * - **It is not the same hit** — {@link REFRACTORY} s apart; once a hit fires * the baseline starts just under its peak so its own tail can't re-arm. * * It fires the moment the threshold is crossed and is *topped up* while the * attack keeps rising (up to {@link ATTACK_WINDOW} s): the picture can move * with the sound instead of ~30 ms after it. */ /** Frames the "sharp rise" looks back over. The engine's FFT window (43 ms) * already smears an attack across two frames, so two, not the phone's ~17 ms. */ export const FAST_FRAMES = 2; export const FAST_RISE_DB = 3.0; export const RISE_DB = 3.5; export const GATE_DB = 22.0; export const FLOOR_DB = -58.0; /** Strength spans this many dB below the recent loudest bass. */ export const RANGE_DB = 14.0; /** Below this a hit would barely move anything: noise, not a beat. */ export const MIN_STRENGTH = 0.15; export const REFRACTORY = 0.11; export const ATTACK_WINDOW = 0.04; export const BASE_TAU = 0.09; export const SETTLE_DB = 3.0; /** How fast "the loudest bass lately" forgets, so a quiet verse after a loud * drop still gets full-strength hits within a few seconds. */ export const PEAK_RELEASE_DB_PER_S = 3.0; /** Frames since a reset before a hit may fire (the baseline starts from nothing). */ const WARMUP_FRAMES = 4;

nodes.name: BassHit
nodes.body_text: interface BassHit { /** 0..1 against the song's recent loudest bass. */ strength: number; /** What this report adds: the whole strength when the hit starts, the increase after. */ gain: number; /** Whether this starts a hit (rather than topping one up). */ onset: boolean; }

nodes.name: BassBeat
nodes.body_text: class BassBeat { private recent: number[] = []; private base: number | null = null; private peak = -120; private clock = 0; private lastOnset = -1e9; private seen = 0; private openAt: number | null = null; private openBest = 0; private openReported = 0; /** Feed one frame's bass level (dBFS) `dt` seconds after the previous one; * returns the hit it holds, if any. */ step(db: number, dt: number): BassHit | null { const level = Number.isFinite(db) ? db : -120; const hop = Number.isFinite(dt) ? Math.max(0, dt) : 0; this.seen += 1; let lowest = level; if (this.recent.length > 0) lowest = Math.min(...this.recent); const fastRise = this.recent.length > 0 ? level - lowest : 0; this.recent.push(level); if (this.recent.length > FAST_FRAMES) this.recent.shift(); this.clock += hop; if (this.base === null) this.base = level; this.peak = level > this.peak ? level : Math.max(level, this.peak - PEAK_RELEASE_DB_PER_S * hop); let out: BassHit | null = null; if (this.openAt !== null) { if (level > this.openBest && this.clock - this.openAt <= ATTACK_WINDOW) { this.openBest = level; const s = this.strengthOf(level); if (s > this.openReported) { out = { strength: s, gain: s - this.openReported, onset: false }; this.openReported = s; } } else { this.openAt = null; this.base = Math.max(this.base, this.openBest - SETTLE_DB); } } if ( this.openAt === null && out === null && level - this.base > RISE_DB && fastRise >= FAST_RISE_DB && level > this.peak - GATE_DB && level > FLOOR_DB && this.seen > WARMUP_FRAMES && this.clock - this.lastOnset > REFRACTORY ) { const s = this.strengthOf(level); if (s >= MIN_STRENGTH) { this.openAt = this.clock; this.openBest = level; this.openReported = s; this.lastOnset = this.clock; out = { strength: s, gain: s, onset: true }; } } if (this.openAt === null) { this.base += (level - this.base) * (1 - Math.exp(-hop / BASE_TAU)); } return out; } /** Forget the song: a new track or a restart begins from nothing. */ reset(): void { this.recent = []; this.base = null; this.peak = -120; this.clock = 0; this.lastOnset = -1e9; this.seen = 0; this.openAt = null; this.openBest = 0; this.openReported = 0; } private strengthOf(db: number): number { return Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (db - (this.peak - RANGE_DB)) / RANGE_DB)); } }

Math.max(0, dt) : 0; this.seen += 1; let lowest = level; if (this.recent.length > 0) lowest = Math.min(...this.recent); const fastRise = this.recent.length > 0 ? level - lowest : 0; this.recent.push(level); if (this.recent.length > FAST_FRAMES) this.recent.shift(); this.clock += hop; if (this.base === null) this.base = level; this.peak = level > this.peak ? level : Math.max(level, this.peak - PEAK_RELEASE_DB_PER_S * hop); let out: BassHit | null = null; if (this.openAt !== null) { if (level > this.openBest && this.clock - this.openAt <= ATTACK_WINDOW) { this.openBest = level; const s = this.strengthOf(level); if (s > this.openReported) { out = { strength: s, gain: s - this.openReported, onset: false }; this.openReported = s; } } else { this.openAt = null; this.base = Math.max(this.base, this.openBest - SETTLE_DB); } } if ( this.openAt === null && out === null && level - this.base > RISE_DB && fastRise >= FAST_RISE_DB && level > this.peak - GATE_DB && level > FLOOR_DB && this.seen > WARMUP_FRAMES && this.clock - this.lastOnset > REFRACTORY ) { const s = this.strengthOf(level); if (s >= MIN_STRENGTH) { this.openAt = this.clock; this.openBest = level; this.openReported = s; this.lastOnset = this.clock; out = { strength: s, gain: s, onset: true }; } } if (this.openAt === null) { this.base += (level - this.base) * (1 - Math.exp(-hop / BASE_TAU)); } return out; }

nodes.name: reset
nodes.body_text: reset(): void { this.recent = []; this.base = null; this.peak = -120; this.clock = 0; this.lastOnset = -1e9; this.seen = 0; this.openAt = null; this.openBest = 0; this.openReported = 0; }

nodes.name: strengthOf
nodes.body_text: private strengthOf(db: number): number { return Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (db - (this.peak - RANGE_DB)) / RANGE_DB)); }

nodes.body_text: import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; import { PositionExtrapolator } from "./position"; describe("PositionExtrapolator", () => { it("advances the last report by the time since it, while running", () => { const p = new PositionExtrapolator(); p.sync(61_400, 1000, true); expect(p.positionAt(1000)).toBe(61_400); expect(p.positionAt(1060)).toBe(61_460); }); it("holds still while paused or buffering", () => { const p = new PositionExtrapolator(); p.sync(5000, 1000, false); expect(p.positionAt(9000)).toBe(5000); }); it("never runs backwards if the clock reading precedes the report", () => { const p = new PositionExtrapolator(); p.sync(5000, 1000, true); expect(p.positionAt(900)).toBe(5000); }); it("re-anchors on every report and tolerates junk", () => { const p = new PositionExtrapolator(); p.sync(1000, 0, true); p.sync(2000, 500, true); expect(p.positionAt(600)).toBe(2100); p.sync(Number.NaN, 0, true); expect(p.positionAt(0)).toBe(0); p.sync(-50, 0, false); expect(p.positionAt(10)).toBe(0); }); });

nodes.name: position.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Playback position between the engine's progress events (~10/s): the last * reported position, advanced by the time since it was reported while playing. */

nodes.name: PositionExtrapolator
nodes.body_text: class PositionExtrapolator { private posMs = 0; private at = 0; private running = false; /** The engine reported `posMs` at local time `atMs`. `running`: the position * is advancing (playing, not paused, not buffering). */ sync(posMs: number, atMs: number, running: boolean): void { this.posMs = Number.isFinite(posMs) ? Math.max(0, posMs) : 0; this.at = atMs; this.running = running; } positionAt(nowMs: number): number { return this.running ? this.posMs + Math.max(0, nowMs - this.at) : this.posMs; } }

nodes.name: sync
nodes.signature: sync(posMs: number, atMs: number, running: boolean): void
nodes.body_text: sync(posMs: number, atMs: number, running: boolean): void { this.posMs = Number.isFinite(posMs) ? Math.max(0, posMs) : 0; this.at = atMs; this.running = running; }

nodes.name: positionAt
nodes.body_text: positionAt(nowMs: number): number { return this.running ? this.posMs + Math.max(0, nowMs - this.at) : this.posMs; }

nodes.name: streamer.test.ts
nodes.body_text: import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"; import type { VizFrame } from "../protocol"; import { SOURCE_BANDS } from "./bands"; import { VizStreamer, type VizDeps, type VizOptions } from "./streamer"; /** A bass-heavy spectrum: the lowest bands loud. */ describe("lifecycle: stream only while subscribed AND online AND playing", () => { it("does nothing until all three hold", () => { const r = rig(); r.s.setOnline(true); expect(r.listen).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); // online + playing, nobody watching r.s.setSubscribed(true); expect(r.listen).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); expect(r.s.isStreaming).toBe(true); }); it("does not start while paused, and starts when playback does", () => { const r = rig(); r.setPlaying(false); r.s.setOnline(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); expect(r.listen).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); r.setPlaying(true); r.s.refresh(); expect(r.listen).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); }); it("releases the listener when playback pauses", () => { const r = rig(); r.s.setOnline(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); r.setPlaying(false); r.s.refresh(); expect(r.stop).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); expect(r.s.isStreaming).toBe(false); r.setPlaying(true); r.s.refresh(); expect(r.listen).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2); }); it("releases it on viz_sub off", () => { const r = rig(); r.s.setOnline(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); r.s.setSubscribed(false); expect(r.stop).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); }); it("releases it on disconnect, and a subscription does not survive its socket", () => { const r = rig(); r.s.setOnline(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); r.s.setOnline(false); expect(r.stop).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); r.s.setOnline(true); // reconnected: nothing until the hub says viz_sub on again expect(r.listen).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); r.s.setSubscribed(true); expect(r.listen).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2); }); it("ignores a viz_sub on that arrives with no socket up", () => { const r = rig(); r.s.setSubscribed(true); r.s.setOnline(true); expect(r.listen).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); it("does not stack listeners on repeated refreshes or repeated subscribes", () => { const r = rig(); r.s.setOnline(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); r.s.refresh(); r.s.refresh(); expect(r.listen).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); }); it("dispose() releases everything", () => { const r = rig(); r.s.setOnline(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); r.s.dispose(); expect(r.stop).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); r.s.refresh(); expect(r.listen).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); }); }); describe("frame content", () => { it("sends the contract's shape", () => { const r = streaming(); r.feed(quiet()); const f = r.sent[0]!.frame; expect(f.bands).toHaveLength(32); expect(f.bands.every((b) => b >= 0 && b <= 1)).toBe(true); expect(f.level).toBe(0.5); expect(f.beat).toBe(0); expect(JSON.stringify({ t: "viz", frame: f }).length).toBeLessThan(1024); }); it("stamps heardAt in HUB time and positionMs from the playback position", () => { const r = streaming(); r.setHubOffset(5_000_000); r.setPosition(61_400); r.feed(quiet()); expect(r.sent[0]!.frame.heardAt).toBe(r.now() + 5_000_000); expect(r.sent[0]!.frame.positionMs).toBe(61_400); }); it("adds the output latency to both: the audio is heard that much later", () => { const r = streaming(); r.setLatency(200); r.setHubOffset(1000); r.feed(quiet()); expect(r.sent[0]!.frame.heardAt).toBe(r.now() + 1000 + 200); expect(r.sent[0]!.frame.positionMs).toBe(61_400 + 200); }); it("follows the hub clock as it is re-measured", () => { const r = streaming(); r.feed(quiet()); r.advance(60); r.setHubOffset(1_000_250); r.feed(quiet()); const [a, b] = r.sent.map((x) => x.frame.heardAt - x.at); expect(a).toBe(1_000_000); expect(b).toBe(1_000_250); }); it("never sends a negative latency or position", () => { const r = streaming(); r.setLatency(-500); r.setPosition(-20); r.feed(quiet()); expect(r.sent[0]!.frame.positionMs).toBe(0); expect(r.sent[0]!.frame.heardAt).toBe(r.now() + 1_000_000); }); it("stays quiet once playback stops even if a frame is already in flight", () => { const r = streaming(); r.setPlaying(false); r.feed(quiet()); expect(r.sent).toHaveLength(0); }); }); describe("throttle", () => { it("runs at ~20 fps from ~31 fps engine frames, never closer than the minimum gap", () => { const r = streaming(); r.stream(2000); expect(r.sent.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(38); expect(r.sent.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(42); for (let i = 1; i < r.sent.length; i++) { expect(r.sent[i]!.at - r.sent[i - 1]!.at).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(25); } }); it("never exceeds the hub's 30/s in any sliding second, however fast frames arrive", () => { const r = streaming({ intervalMs: 1, minGapMs: 0, maxPerSecond: 30 }); r.stream(3000, 5); // 200 engine frames a second const times = r.sent.map((x) => x.at); for (let i = 0; i < times.length; i++) { const inWindow = times.filter((t) => t >= times[i]! && t < times[i]! + 1000).length; expect(inWindow).toBeLessThanOrEqual(30); } expect(times.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(85); // and it does use the budget }); it("holds a custom per-second cap exactly", () => { const r = streaming({ intervalMs: 1, minGapMs: 0, maxPerSecond: 5 }); r.stream(900, 10); expect(r.sent).toHaveLength(5); }); it("a restart sends at once even right after the last frame (the old schedule is forgotten)", () => { const r = streaming(); r.stream(500); r.advance(100); r.feed(quiet()); // due: goes out const before = r.sent.length; r.advance(5); // 5 ms after a send is inside the minimum gap… r.setPlaying(false); r.s.refresh(); r.setPlaying(true); r.s.refresh(); r.feed(quiet()); // …but a fresh stream owes nothing to the last one expect(r.sent.length).toBe(before + 1); }); it("restarts the schedule cleanly after a stop and start", () => { const r = streaming(); r.stream(500); const before = r.sent.length; r.setPlaying(false); r.s.refresh(); r.advance(5000); r.setPlaying(true); r.s.refresh(); r.feed(quiet()); expect(r.sent.length).toBe(before + 1); }); }); describe("beat", () => { /** Settles on a quiet bass line for ~1 s, returning the next-frame time. */ /** Settle, send one regular frame, then wait `after` ms. */ it("sends a bass onset at once instead of waiting for the next slot", () => { // 100 ms interval, 30 ms after a send: a regular frame is not due… const control = justSent({ intervalMs: 100 }, 30); const before = control.sent.length; control.feed(quiet()); expect(control.sent.length, "no onset: waits for its slot").toBe(before); // …but a kick at the same moment goes out immediately. const r = justSent({ intervalMs: 100 }, 30); const count = r.sent.length; r.feed(kick()); expect(r.sent.length).toBe(count + 1); expect(r.sent.at(-1)!.frame.beat).toBeGreaterThan(0); }); it("carries an onset that falls inside the minimum gap to the next frame it sends", () => { const r = justSent({}, 10); // 10 ms after a send: inside the 25 ms gap const count = r.sent.length; r.feed(kick()); expect(r.sent.length, "too soon to send").toBe(count); r.advance(40); r.feed(kick()); expect(r.sent.length).toBe(count + 1); expect(r.sent.at(-1)!.frame.beat).toBeGreaterThan(0); }); it("reports beat 0 on frames without an onset, and clears it once sent", () => { const r = settled(); r.advance(50); r.feed(kick()); r.advance(60); r.feed(kick()); // the kick is sustained, not a new onset expect(r.sent.at(-1)!.frame.beat).toBe(0); }); it("never reports a beat outside 0..1", () => { const r = settled(); r.advance(50); r.feed(kick()); for (const { frame } of r.sent) { expect(frame.beat).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0); expect(frame.beat).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1); } }); it("starts the detector over when the track changes", () => { const r = settled(); r.s.resetAnalysis(); r.advance(50); const count = r.sent.length; r.feed(kick()); // inside the warm-up after a reset: not a beat expect(r.sent.at(-1)!.frame.beat).toBe(0); expect(r.sent.length).toBe(count + 1); }); }); describe("failures", () => { it("a rejected send does not throw or stop the stream", async () => { const r = streaming(); r.send.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error("offline")); expect(() => r.stream(300)).not.toThrow(); await Promise.resolve(); expect(r.send.mock.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(1); expect(r.s.isStreaming).toBe(true); }); });

nodes.name: quiet
nodes.body_text: quiet = () => new Array<number>(SOURCE_BANDS).fill(0.5)

nodes.name: rig
nodes.body_text: function rig(options: Partial<VizOptions> = {}) { let now = 10_000; let playing = true; let latency = 0; let position = 61_400; let hubOffset = 1_000_000; const sent: Array<{ at: number; frame: VizFrame }> = []; let onSpectrum: ((s: readonly number[]) => void) | null = null; const listen = vi.fn((cb: (s: readonly number[]) => void) => { onSpectrum = cb; return stop; }); const stop = vi.fn(() => { onSpectrum = null; }); const send = vi.fn(async (frame: VizFrame) => void sent.push({ at: now, frame })); const deps: VizDeps = { listen, send, isPlaying: () => playing, positionMs: () => position, hubNowMs: () => now + hubOffset, nowMs: () => now, outputLatencyMs: () => latency, }; const s = new VizStreamer(deps, options); const feed = (spectrum: readonly number[]) => onSpectrum?.(spectrum); /** Frames every `stepMs` for `totalMs` of the given spectrum. */ const stream = (totalMs: number, stepMs = 32, spectrum: () => readonly number[] = quiet) => { const end = now + totalMs; while (now < end) { feed(spectrum()); now += stepMs; } }; return { s, sent, listen, stop, send, feed, stream, advance: (ms: number) => (now += ms), now: () => now, setPlaying: (p: boolean) => (playing = p), setLatency: (l: number) => (latency = l), setPosition: (p: number) => (position = p), setHubOffset: (o: number) => (hubOffset = o), isListening: () => onSpectrum !== null, }; }

nodes.name: feed
nodes.body_text: feed = (spectrum: readonly number[]) => onSpectrum?.(spectrum)

nodes.name: stream
nodes.signature: stream = (totalMs: number, stepMs = 32, spectrum: () => readonly number[] = quiet)
nodes.body_text: stream = (totalMs: number, stepMs = 32, spectrum: () => readonly number[] = quiet) => { const end = now + totalMs; while (now < end) { feed(spectrum()); now += stepMs; } }

nodes.name: streaming
nodes.body_text: function streaming(options: Partial<VizOptions> = {}) { const r = rig(options); r.s.setOnline(true); r.s.setSubscribed(true); return r; }

nodes.name: settled
nodes.body_text: function settled() { const r = streaming(); r.stream(1000); return r; }

nodes.name: justSent
nodes.body_text: function justSent(options: Partial<VizOptions>, after: number) { const r = streaming(options); r.stream(1000); r.advance(200); r.feed(quiet()); // due: goes out r.advance(after); return r; }

nodes.name: streamer.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * The visualiser stream (§3.11, v1.1): what this desktop's audio looks like, * sent to a browser that draws it, on the beat. The shape follows the phone's * `ConnectVizStreamer` (`hype/lib/services/connect/connect_viz.dart`). * * # Only while somebody is watching, and only while it plays * * The engine's frames (~30/s of IPC, plus the re-binning and the beat * detector here) are listened to exactly while all of these hold, and released * the moment one stops: * * - a controller subscribed (`viz_sub on:true` from the hub), * - the socket is online (a subscription belongs to a socket; the hub repeats * it after the next `welcome`), and * - music is playing (a paused player sends nothing). * * # Frame rate * * A frame goes out every {@link VizOptions.intervalMs} (50 ms = 20 fps), never * closer than `minGapMs`, and never more than `maxPerSecond` in any sliding * second (the hub drops the excess silently, and the Rust client refuses it). * A bass onset that lands between two slots is sent at once (still honouring * the gap) instead of up to 50 ms late — the point is to be on the beat. * * # Timing * * `heardAt` is when the frame's audio reaches the listener, in the HUB's clock: * the hub time now plus the output latency. The engine's frame describes the * block it is writing to the output right now and exposes no device latency, so * the latency is 0 (a Bluetooth sink will look that much early). `positionMs` * is the playback position of that audio. */ import type { VizFrame } from "../protocol"; import { BassBeat } from "./bassBeat"; import { bassDb, clamp01, rebinBands, round2, vizLevel } from "./bands"; export const DEFAULT_VIZ_OPTIONS: VizOptions = { intervalMs: 50, minGapMs: 25, maxPerSecond: 30 }; /** Frames closer than this are one stall's worth of jitter, further apart are a * pause; the beat detector's clock is clamped to this range. */ const MIN_DT_S = 0.005; const MAX_DT_S = 0.1;

nodes.name: VizOptions
nodes.body_text: interface VizOptions { /** Target spacing of frames. */ intervalMs: number; /** Hard floor on spacing between two frames. */ minGapMs: number; /** The hub drops frames beyond this many per second. */ maxPerSecond: number; }

nodes.name: VizDeps
nodes.body_text: interface VizDeps { /** Start receiving engine spectra; returns the stop function. Only called * while streaming is wanted. */ listen(onSpectrum: (spectrum: readonly number[]) => void): () => void; /** Queue a frame for the hub; rejection means it didn't go. */ send(frame: VizFrame): Promise<void>; isPlaying(): boolean; /** Playback position now, ms. */ positionMs(): number; /** The hub's epoch ms now. */ hubNowMs(): number; /** Monotonic ms. */ nowMs(): number; /** Delay between the engine frame and the sound (0 when unknown). */ outputLatencyMs?(): number; }

nodes.name: VizStreamer
nodes.body_text: class VizStreamer { private subscribed = false; private online = false; private stop: (() => void) | null = null; private readonly bass = new BassBeat(); private lastFrameAt: number | null = null; private lastSentAt = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY; private dueAt = 0; private pendingBeat = 0; private recentSends: number[] = []; private readonly options: VizOptions; constructor( private readonly deps: VizDeps, options: Partial<VizOptions> = {}, ) { this.options = { ...DEFAULT_VIZ_OPTIONS, ...options }; } /** Whether engine frames are being listened to. */ get isStreaming(): boolean { return this.stop !== null; } /** A controller started (`true`) or stopped (`false`) watching. */ setSubscribed(on: boolean): void { // A subscription belongs to a socket: one arriving with none up is stale, // and the hub repeats it after the next `welcome` anyway. this.subscribed = on && this.online; this.refresh(); } /** The socket came up or went away. A subscription does not survive it. */ setOnline(online: boolean): void { this.online = online; if (!online) this.subscribed = false; this.refresh(); } /** Re-reads whether anything is playing; call when playback changes. */ refresh(): void { const wanted = this.subscribed && this.online && this.deps.isPlaying(); if (wanted && this.stop === null) { this.resetAnalysis(); this.recentSends = []; this.lastSentAt = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY; this.dueAt = 0; this.stop = this.deps.listen((spectrum) => this.onSpectrum(spectrum)); } else if (!wanted && this.stop !== null) { const stop = this.stop; this.stop = null; stop(); } } /** A new track (or a seek) begins: the beat detector forgets the last song. */ resetAnalysis(): void { this.bass.reset(); this.pendingBeat = 0; this.lastFrameAt = null; } dispose(): void { this.subscribed = false; this.online = false; this.refresh(); } private onSpectrum(spectrum: readonly number[]): void { const now = this.deps.nowMs(); // Every frame feeds the detector, sent or not: it needs a continuous // signal, and a hit in a skipped frame is carried to the next one sent. const dt = this.lastFrameAt === null ? MAX_DT_S : Math.min(MAX_DT_S, Math.max(MIN_DT_S, (now - this.lastFrameAt) / 1000)); this.lastFrameAt = now; const hit = this.bass.step(bassDb(spectrum), dt); if (hit && hit.strength > this.pendingBeat) this.pendingBeat = hit.strength; const onset = hit?.onset === true; const { intervalMs, minGapMs, maxPerSecond } = this.options; if (now - this.lastSentAt < minGapMs) return; this.recentSends = this.recentSends.filter((t) => now - t < 1000); if (this.recentSends.length >= maxPerSecond) return; const due = now >= this.dueAt; if (!due && !onset) return; if (!this.deps.isPlaying()) return; const latency = Math.max(0, this.deps.outputLatencyMs?.() ?? 0); const frame: VizFrame = { heardAt: Math.round(this.deps.hubNowMs() + latency), positionMs: Math.max(0, Math.round(this.deps.positionMs() + latency)), bands: rebinBands(spectrum), level: vizLevel(spectrum), beat: round2(clamp01(this.pendingBeat)), }; this.deps.send(frame).catch(() => {}); this.pendingBeat = 0; this.lastSentAt = now; this.recentSends.push(now); if (due) { // Keep the cadence rather than drifting by each arrival's jitter (so // ~31 engine frames a second still yield 20 a second); after a stall do // not try to catch up. An early onset leaves the schedule be. const next = this.dueAt + intervalMs; this.dueAt = next > now ? next : now + intervalMs; } } }

nodes.name: constructor
nodes.signature: constructor( private readonly deps: VizDeps, options: Partial<VizOptions> = {}, )
nodes.body_text: constructor( private readonly deps: VizDeps, options: Partial<VizOptions> = {}, ) { this.options = { ...DEFAULT_VIZ_OPTIONS, ...options }; }

nodes.name: isStreaming
nodes.body_text: get isStreaming(): boolean { return this.stop !== null; }

nodes.name: setSubscribed
nodes.body_text: setSubscribed(on: boolean): void { // A subscription belongs to a socket: one arriving with none up is stale, // and the hub repeats it after the next `welcome` anyway. this.subscribed = on && this.online; this.refresh(); }

nodes.name: setOnline
nodes.body_text: setOnline(online: boolean): void { this.online = online; if (!online) this.subscribed = false; this.refresh(); }

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.body_text: refresh(): void { const wanted = this.subscribed && this.online && this.deps.isPlaying(); if (wanted && this.stop === null) { this.resetAnalysis(); this.recentSends = []; this.lastSentAt = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY; this.dueAt = 0; this.stop = this.deps.listen((spectrum) => this.onSpectrum(spectrum)); } else if (!wanted && this.stop !== null) { const stop = this.stop; this.stop = null; stop(); } }

nodes.name: resetAnalysis
nodes.body_text: resetAnalysis(): void { this.bass.reset(); this.pendingBeat = 0; this.lastFrameAt = null; }

nodes.name: dispose
nodes.body_text: dispose(): void { this.subscribed = false; this.online = false; this.refresh(); }

MAX_DT_S : Math.min(MAX_DT_S, Math.max(MIN_DT_S, (now - this.lastFrameAt) / 1000)); this.lastFrameAt = now; const hit = this.bass.step(bassDb(spectrum), dt); if (hit && hit.strength > this.pendingBeat) this.pendingBeat = hit.strength; const onset = hit?.onset === true; const { intervalMs, minGapMs, maxPerSecond } = this.options; if (now - this.lastSentAt < minGapMs) return; this.recentSends = this.recentSends.filter((t) => now - t < 1000); if (this.recentSends.length >= maxPerSecond) return; const due = now >= this.dueAt; if (!due && !onset) return; if (!this.deps.isPlaying()) return; const latency = Math.max(0, this.deps.outputLatencyMs?.() ?? 0); const frame: VizFrame = { heardAt: Math.round(this.deps.hubNowMs() + latency), positionMs: Math.max(0, Math.round(this.deps.positionMs() + latency)), bands: rebinBands(spectrum), level: vizLevel(spectrum), beat: round2(clamp01(this.pendingBeat)), }; this.deps.send(frame).catch(() => {}); this.pendingBeat = 0; this.lastSentAt = now; this.recentSends.push(now); if (due) { // Keep the cadence rather than drifting by each arrival's jitter (so // ~31 engine frames a second still yield 20 a second); after a stall do // not try to catch up. An early onset leaves the schedule be. const next = this.dueAt + intervalMs; this.dueAt = next > now ? next : now + intervalMs; } }

Presets has no on/off state. */ /** * Turn `id` on or off: the exact calls (and premium gates, which only guard * turning ON) the cards have always made. nodes.body_text: interface EffectDescriptor { id: EffectId; /** Short label for the rack tile. */ label: string; /** Accessible name of the on/off switch (rack). */ switchLabel: string; icon: LucideIcon; /** DOM id of the card (Equalizer lives on its own view, so it has none). */ anchor: string; }

nodes.name: EffectToggle
nodes.body_text: interface EffectToggle extends EffectDescriptor { /** False for effects with no on/off state (Presets). */ hasSwitch: boolean; enabled: boolean; /** False when the effect cannot be switched on from here (Headphone). */ canToggleOn: boolean; toggle: (on: boolean) => void; }

nodes.name: enabledOf
nodes.signature: function enabledOf(id: EffectId, state: EngineState): boolean
nodes.body_text: function enabledOf(id: EffectId, state: EngineState): boolean { switch (id) { case "equalizer": return state.eq.enabled; case "presets": return false; case "bass": return state.bass.enabled; case "surround": return state.spatializer.enabled; case "surround3d": return state.surround3d.enabled; case "room": return state.room.enabled; case "convolver": return state.convolver.enabled; case "compander": return state.compander.enabled; case "saturation": return state.saturation.enabled; case "script": return state.script.enabled; case "headphone": return state.headphone.enabled; case "limiter": return state.output.limiterEnabled; } }

nodes.name: toggleEffect
nodes.signature: function toggleEffect(id: EffectId, on: boolean): void
nodes.body_text: function toggleEffect(id: EffectId, on: boolean): void { const s = useEngineStore.getState(); const st = s.state; switch (id) { case "equalizer": return s.setEqEnabled(on); case "presets": return; case "bass": return s.setBass(on, st.bass.amount, st.bass.harmonics, st.bass.adaptive); case "surround": return s.setSpatializer(on, st.spatializer.amount, st.spatializer.mode); case "surround3d": if (on && !requirePremium("SURROUND_3D")) return; return s.setSurround3d({ ...st.surround3d, enabled: on }); case "room": if (on && !requirePremium("ROOM_REVERB")) return; return s.setRoom({ ...st.room, enabled: on }); case "convolver": if (on && !requirePremium("CONVOLVER")) return; return s.setConvolver({ ...st.convolver, enabled: on }); case "compander": return s.setCompander({ ...st.compander, enabled: on }); case "saturation": return s.setSaturation({ ...st.saturation, enabled: on }); case "script": return s.setScriptEnabled(on); case "headphone": // A profile must be chosen to turn this on; the rack jumps to the card. if (!on) s.clearProfile(); return; case "limiter": return s.setOutput({ ...st.output, limiterEnabled: on }); } }

nodes.name: toggleFor
nodes.signature: function toggleFor(descriptor: EffectDescriptor, enabled: boolean): EffectToggle
nodes.body_text: function toggleFor(descriptor: EffectDescriptor, enabled: boolean): EffectToggle { const { id } = descriptor; return { ...descriptor, hasSwitch: id !== "presets", enabled, canToggleOn: id !== "presets" && id !== "headphone", toggle: (on) => toggleEffect(id, on), }; }

nodes.name: byId
nodes.body_text: byId = (id: EffectId): EffectDescriptor => EFFECTS.find((e) => e.id === id) as EffectDescriptor

nodes.name: useEffectToggle
nodes.body_text: function useEffectToggle(id: EffectId): EffectToggle { const enabled = useEngineStore((s) => enabledOf(id, s.state)); return useMemo(() => toggleFor(byId(id), enabled), [id, enabled]); }

nodes.name: useEffectToggles
nodes.body_text: function useEffectToggles(): Record<EffectId, EffectToggle> { const flags = useEngineStore(useShallow((s) => EFFECTS.map((e) => enabledOf(e.id, s.state)))); return useMemo( () => Object.fromEntries(EFFECTS.map((e, i) => [e.id, toggleFor(e, flags[i] ?? false)])) as Record< EffectId, EffectToggle >, [flags], ); }

nodes.name: xForFreq
nodes.body_text: xForFreq = (hz: number) => ((Math.log10(hz) - LOG_LO) / (LOG_HI - LOG_LO)) * W

nodes.name: yForDb
nodes.body_text: yForDb = (db: number) => { const amp = H / 2 - PAD_Y; return H / 2 - (Math.max(-DB_RANGE, Math.min(DB_RANGE, db)) / DB_RANGE) * amp; }

nodes.body_text: async function switchMode( target: AppMode, deps: SwitchDeps = defaultDeps, ): Promise<SwitchOutcome> { if (running) return "busy"; running = true; try { if (target === "player") { await deps.disable(); return "switched"; } if (!deps.requirePremium("SYSTEM_EQ")) return "blocked"; let status: SystemAudioStatus | null = null; try { status = await deps.systemAudioStatus(); } catch { status = null; // unknown — try enabling anyway } if (status) { if (!status.supported) { deps.toast.error("Equalizer mode isn't available on this computer."); return "unsupported"; } if (systemAudioAffordance(status) !== "enable") { void deps.openSettings("system-audio").catch(() => {}); deps.toast.info("Equalizer mode needs a one-time setup — finish it in Settings."); return "needs-setup"; } } await deps.enable(); const { enabled, error } = deps.eqState(); if (!enabled) { deps.toast.error(`Couldn't switch to Equalizer mode: ${error ?? "unknown error"}`); return "failed"; } deps.setRoute("equalizer"); return "switched"; } finally { running = false; } }

nodes.name: systemEqScope.ts
nodes.body_text: import { requirePremium } from "@/components/PremiumGate"; import { ipcErrorMessage } from "@/lib/ipc"; import type { SystemEqScope, SystemEqScopeMode } from "@/lib/types"; import { useEngineStore } from "@/stores/engine"; import { useSystemEqStore } from "@/stores/systemEq"; /** * Shared per-app scope logic for system-wide EQ (Settings card + the * Equalizer-mode sidebar panel). Each function resolves to an error message, * or `null` on success / when a premium gate refused. */ /** * Commit the scope to the backend FIRST (awaited), then — if system EQ is on — * rebuild the tap through the systemEq store so the new scope takes effect. A * failed rebuild stops, records the error and clears `enabled` (store behaviour). */ /** "All apps" / "Only N apps" / "All except N apps". */

nodes.name: applySystemEqScope
nodes.signature: async function applySystemEqScope(next: SystemEqScope): Promise<string | null>
nodes.body_text: async function applySystemEqScope(next: SystemEqScope): Promise<string | null> { try { await useEngineStore.getState().setSystemEqScope(next); } catch (e) { return ipcErrorMessage(e); } const eq = useSystemEqStore.getState(); if (eq.enabled) await eq.enable(); return null; }

nodes.name: setScopeMode
nodes.body_text: function setScopeMode(mode: SystemEqScopeMode): Promise<string | null> { if (!requirePremium("PER_APP_EQ")) return Promise.resolve(null); const scope = useEngineStore.getState().state.systemEqScope; return applySystemEqScope({ mode, apps: scope.apps }); }

nodes.name: toggleScopeApp
nodes.body_text: function toggleScopeApp(id: string): Promise<string | null> { if (!requirePremium("PER_APP_EQ")) return Promise.resolve(null); const scope = useEngineStore.getState().state.systemEqScope; const apps = scope.apps.includes(id) ? scope.apps.filter((a) => a !== id) : [...scope.apps, id]; return applySystemEqScope({ mode: scope.mode, apps }); }

nodes.name: scopeSummary
nodes.body_text: function scopeSummary(scope: SystemEqScope): string { const n = scope.apps.length; const apps = `${n} app${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}`; if (scope.mode === "only") return `Only ${apps}`; if (scope.mode === "except") return `All except ${apps}`; return "All apps"; }

nodes.body_text: function recent(items: AppNotification[], now = Date.now()): AppNotification[] { return items .filter((n) => { const t = Date.parse(n.createdAt); return Number.isNaN(t) || now - t <= WINDOW_MS; }) .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt)); }

nodes.name: ago
nodes.signature: function ago(iso: string, now = Date.now()): string
nodes.body_text: function ago(iso: string, now = Date.now()): string { const t = Date.parse(iso); if (Number.isNaN(t)) return ""; const m = Math.max(0, Math.round((now - t) / 60_000)); if (m < 1) return "now"; if (m < 60) return `${m}m`; const h = Math.round(m / 60); if (h < 24) return `${h}h`; return `${Math.round(h / 24)}d`; }

nodes.body_text: function groupTracks(tracks: MusicTrack[], facet: Facet): Group[] { const keyer: Record<Exclude<Facet, "songs">, (t: MusicTrack) => string> = { albums: (t) => t.album?.trim() || "Singles", artists: (t) => t.artist?.trim() || "Unknown artist", folders: (t) => t.folder?.trim() || "Other", genres: (t) => t.genre?.trim() || "Unknown genre", }; const fn = keyer[facet as Exclude<Facet, "songs">]; const map = new Map<string, Group>(); for (const t of tracks) { const label = fn(t); const existing = map.get(label.toLowerCase()); if (existing) { existing.tracks.push(t); } else { map.set(label.toLowerCase(), { key: label.toLowerCase(), label, subtitle: "", seed: facet === "albums" ? label : `${facet}:${label}`, art: trackArt(t), tracks: [t], }); } } const groups = [...map.values()]; for (const g of groups) { g.subtitle = facet === "albums" ? "Unknown artist", art: trackArt(t), seed: t.album?.trim() || t.title, index: i, })); }

nodes.name: ScrollingWaveform.tsx
nodes.body_text: import { useEffect, useRef } from "react"; import { useEngineStore } from "@/stores/engine"; /** Device-independent width of one sample column (CSS px). */ const COL_W = 2; /** Cap the backing-store scale (mirrors the visualizer scenes' MAX_DPR = 2): * beyond 2× the extra pixels are invisible behind the blur, but the full-ring * redraw cost keeps climbing with the raw devicePixelRatio. */ const MAX_DPR = 2; /** The capped device pixel ratio used for canvas sizing and drawing. */ /** A fixed-length ring buffer of recent stereo levels (one slot per frame). */ /** Redraw the whole ring buffer: oldest at the left, newest at the right. */ /** The canvas + its data pump. Mounted only while a track is loaded, so it * starts fresh each session and tears down cleanly on stop. */ /** * A VirtualDJ-style scrolling stereo waveform that fills its container (mounted * in the top bar): left channel sweeps the top in blue, right channel the bottom * in red, newest at the right edge. It runs while audio plays and freezes when * paused. Renders nothing when no track is loaded. */

nodes.name: cappedDpr
nodes.body_text: cappedDpr = (): number => Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, MAX_DPR)

nodes.name: Ring
nodes.body_text: interface Ring { l: Float32Array; r: Float32Array; /** Index the next sample will be written to (oldest sample lives here). */ head: number; len: number; }

nodes.name: clamp01
nodes.body_text: clamp01 = (v: number): number => (v > 1 ? 1 : v < 0 ? 0 : v)

nodes.name: drawWaveform
nodes.signature: function drawWaveform( ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, width: number, height: number, buf: Ring | null, ): void
nodes.body_text: function drawWaveform( ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, width: number, height: number, buf: Ring | null, ): void { ctx.clearRect(0, 0, width, height); if (!buf) return; const dpr = cappedDpr(); const colW = COL_W * dpr; const mid = height / 2; for (let x = 0; x < buf.len; x++) { const idx = (buf.head + x) % buf.len; const lv = buf.l[idx]!; const rv = buf.r[idx]!; const px = x * colW; // Top half = left channel (blue); bottom half = right channel (red), // brighter as the level rises — VirtualDJ's stereo signature. if (lv > 0.001) { ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(56, 140, 255, ${0.3 + 0.7 * lv})`; ctx.fillRect(px, mid - lv * mid, colW + 0.6, lv * mid); } if (rv > 0.001) { ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(240, 60, 70, ${0.3 + 0.7 * rv})`; ctx.fillRect(px, mid, colW + 0.6, rv * mid); } } // Faint centre seam. ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)"; ctx.fillRect(0, mid - dpr * 0.5, width, dpr); }

nodes.name: SeekBar.test.ts
nodes.body_text: import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; import { seekDisplayValue } from "./SeekBar"; describe("seekDisplayValue", () => { /** The rule the whole scrub pattern exists for: while dragging, the thumb * follows the finger, not the still-advancing playback position. */ it("shows the scrub value while dragging, ignoring playback position", () => { expect(seekDisplayValue(30, 12, 200)).toBe(30); }); it("shows the real position when not dragging", () => { expect(seekDisplayValue(null, 12, 200)).toBe(12); }); /** A position past a known duration (rounding, a stream over-reporting) must * not push the thumb off the end of the bar. */ it("clamps the resting position to the duration", () => { expect(seekDisplayValue(null, 205, 200)).toBe(200); }); /** Before a stream's length is known, there's nothing to clamp to; show the * position as-is rather than snapping it to zero. */ it("shows the position unclamped when duration is unknown", () => { expect(seekDisplayValue(null, 42, 0)).toBe(42); }); /** Scrubbing to zero is a real value, not "no scrub" — it must not fall * through to the playback position. */ it("treats a scrub value of 0 as an active scrub", () => { expect(seekDisplayValue(0, 55, 200)).toBe(0); }); });

nodes.name: SeekBar.tsx
nodes.body_text: import { useState } from "react"; import { Slider } from "@/components/Slider"; import { formatTime } from "@/lib/format"; /** * The value the thumb should sit at: the scrub position while dragging, the * engine's real position otherwise, clamped to the known duration. * * Pure so the "a live drag shows where you're dragging, not where playback is" * rule is tested without a pointer. `scrub` is `null` whenever the user isn't * actively dragging. */ /** * A seek bar that scrubs visually during a drag but only *seeks* on release. * * This is the whole point: a streamed source (cloud, phone, YouTube Music) seeks * by re-opening its network connection at the new byte offset. The shared * [`Slider`] streams a value on every pointer move, so wiring seek straight to * `onChange` fires one connection re-open per drag frame — dozens a second — * which starves the audio ring and stops playback. Here `onChange` only moves * the thumb (local state, no engine call); the real seek runs once, from * `onCommit`, when the user lets go. A local file wouldn't care, but the bar * can't tell which it is, so it treats both the safe way. */

nodes.body_text: function seekDisplayValue( scrub: number | null, position: number, duration: number, ): number { if (scrub !== null) return scrub; return Math.min(position, duration > 0 ? duration : position); }

nodes.body_text: function timedWords(line: LyricLine): TimedWord[] { const start = line.timeMs ?? 0; const end = line.endMs ?? start + 4000; if (line.words?.length) { return line.words.map((w, i) => ({ text: w.text, startMs: w.timeMs, endMs: line.words![i + 1]?.timeMs ?? end, })); } const words = line.text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean); const totalChars = words.reduce((n, w) => n + w.length, 0) || 1; const span = Math.max(end - start, 400); let acc = start; return words.map((w) => { const from = acc; acc += span * (w.length / totalChars); return { text: w, startMs: from, endMs: acc }; }); }

A phone track is checked for * its own downloaded `.lrc` first (so the user's sidecars win); local files go * through the backend's sidecar/embedded path; everything then falls back to * the online chain (LRCLIB → HypeMuzik backend) by title/artist. */ /** * Lyrics for whatever is currently playing. nodes.signature: function cacheSet(key: string, value: ParsedLyrics | null): void
nodes.body_text: function cacheSet(key: string, value: ParsedLyrics | null): void { cache.set(key, value); while (cache.size > CACHE_CAP) { const oldest = cache.keys().next().value; if (oldest === undefined) break; cache.delete(oldest); } }

nodes.name: videoSync.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Keeping a muted `<video>` beside DSP-chain audio. * * Two clocks exist and only one is the truth. The engine owns playback — it * decodes, it applies the chain, it is what you hear — so the picture follows * it, never the reverse. The video element is never allowed to influence audio * in any way; the worst a broken video may do is look wrong. * * They drift regardless: separate decoders, separate buffering, and a video * whose bytes arrive over a link that may be slower than the audio's. So the * position is compared each progress tick and the video is nudged only when the * gap is big enough to see. Correcting continuously would mean seeking on every * tick, which stutters far worse than the drift it fixes. * * The decision is a pure function so it can be tested without a DOM, a network, * or an audio engine — the parts that make this hard to reason about are exactly * the parts worth isolating from it. */ /** How far the picture may drift before it's worth a correction. * * Under this, a viewer can't tell — and a seek costs a decode flush and a * visible stutter, so correcting it would be the more noticeable of the two * faults. Music video is also forgiving in a way film isn't: nobody lip-reads * a music video, and the beat you're hearing is the engine's regardless. */ export const DRIFT_TOLERANCE_SECS = 0.25; /** A video that has drifted this far isn't drifting, it's lost — a stall, a * buffer starve, or a seek the element never saw. Correct it the same way; the * constant exists to name the case, not to branch on it. */ export const DRIFT_LOST_SECS = 5; /** * What the picture should do to match the sound. * * Ordering matters: transport before position. Seeking a video that is about to * be paused is wasted work, and a video left playing while the engine is paused * runs away — the drift then grows without bound instead of being corrected. */

nodes.name: SyncInputs
nodes.body_text: interface SyncInputs { /** The engine's position — the truth. */ enginePos: number; /** The element's own clock. */ videoPos: number; /** Whether the engine considers itself paused. */ paused: boolean; /** Whether the element is currently paused. */ videoPaused: boolean; /** Whether the element has enough data to play at all. Correcting a video * that hasn't buffered yet just fights its loader. */ ready: boolean; }

nodes.name: SyncAction
nodes.body_text: interface SyncAction { /** Seek the element here, or null to leave its clock alone. */ seekTo: number | null; /** Play/pause the element, or null to leave it as it is. */ setPaused: boolean | null; }

nodes.name: syncAction
nodes.body_text: function syncAction(i: SyncInputs): SyncAction { const setPaused = i.videoPaused !== i.paused ? i.paused : null; // Nothing decoded yet: its clock is meaningless and seeking only interrupts // the buffering that would make it meaningful. if (!i.ready) return { seekTo: null, setPaused }; const drift = Math.abs(i.videoPos - i.enginePos); return { seekTo: drift > DRIFT_TOLERANCE_SECS ? i.enginePos : null, setPaused, }; }

nodes.name: playbackSession.ts
nodes.body_text: import type { QueueItem, QueueSource, RepeatMode } from "@/stores/engine"; /** * The playback session that survives a relaunch: the queue, where in it the * listener was, how far into the track, and shuffle/repeat. Same model as the * mobile app (`lib/services/playback_session.dart`): restoring rebuilds the * queue but loads nothing; the first press of play loads the track and seeks * to the saved position. A restored session is always paused: an app that * makes noise because it was opened is a bad guest. * * Pure: serialisation, windowing and validation only. Persistence lives in * `useSessionPersistence`, the restore/resume behaviour in the engine store. */ export const SESSION_VERSION = 1; /** Longest queue kept, windowed around the current track. */ export const MAX_SESSION_TRACKS = 500; /** How many already-played tracks the window keeps behind the current one. */ export const SESSION_TRACKS_BEHIND = 50; /** The engine-store fields a session is taken from. */ /** Sources a session can bring back. A phone cast is the phone's playback, not ours. */ const RESTORABLE: ReadonlySet<QueueSource> = new Set(["local", "phone", "cloud", "ytmusic", "radio"]); /** The payload field each source needs to play again. */ const PAYLOAD: Record<Exclude<QueueSource, "cast">, keyof QueueItem> = { local: "track", phone: "phoneTrack", cloud: "cloud", ytmusic: "ytTrack", radio: "radioUrl", }; /** A copy fit to store: inline (`data:`) cover art is dropped; it is re-read. */ /** * The session to save for `s`, or null when there is nothing to come back to * (an empty queue, or a cast from the phone). Long queues are windowed to * {@link MAX_SESSION_TRACKS} around the current track, in play order. */ /** * Parse and repair a saved session; null if it can't be used. Invalid items * are dropped and the order re-pointed; entries the order lost are appended * so a queue can never lose tracks to a stale index. If the current track * itself is unusable there is nothing sensible to resume. */

nodes.name: PlaybackSession
nodes.body_text: interface PlaybackSession { v: typeof SESSION_VERSION; queue: QueueItem[]; /** Play order: indices into `queue` (a permutation when shuffled). */ order: number[]; /** Position of the current track within `order`. */ orderPos: number; shuffle: boolean; repeat: RepeatMode; /** Seconds into the current track. */ positionSecs: number; }

nodes.name: SessionSource
nodes.body_text: interface SessionSource { queue: QueueItem[]; order: number[]; orderPos: number; shuffle: boolean; repeat: RepeatMode; positionSecs: number; /** Set while a restored session hasn't been played yet: its saved position. */ resumeAt: number | null; }

nodes.name: storable
nodes.body_text: function storable(item: QueueItem): QueueItem { if (typeof item.cover === "string" && item.cover.startsWith("data:")) { const { cover: _cover, ...rest } = item; return rest; } return item; }

nodes.name: snapshotSession
nodes.body_text: function snapshotSession(s: SessionSource): PlaybackSession | null { const current = s.order[s.orderPos]; const item = current === undefined ? undefined : s.queue[current]; if (!item || !RESTORABLE.has(item.source)) return null; // A live station has no position; a track's is the saved one if it hasn't // been played since the restore. const positionSecs = item.source === "radio" ? 0 : Math.max(0, s.resumeAt ?? s.positionSecs); if (s.order.length <= MAX_SESSION_TRACKS) { return { v: SESSION_VERSION, queue: s.queue.map(storable), order: [...s.order], orderPos: s.orderPos, shuffle: s.shuffle, repeat: s.repeat, positionSecs, }; } // Window the play order, not the unshuffled list: the latter would drop // tracks the shuffled order still points at. The window becomes the queue, // in play order. const start = Math.max( 0, Math.min(s.orderPos - SESSION_TRACKS_BEHIND, s.order.length - MAX_SESSION_TRACKS), ); const window = s.order.slice(start, start + MAX_SESSION_TRACKS); const queue = window .map((i) => s.queue[i]) .filter((it): it is QueueItem => it !== undefined) .map(storable); return { v: SESSION_VERSION, queue, order: queue.map((_, i) => i), orderPos: s.orderPos - start, shuffle: s.shuffle, repeat: s.repeat, positionSecs, }; }

nodes.name: isObj
nodes.signature: isObj = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown>
nodes.body_text: isObj = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> => typeof v === "object" && v !== null

nodes.name: validItem
nodes.signature: function validItem(v: unknown): v is QueueItem
nodes.body_text: function validItem(v: unknown): v is QueueItem { if (!isObj(v)) return false; if (typeof v.id !== "string" || typeof v.title !== "string") return false; const source = v.source as QueueSource; if (!RESTORABLE.has(source)) return false; const payload = v[PAYLOAD[source as Exclude<QueueSource, "cast">]]; if (source === "radio") return typeof payload === "string" && payload.length > 0; if (!isObj(payload)) return false; // Phone tracks also need their device to stream from. if (source === "phone" && !isObj(v.device)) return false; return true; }

nodes.name: parseSession
nodes.signature: function parseSession(text: string | null | undefined): PlaybackSession | null
nodes.body_text: function parseSession(text: string | null | undefined): PlaybackSession | null { if (!text) return null; let raw: unknown; try { raw = JSON.parse(text); } catch { return null; } if (!isObj(raw) || raw.v !== SESSION_VERSION || !Array.isArray(raw.queue) || !Array.isArray(raw.order)) { return null; } // Keep valid items; map old indices to new ones. const queue: QueueItem[] = []; const remap = new Map<number, number>(); raw.queue.forEach((it, i) => { if (validItem(it)) { remap.set(i, queue.length); queue.push(it); } }); if (queue.length === 0) return null; const rawOrder = raw.order as unknown[]; const rawPos = typeof raw.orderPos === "number" ? raw.orderPos : -1; const currentOld = Number.isInteger(rawOrder[rawPos]) ? (rawOrder[rawPos] as number) : undefined; const currentNew = currentOld === undefined ? undefined : remap.get(currentOld); if (currentNew === undefined) return null; // Re-point the order: valid, de-duplicated, then anything it forgot. const seen = new Set<number>(); const order: number[] = []; for (const o of rawOrder) { const n = Number.isInteger(o) ? remap.get(o as number) : undefined; if (n !== undefined && !seen.has(n)) { seen.add(n); order.push(n); } } for (let i = 0; i < queue.length; i++) if (!seen.has(i)) order.push(i); const repeat: RepeatMode = raw.repeat === "all" || raw.repeat === "one" ? raw.repeat : "off"; const positionSecs = typeof raw.positionSecs === "number" && Number.isFinite(raw.positionSecs) && raw.positionSecs > 0 ? raw.positionSecs : 0; return { v: SESSION_VERSION, queue, order, orderPos: order.indexOf(currentNew), shuffle: raw.shuffle === true, repeat, positionSecs, }; }

nodes.body_text: import { useEffect } from "react"; import { sessionLoad, sessionSave } from "@/lib/ipc"; import { useEngineStore } from "@/stores/engine"; import { parseSession, snapshotSession } from "./playbackSession"; /** Queue/position-in-queue changes are saved at most this often. */ export const SESSION_SAVE_THROTTLE_MS = 500; /** * While playing, the position is saved this often. Saving on every progress * tick would be a disk write per frame of the progress bar; this loses at * most a few seconds on a hard quit. */ export const POSITION_SAVE_MS = 5_000; /** * Bring the last playback session back on launch, and keep it saved. Mount * once, in the main window (it owns playback). * * Nothing is saved until the restore has been attempted: the store starts * empty, and saving that first would erase the session about to be restored. */

nodes.name: useSessionPersistence
nodes.body_text: function useSessionPersistence(): void { useEffect(() => { let disposed = false; let ready = false; // `undefined` = nothing written yet this run; `null` = written "no session". let lastJson: string | null | undefined; let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined; const save = () => { if (disposed || !ready) return; let json: string | null; try { const snap = snapshotSession(useEngineStore.getState()); json = snap ? JSON.stringify(snap) : null; } catch { return; } if (json === lastJson) return; lastJson = json; void sessionSave(json).catch(() => {}); }; // Doesn't reset a pending save: the queue array is replaced often by // background tag enrichment, and a resetting debounce could starve. const schedule = () => { if (disposed || timer !== undefined) return; timer = setTimeout(() => { timer = undefined; save(); }, SESSION_SAVE_THROTTLE_MS); }; void sessionLoad() .then((text) => { if (disposed) return; const session = parseSession(text); if (session) useEngineStore.getState().restoreSession(session); }) .catch(() => {}) .finally(() => { if (disposed) return; ready = true; schedule(); }); const unsubscribe = useEngineStore.subscribe((s, prev) => { if ( s.queue !== prev.queue || s.order !== prev.order || s.orderPos !== prev.orderPos || s.shuffle !== prev.shuffle || s.repeat !== prev.repeat || s.resumeAt !== prev.resumeAt || // Pausing is a natural "stopped here": keep the exact spot. (s.paused && !prev.paused) ) { schedule(); } }); const ticker = setInterval(() => { const s = useEngineStore.getState(); if (s.playing && !s.paused) save(); }, POSITION_SAVE_MS); // The window hiding (macOS close hides it) or going away: save the spot now. const flush = () => save(); const onVisibility = () => { if (document.visibilityState === "hidden") flush(); }; document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", onVisibility); window.addEventListener("pagehide", flush); window.addEventListener("beforeunload", flush); return () => { disposed = true; if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer); clearInterval(ticker); unsubscribe(); document.removeEventListener("visibilitychange", onVisibility); window.removeEventListener("pagehide", flush); window.removeEventListener("beforeunload", flush); }; }, []); }

JSON.stringify(snap) : null; } catch { return; } if (json === lastJson) return; lastJson = json; void sessionSave(json).catch(() => {}); }

nodes.body_text: import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; import { downloadPercent } from "./UpdateRow"; /** * The only real decision in the update UI: a chunked response carries no * `Content-Length`, so there is no total to divide by. * * Treating that as zero gives a progress bar pinned at 0% for the whole * download — which reads as a stall, at exactly the moment the user is waiting * on tens of megabytes. `null` is the signal to show an indeterminate bar * instead, and that difference is worth pinning down. */ describe("downloadPercent", () => { it("reports progress when the server sent a length", () => { expect(downloadPercent(0, 100)).toBe(0); expect(downloadPercent(50, 100)).toBe(50); expect(downloadPercent(100, 100)).toBe(100); }); it("is null when there is no total, rather than zero", () => { expect(downloadPercent(1_000_000, null)).toBeNull(); }); /** A zero or negative total is a broken header, not a finished download. * Dividing by it yields Infinity or NaN, both of which render as garbage. */ it("treats a nonsense total as no total at all", () => { expect(downloadPercent(10, 0)).toBeNull(); expect(downloadPercent(10, -1)).toBeNull(); }); /** Servers can send slightly more than they promised (trailing bytes, or a * length that excluded encoding). The bar must not exceed full. */ it("never exceeds 100 when more arrives than was promised", () => { expect(downloadPercent(120, 100)).toBe(100); }); });

nodes.body_text: import type { SystemAudioStatus } from "../../lib/ipc"; /** Which affordance the System-wide audio card shows for a given status. */ /** * Decide the card's affordance from {@link SystemAudioStatus}. * * The order matters: `available` wins outright (an already-working pipeline is * never asked to install anything), and "Install audio driver" is offered only * when there is actually a bundled package to install — a driverless build * showing that button could only dead-end in an error. */

nodes.name: SystemAudioAffordance
nodes.signature: type SystemAudioAffordance = | "enable" // ready now → Enable / Restart / Stop | "install" // driver bundled but not installed → "Install audio driver" | "not-bundled" // no signed driver in this build → one-click VB-CABLE setup | "unavailable";
nodes.body_text: type SystemAudioAffordance = | "enable" // ready now → Enable / Restart / Stop | "install" // driver bundled but not installed → "Install audio driver" | "not-bundled" // no signed driver in this build → one-click VB-CABLE setup | "unavailable";

nodes.name: systemAudioAffordance
nodes.body_text: function systemAudioAffordance( status: SystemAudioStatus, ): SystemAudioAffordance { if (status.available) return "enable"; if (status.needsDriver && status.driverBundled) return "install"; if (!status.driverBundled) return "not-bundled"; return "unavailable"; }

import "@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest"; const win = vi.hoisted(() => ({ close: vi.fn(async () => {}), sectionHandler: null as null | ((section: string) => void), })); vi.mock("@tauri-apps/api/window", () => ({ getCurrentWindow: () => ({ close: win.close }), })); vi.mock("@tauri-apps/api/webviewWindow", () => ({ getCurrentWebviewWindow: () => ({ label: "settings" }), })); // The backend never answers: every card renders its loading state. vi.mock("@tauri-apps/api/core", () => ({ invoke: vi.fn(() => new Promise(() => {})), convertFileSrc: (p: string) => p, })); vi.mock("@tauri-apps/api/event", () => ({ emit: vi.fn(async () => {}), emitTo: vi.fn(async () => {}), listen: vi.fn(async () => () => {}), })); vi.mock("@/lib/ipc", async (importOriginal) => { const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import("@/lib/ipc")>(); return { ...actual, onSettingsSection: vi.fn(async (handler: (section: string) => void) => { win.sectionHandler = handler; return () => { win.sectionHandler = null; }; }), }; }); import { SettingsWindow } from "./SettingsWindow"; import { SETTINGS_SECTIONS } from "./sections"; const scrollIntoView = vi.fn(); beforeEach(() => { win.close.mockClear(); scrollIntoView.mockClear(); Element.prototype.scrollIntoView = scrollIntoView; window.location.hash = ""; }); afterEach(cleanup); describe("SettingsWindow", () => { it("renders every section anchor and a nav entry for each", async () => { await mount(); for (const { id, label } of SETTINGS_SECTIONS) { expect(document.getElementById(id), id).not.toBeNull(); expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: label })).toBeInTheDocument(); } }); it("scrolls to a section when settings://section arrives", async () => { await mount(); expect(win.sectionHandler).not.toBeNull(); act(() => win.sectionHandler?.("cloud")); expect(scrollIntoView).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); expect(scrollIntoView.mock.instances[0]).toBe(document.getElementById("cloud")); }); it("ignores unknown sections", async () => { await mount(); act(() => win.sectionHandler?.("nope")); expect(scrollIntoView).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); }); it("scrolls to the section in the URL hash on mount", async () => { window.location.hash = "#youtube-music"; await mount(); expect(scrollIntoView.mock.instances[0]).toBe(document.getElementById("youtube-music")); }); it("closes on Escape", async () => { await mount(); fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: "Escape" }); expect(win.close).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); }); it("closes on Cmd/Ctrl+W", async () => { await mount(); fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: "w", metaKey: true }); expect(win.close).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); }); it("does not close on Escape while an input is focused", async () => { await mount(); const input = document.createElement("input"); document.body.appendChild(input); input.focus(); fireEvent.keyDown(input, { key: "Escape" }); expect(win.close).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); input.remove(); }); it("does not close on Escape while a dialog is open", async () => { await mount(); const dialog = document.createElement("div"); dialog.setAttribute("role", "dialog"); document.body.appendChild(dialog); fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: "Escape" }); expect(win.close).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); dialog.remove(); }); });

"smooth" : "auto", block: "start", }); setActive(id); pinnedUntil.current = Date.now() + 1200; if (opts?.flash && !prefersReducedMotion) { el.classList.add(...FLASH); window.setTimeout(() => el.classList.remove(...FLASH), FLASH_MS); } }, []); // Deep link from the URL hash, then from a later `settings_open(section)`. useEffect(() => { const hash = decodeURIComponent(window.location.hash.replace(/^#/, "")); if (hash) goTo(hash); let unlisten: (() => void) | undefined; let cancelled = false; onSettingsSection((section) => goTo(section, { flash: true, smooth: true })) .then((un) => (cancelled ? un() : (unlisten = un))) .catch(() => {}); return () => { cancelled = true; unlisten?.(); }; }, [goTo]); // Highlight the section in view. useEffect(() => { const root = scrollRef.current; if (!root || typeof IntersectionObserver === "undefined") return; const observer = new IntersectionObserver( (entries) => { if (Date.now() < pinnedUntil.current) return; const hit = entries .filter((e) => e.isIntersecting) .sort((a, b) => a.boundingClientRect.top - b.boundingClientRect.top)[0]; if (hit && isSettingsSection(hit.target.id)) setActive(hit.target.id); }, { root, rootMargin: "0px 0px -70% 0px" }, ); for (const { id } of SETTINGS_SECTIONS) { const el = document.getElementById(id); if (el) observer.observe(el); } // At the very bottom the last sections never reach the top band; highlight // the last one whose heading is on screen instead. const onScroll = () => { if (Date.now() < pinnedUntil.current) return; if (root.scrollTop + root.clientHeight < root.scrollHeight - 2) return; const bottom = root.getBoundingClientRect().bottom; const visible = SETTINGS_SECTIONS.filter(({ id }) => { const el = document.getElementById(id); return el ? el.getBoundingClientRect().top < bottom - 48 : false; }); const last = visible[visible.length - 1]; if (last) setActive(last.id); }; root.addEventListener("scroll", onScroll, { passive: true }); return () => { observer.disconnect(); root.removeEventListener("scroll", onScroll); }; }, []); // Esc / Cmd+W / Ctrl+W close the window. useEffect(() => { const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => { if (e.defaultPrevented) return; if (e.key === "Escape") { if (!escapeIsClaimed()) closeWindow(); } else if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === "w") { e.preventDefault(); closeWindow(); } }; window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey); return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey); }, []); return (

Guarded by a run id so // a slow probe for a list the user already navigated away from can't overwrite // the current one's results. const runHealthCheck = useCallback((channels: TvChannel[]) => { setProbedIds(new Set()); setAliveIds(new Set()); const slice = channels.slice(0, PROBE_CAP); if (slice.length === 0) return; const run = ++healthRunRef.current; setChecking(true); tvCheckAlive(slice) .then((ids) => { if (healthRunRef.current !== run) return; Renders through a portal to * document.body as a draggable picture-in-picture (mini / normal / fullscreen) * so the channel list stays browsable; selecting another channel re-points the * same element. Full control set: play/pause, seek + time (VOD/DVR), volume, * quality, audio tracks, PiP, keyboard shortcuts, fullscreen. */ const SPEEDS = [0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2]; /** A round translucent control button. */

nodes.body_text: function TvPlayer({ channel, onClose }: { channel: TvChannel; onClose: () => void }) { const videoRef = useRef<HTMLVideoElement>(null); const hlsRef = useRef<HlsType | null>(null); const hideTimer = useRef<number | null>(null); const drag = useRef<{ px: number; py: number; ox: number; oy: number } | null>(null); const [status, setStatus] = useState<Status>("loading"); const [muted, setMuted] = useState(false); const [volume, setVolume] = useState(1); const [mode, setMode] = useState<Mode>("normal"); const [pos, setPos] = useState<{ x: number; y: number } | null>(null); const [controlsShown, setControlsShown] = useState(true); const [reloadKey, setReloadKey] = useState(0); const [isLive, setIsLive] = useState(true); const [duration, setDuration] = useState(0); const [currentTime, setCurrentTime] = useState(0); const [buffered, setBuffered] = useState(0); const [levels, setLevels] = useState<Level[]>([]); const [currentLevel, setCurrentLevel] = useState(-1); // -1 = auto const [audioTracks, setAudioTracks] = useState<Track[]>([]); const [audioTrack, setAudioTrack] = useState(-1); const [subtitleTracks, setSubtitleTracks] = useState<Track[]>([]); const [subtitleTrack, setSubtitleTrack] = useState(-1); // -1 = off const [speed, setSpeed] = useState(1); const [settingsOpen, setSettingsOpen] = useState(false); const [pipActive, setPipActive] = useState(false); const stopEngine = useEngineStore((s) => s.stop); // Load / switch the stream whenever the channel (or a manual retry) changes. useEffect(() => { const video = videoRef.current; if (!video) return; let cancelled = false; // How many times we'll try to recover from a fatal error before calling the // channel dead. hls.js's default reaction to a fatal network error is to // reload forever — for a stream that is genuinely down (and iptv-org ships // many), that is an eternal spinner the user reads as "the app is broken" // rather than "this channel is". A small budget lets a real transient blip // recover while a dead channel fails fast and honestly. const MAX_RECOVERIES = 3; let recoveries = 0; // Nothing has played within this long ⇒ dead, even if hls.js never emitted a // fatal error. This is the safety net for the case the backend probe can't // catch: a master playlist that loads but whose segments 403/stall, which // otherwise buffers silently forever. const STALL_DEADLINE_MS = 15_000; let stallTimer: number | undefined; const armStall = () => { window.clearTimeout(stallTimer); stallTimer = window.setTimeout(() => { if (!cancelled) setStatus("error"); }, STALL_DEADLINE_MS); }; setStatus("loading"); setLevels([]); setAudioTracks([]); setSubtitleTracks([]); setSubtitleTrack(-1); setSpeed(1); setIsLive(true); void stopEngine(); const teardown = () => { window.clearTimeout(stallTimer); if (hlsRef.current) { hlsRef.current.destroy(); hlsRef.current = null; } video.removeAttribute("src"); video.load(); }; teardown(); const play = () => { video.play().catch(() => { video.muted = true; setMuted(true); void video.play().catch(() => {}); }); }; // Real playback disarms the stall deadline and refills the recovery budget, // so a stream that plays, blips, and recovers isn't punished for the blip. const onPlaying = () => { window.clearTimeout(stallTimer); recoveries = 0; }; video.addEventListener("playing", onPlaying); tvStreamUrl(channel) .then(async (url) => { if (cancelled) return; const { default: Hls } = await import("hls.js"); if (cancelled) return; if (Hls.isSupported()) { const hls = new Hls({ enableWorker: true, startFragPrefetch: true, lowLatencyMode: false, backBufferLength: 30, manifestLoadingTimeOut: 8000, manifestLoadingMaxRetry: 3, levelLoadingTimeOut: 8000, fragLoadingTimeOut: 20000, }); hlsRef.current = hls; hls.loadSource(url); hls.attachMedia(video); armStall(); hls.on(Hls.Events.MANIFEST_PARSED, () => { play(); setLevels( hls.levels.map((l, i) => ({ index: i, label: l.height ? `${l.height}p` : `${Math.round((l.bitrate || 0) / 1000)}k`, })), ); }); hls.on(Hls.Events.LEVEL_SWITCHED, (_e, data) => { setCurrentLevel(hls.autoLevelEnabled ? -1 : data.level); }); hls.on(Hls.Events.LEVEL_LOADED, (_e, data) => setIsLive(data.details.live)); hls.on(Hls.Events.AUDIO_TRACKS_UPDATED, () => { setAudioTracks( hls.audioTracks.map((t) => ({ id: t.id, label: t.name || t.lang || `Track ${t.id + 1}` })), ); setAudioTrack(hls.audioTrack); }); hls.on(Hls.Events.AUDIO_TRACK_SWITCHED, (_e, data) => setAudioTrack(data.id)); hls.on(Hls.Events.SUBTITLE_TRACKS_UPDATED, () => { setSubtitleTracks( hls.subtitleTracks.map((t) => ({ id: t.id, label: t.name || t.lang || `Track ${t.id + 1}` })), ); }); hls.on(Hls.Events.SUBTITLE_TRACK_SWITCH, (_e, data) => setSubtitleTrack(data.id)); hls.on(Hls.Events.ERROR, (_e, data) => { if (!data.fatal) return; // Give recovery a bounded number of tries, then stop. A reshuffle inside a band would be visible churn. */ it("preserves catalog order within each health band", () => { const out = rankByHealth(list, probed, alive).map((c) => c.id); expect(out.indexOf("alive1")).toBeLessThan(out.indexOf("alive2")); expect(out.indexOf("dead1")).toBeLessThan(out.indexOf("dead2")); }); /** Before any probe completes, the list must not reorder — otherwise it jumps * the instant a check returns nothing. */ it("leaves the list untouched when nothing has been probed", () => { const out = rankByHealth(list, new Set(), new Set()); expect(out.map((c) => c.id)).toEqual(list.map((c) => c.id)); }); });

nodes.name: tvList.ts
nodes.body_text: import type { TvChannel } from "@/lib/types"; /** * The presentation logic for a TV channel list — filtering and health-ordering — * as pure functions, so the part that decides what a user sees is tested without * a component, a network, or the DOM. */ /** What a health probe concluded about a channel, from the caller's sets. * * A channel is only `dead` if it was actually probed and failed. One we haven't * probed is `unknown`, never `dead` — we don't dim a channel we never checked. */ /** Case-insensitive filter over a channel's name and category. * * For filtering *within* a loaded country/category list — distinct from the * global catalog search, which is a backend call. An empty query is the whole * list. */ /** Working channels first, unchecked next, dead last — a **stable** reorder, so * within each band the catalog's own order is preserved. * * Dead channels are kept, not dropped: a stream that's momentarily down should * sink, not vanish (and reappear jarringly when it recovers). The caller dims * them. Returns the input unchanged when nothing has been probed yet, so the * list doesn't reshuffle the instant a check completes on an empty result. */

nodes.name: Health
nodes.body_text: type Health = "alive" | "dead" | "unknown";

nodes.name: channelHealth
nodes.signature: function channelHealth( id: string, probed: ReadonlySet<string>, alive: ReadonlySet<string>, ): Health
nodes.body_text: function channelHealth( id: string, probed: ReadonlySet<string>, alive: ReadonlySet<string>, ): Health { if (!probed.has(id)) return "unknown"; return alive.has(id) ? "alive" : "dead"; }

nodes.name: filterChannels
nodes.signature: function filterChannels(channels: TvChannel[], query: string): TvChannel[]
nodes.body_text: function filterChannels(channels: TvChannel[], query: string): TvChannel[] { const q = query.trim().toLowerCase(); if (!q) return channels; return channels.filter( (c) => c.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || (c.group?.toLowerCase().includes(q) ?? false), ); }

nodes.name: rankByHealth
nodes.signature: function rankByHealth( channels: TvChannel[], probed: ReadonlySet<string>, alive: ReadonlySet<string>, ): TvChannel[]
nodes.body_text: function rankByHealth( channels: TvChannel[], probed: ReadonlySet<string>, alive: ReadonlySet<string>, ): TvChannel[] { if (probed.size === 0) return channels; const rank: Record<Health, number> = { alive: 0, unknown: 1, dead: 2 }; // Decorate-sort-undecorate keeps it stable and O(n log n) without relying on // the engine's sort stability for the tie-break — the index is the tie-break. return channels .map((c, i) => ({ c, i, r: rank[channelHealth(c.id, probed, alive)] })) .sort((a, b) => a.r - b.r || a.i - b.i) .map((x) => x.c); }
