nodes.name: ipc.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Typed IPC layer. * * Every Tauri command is wrapped in a typed function here; components never * call `invoke` directly. Commands reject with an `IpcError`; `isIpcError` * narrows the unknown rejection so callers can surface `code`/`message`. * Streaming telemetry arrives over events, wrapped in `onEngineFrame` / * `onTransport`. */ import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core"; import { listen } from "@tauri-apps/api/event"; import type { UnlistenFn } from "@tauri-apps/api/event"; import { open } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog"; import type { AccountStatus, AppInfo, AutoEqEntry, ChainPreset, CloudAccount, CloudAudioPage, CloudEntry, CloudProvider, CloudStatus, CloudTrackMeta, CompanderState, DeviceInfo, EngineFrame, EngineState, EqPreset, HeadphoneProfile, IpcError, LibraryPage, LibraryTrack, LicenseStatus, MixerSnapshot, OutputDevice, OutputState, PhoneDevice, PhoneTrack, Playlist, RadioBatch, RadioCountry, RadioStation, TvChannel, TvCategory, TvCountry, ExploreItem, ExploreSection, ExploreShelf, YtDownloadProgress, YtMusicPage, YtMusicStatus, YtTrack, ConvolverState, RoomState, SaturationState, SpatialMode, SurroundSpeakers, SystemEqScope, TrackMeta, TransportProgress, Entitlements, } from "./types"; import type { DeviceInfo as ConnectDeviceInfo, DeviceKind as ConnectDeviceKind, Frame as ConnectFrame, } from "@/features/connect/protocol"; /* ----------------------------------------------------------------- commands */ /** App name, version, and engine schema revision. */ /** System output devices (UID + transport + default flag) for the picker. */ /** Make the given device (by UID) the system default output. The engine follows * the default, so this moves the app's (and all system) audio to it. */ /** System input (capture) devices. */ /** Read the current engine state. */ /** Toggle global enhancement power. */ /** Set master output volume (linear gain). */ /** Apply a manual 31-band EQ edit. */ /** Configure the bass boost stage. */ /** Configure the spatializer (surround) stage. */ /** Configure the 3D-surround (virtual-speaker) stage. */ /** Configure the room-reverb ("room effects") stage. */ /** Configure the convolution reverb / IR-correction stage. */ /** Configure the multiband compander stage. */ /** Configure the tube-saturation stage. */ /* -------------------------------------------------------------- liveprog */ /** Compile an EEL2-subset script and load it into the chain. * * Rejects with the compile error (`[line:col] message`) and changes nothing — * a script that won't compile leaves whatever was already running in place. */ /** Enable or disable the LiveProg stage without recompiling it. */ /** Load an impulse-response file; returns metadata about what was loaded. */ /* ------------------------------------------------------------ cloud music */ /** The connected cloud accounts + which providers are configured. */ /** Run the OAuth flow for a provider (opens the browser) and add the signed-in * account. Connecting a second account of the same provider adds another. */ /** Forget one account's stored tokens (by account id). */ /** List one cloud folder's contents (subfolders + audio); "" = account root. */ /** Every audio file in an account, flat (all folders), for the Player's unified * library. Mirrors the mobile app's account-wide listing. The listing is * cached on disk per account: by default a cached copy is returned instantly * (with `fromCache: true`); pass `refresh` to re-list from the account and * update the cache. */ /** Every cached *text tag* for an account (no cover art), keyed by file id. * Hydrates the library's titles/artists/albums instantly on launch without * pulling every track's ~100 KB base64 cover into memory — covers resolve * lazily per visible row via {@link cloudTrackCover}. */ /** Read a cloud track's embedded tags (title/artist/album + cover) from the * file's leading bytes. Cached on disk per file, so it's a one-time download. */ /** Read a cloud track's text tags **only** (no cover). Backs the background * library preload: still caches the full metadata on disk (so a later cover * lookup is warm), but never ships the base64 cover over IPC or into the heap. */ /** Resolve just one cloud track's cover art (a `data:` URI), lazily per visible * row — a warm cache hit once the tags preload has downloaded the file. */ /** Stream a cloud file through the enhancement chain. */ /** One track in a cloud crossfade/gapless queue (id + extension hint). */ /** Play a cloud queue gaplessly/crossfading; URLs resolve lazily per track. All * items must belong to the same account (`accountId`). */ /* ---------------------------------------------------------- YouTube Music */ /** Whether we're signed in, and whether yt-dlp/ffmpeg are installed. */ /** Open Google's sign-in window and resolve once a session appears. Rejects * with code `cancelled` (window closed) or `timeout`. */ /** Forget the session and drop the cached listing. */ /** Install whatever YT Music tooling is missing (yt-dlp, ffmpeg) into the * app-managed folder — download, checksum-verify, atomic install; progress * arrives on the `ytmusic-setup-progress` event. Resolves to the fresh * status once everything is in place. */ /** Every track across the account's playlists. Like {@link cloudAllAudio}, the * listing is cached on disk: by default a cached copy returns instantly (with * `fromCache: true`); pass `refresh` to re-list and update the cache. */ /** The mood/genre categories YouTube offers. */ /** One category's shelves. Never cached — Explore is YouTube's live catalog, so * each open is a fresh read (that's the point of browsing it). */ /** The tracks behind one Explore item, ready to queue. A song or video answers * with itself — it already knows everything a queue item needs. */ /** Search YouTube Music's catalog. `filter` is one of * `top | songs | videos | albums | artists | playlists`. * * Answers in the same shape a category page does, so results render through the * same shelves. Never cached: a search is a question about right now. */ /** YouTube's own completions for a partial query. * * Fired per keystroke, so it answers with an empty list rather than rejecting: * a failed suggestion is not worth a word on screen, and the search itself will * report anything that actually matters. */ /** One page of the song radio YT Music derives from `videoId`. */ /** The next radio page; `videoId` is the seed the radio was started from. */ /** An artist's page: top songs, albums, singles, videos, playlists. */ /** A loopback URL for this track's video-only rendition, for a muted `<video>`. * * Video-only and muted is what keeps the enhancement chain in the audio path: * the rendition carries no audio track, so the element can only ever be a * picture. Costs a yt-dlp resolve, so only ask when video is actually turned * on. Rejects when there's nothing playable — treat that as "no video", never * as a playback failure. */ /** Warm the resolved-url cache for a track we expect to play next. * * Resolving is a yt-dlp process start (~5s) and it used to happen only once the * previous track had ended, so the whole cost was audible as the gap between * them. Asked early, it runs under the music instead. * * Fire-and-forget: the result lands in a cache the play path reads anyway, so a * rejection here means nothing — the play path will resolve and report properly * if there's a real problem. Never await it on the critical path. */ /** Warm several upcoming tracks' stream urls (sequential in the backend). * Fire-and-forget; the play path never waits on it. */ /** Warm the *video* rendition so the Video tab opens instantly. Same * fire-and-forget contract as {@link ytmusicPrefetch}; a different resolve into * a different cache. */ /** Stream one track through the enhancement chain. Passing the known length * (seconds) makes the seek bar right from the first frame. */ /** One track in a YouTube Music crossfade/gapless queue. */ /** Play a YT Music queue gaplessly/crossfading; URLs resolve lazily per track * (they're short-lived and IP-pinned, so they can't be resolved up front). */ /** Download a track to this machine and index it into the library; returns the * written path. Progress arrives over {@link onYtDownload}. */ /** Download a track and send it on to a paired phone. */ /** Send any already-local file to a paired phone. */ /** The folder downloads are written to. */ /** Set the download folder; `null` resets it to the default. Returns the * folder now in effect. */ /** Subscribe to download progress. Every download reports on this one event, * keyed by `videoId` (a `link_upload` of a local file keys by its path). */ /* ------------------------------------------------------------- Phone Link */ /** Browse the LAN (~2.5 s) for phones sharing their library. */ /** Phones we've already paired with (silent reconnect). */ /** Start continuous phone discovery — phones arrive over `onPhoneFound`. */ /** Stop continuous phone discovery. */ /** Subscribe to phones as they're discovered on the LAN (live, no polling). */ /** Fires when an already-paired phone (re)appears on the LAN — i.e. it's * reachable now — so its library can be auto-synced into the unified library * without a relaunch. Payload is the device id. */ /** Pair with a phone using the 6-digit PIN it's showing. */ /** Pair with a phone by its address (host:port) + PIN — no mDNS discovery * needed (works when discovery can't see the phone, or across networks). */ /** Forget a paired phone. */ // ------------------------------------------- remote (cross-network) phone link /** What the phone scans to pair across networks. */ /** A paired remote phone's live status. */ /** Open a remote pairing session; returns the QR payload + PIN to display. */ /** Close the open remote pairing session. */ /** Status of every paired remote phone. */ /** (Re)dial all known remote phones; returns the refreshed status list. */ /** Forget a remote phone (drops its tunnel + both stores). */ /** Fires when a remote phone pairs / reconnects — re-scan the library. */ /** Fetch a paired phone's track list. */ /** A track's artwork as a data URI, or null if it has none. */ /** A phone track's lyrics (a `.lrc` the user keeps next to the music, or * embedded lyrics) as raw LRC/plain text, or null if the phone has none. */ /** Stream one track from the phone through the enhancement chain. Passing the * track's known length (seconds) makes the stream seekable and shows its * duration straight away. */ /** One track in a phone crossfade/gapless queue (id + extension). */ /** Play a phone queue gaplessly/crossfading; URLs resolve lazily per track. */ /** Now-playing pushed by a phone casting to this desktop. */ /** Subscribe to cast notifications from a paired phone. */ /** All bundled headphone correction profiles. */ /** Apply a headphone profile; returns it. */ /** Clear the active headphone correction. */ /** List all presets (built-in first, then custom). */ /** Apply a preset to the engine; returns the applied preset. */ /** Save the current curve as a new custom preset. */ /** Update an existing custom preset. */ /** Delete a custom preset. */ /** Decode and play a local file through the chain. */ /** Stream and play an internet radio URL. */ /** Play a list of local files as a gapless/crossfading queue from `start`. */ /** Update gapless + crossfade playback behaviour. */ /** Toggle Data Saver / low-bandwidth streaming mode. */ /** Toggle Autoplay — whether a finished YT Music queue extends itself with radio. */ /** Subscribe to the gapless queue's current track index. */ /** Stop playback. */ /** Pause playback (keeps position). */ /** Resume playback. */ /** Seek to `secs` within the current track. */ /** Capture the default input device through the chain (dev stand-in). */ /** Whether true system-wide capture (a signed virtual device) is installed. */ /** Equalize system-wide audio through the chain: macOS taps + re-renders every * app; Linux/Windows re-route all output through a virtual device. */ /** Stop system-wide equalization and restore normal audio routing. */ /** Whether system-wide equalization is available (macOS tap / Linux PipeWire * or PulseAudio / Windows bundled virtual device). */ /** Per-OS readiness of system-wide EQ for the Settings card. */ /** Per-OS system-EQ readiness (supported / available / driver state) in one call. */ /** Outcome of the free Windows APO setup: installed + attached, reboot to finish. */ /** Install the free Windows APO system-wide EQ backend (one UAC prompt: copies * the DLL, registers it, sets DisableProtectedAudioDG, attaches to the default * endpoint). Requires a reboot to finish. Windows-only. */ /** Remove the APO backend (one UAC prompt). Windows-only. */ /** Re-attach the APO to the current default endpoint if it was detached (a * Windows update or device change). Windows-only. */ /** Runtime state of system-wide EQ. `"recovering"` means a transient failure * (e.g. a macOS tap stall under heavy load, or a device change) is being * recovered from in the background — audio is restored but currently unequalised * — rather than the EQ having silently stopped. */ /** Poll the current runtime state of system-wide EQ (active / recovering / * disabled), so the UI can surface background recovery instead of a silent stall. */ /** Install the bundled Windows virtual-audio driver (prompts for admin via UAC). * No-op on platforms that need no driver. Re-query {@link systemAudioStatus} * afterwards to confirm the device enumerated. */ /** Progress phases emitted (as `system-eq-setup-phase` events) while the * one-click Windows routing setup runs. */ /** Outcome of the one-click Windows routing setup: `ready` = the routing device * is present and system-wide EQ can be enabled now; `needsReboot` = installed, * but Windows must restart before the device appears. */ /** One-click Windows system-EQ setup for builds without the bundled driver: * downloads VB-CABLE from VB-Audio's official server (SHA-256-verified), * silently installs it (one UAC prompt), and waits for the routing device to * enumerate. Emits `system-eq-setup-phase` events while it runs. */ /** Result of the Linux system-audio dependency setup. `alreadyReady`/`installed` * = system EQ is (now) usable; `needsManual` = run `command` yourself (sandbox / * unknown distro / no polkit); `notApplicable` = nothing installable would help * or not Linux; `failed` = the install ran but failed. */ /** Linux: ensure the packages a system-EQ backend needs are installed (e.g. * `pulseaudio-utils` on a PipeWire-less box), installing via the auto-detected * package manager behind one `pkexec` prompt. Runs automatically on launch when * needed; this is the manual retry (ignores a prior decline). Emits * `system-eq-setup-phase` / `system-eq-setup-manual` events. */ /** Set which apps the system-wide EQ tap processes (macOS). Restart the tap * (call `playerPlaySystemAudio` again) for it to take effect if it's running. */ /** Whether the native MilkDrop visualizer sidecar is bundled in this build. */ /** Every bundled `.milk` preset name (file stem), sorted. */ /** Open the visualizer window, streaming audio to it and (optionally) starting * on a given preset. */ /** Switch the open visualizer window to a preset (a `.milk` file stem). */ /** Close the visualizer window. */ /** Whether the visualizer window is currently open. */ /* ----------------------------------------------- in-app visualizer scenes */ /** A selectable in-app (Canvas/WebGL) visualizer. */ /** The registry of in-app visualizer scenes (backend source of truth). */ /** The currently selected scene id (persisted by the backend). */ /** Select a scene; the backend persists it. */ /** Whether audio is currently playing. */ /* ----------------------------------------------------------------- mixer */ /* --------------------------------------------------------------- license */ /* --------------------------------------

nodes.name: lrc.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * LRC lyrics parsing. Handles standard `[mm:ss.xx]` line timestamps (synced), * plain unsynced text, `[ar:]/[ti:]/[al:]/[offset:]` metadata tags, and the * "Enhanced LRC" `<mm:ss.xx>` per-word timing that drives Apple-Music-style * word-by-word highlighting (the full plain text is always kept too, so the UI * works whether or not a source provides word timing). */ const TIMESTAMP = /\[(\d{1,3}):(\d{2})(?:\.(\d{2,3}))?\]/g; const META = /^\[([a-z]+):(.*)\]$/i; // Enhanced word-level timing `<mm:ss.xx>`. const WORD_TIMING = /<\d{1,3}:\d{2}(?:\.\d{2,3})?>/g; const WORD_TOKEN = /<(\d{1,3}):(\d{2})(?:\.(\d{2,3}))?>/g; /** Parse `<mm:ss.xx>word` segments from a line body, or undefined if none. */ /** Index of the active line for `positionMs`, or -1 before the first line. */

nodes.name: LyricWord
nodes.body_text: interface LyricWord { /** Milliseconds into the track when this word starts being sung. */ timeMs: number; text: string; }

nodes.name: LyricLine
nodes.body_text: interface LyricLine { /** Milliseconds into the track, or null for unsynced lines. */ timeMs: number | null; text: string; /** Per-word timing, when the source is Enhanced LRC. */ words?: LyricWord[]; /** Start of the next synced line — the moment this one stops being active. * Lets the UI pace a line-level fill when there's no word timing. */ endMs?: number; }

nodes.name: ParsedLyrics
nodes.body_text: interface ParsedLyrics { lines: LyricLine[]; synced: boolean; /** True when at least one line carries Enhanced-LRC word timing. */ wordSynced: boolean; /** Tag offset in ms (added to every timestamp), from `[offset:]`. */ offsetMs: number; }

nodes.name: toMs
nodes.signature: function toMs(min: string, sec: string, frac: string | undefined): number
nodes.body_text: function toMs(min: string, sec: string, frac: string | undefined): number { const f = frac ?? "0"; const ms = f.length === 2 ? parseInt(f, 10) * 10 : parseInt(f, 10); return (parseInt(min, 10) * 60 + parseInt(sec, 10)) * 1000 + ms; }

nodes.name: parseWords
nodes.body_text: function parseWords(body: string): LyricWord[] | undefined { const tokens = [...body.matchAll(WORD_TOKEN)]; if (tokens.length === 0) return undefined; const words: LyricWord[] = []; for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i++) { const m = tokens[i]!; const from = m.index! + m[0].length; const to = i + 1 < tokens.length ? tokens[i + 1]!.index! : body.length; const text = body.slice(from, to).replace(WORD_TIMING, "").trimEnd(); if (text.trim()) { words.push({ timeMs: toMs(m[1]!, m[2]!, m[3]), text }); } } return words.length ? words : undefined; }

nodes.name: parseLrc
nodes.body_text: function parseLrc(raw: string): ParsedLyrics { const lines: LyricLine[] = []; let synced = false; let wordSynced = false; let offsetMs = 0; for (const rawLine of raw.split("\n")) { const line = rawLine.replace(/\s+$/, ""); if (!line.trim()) continue; const stamps = [...line.matchAll(TIMESTAMP)]; if (stamps.length === 0) { const meta = META.exec(line.trim()); if (meta) { if (meta[1]!.toLowerCase() === "offset") { offsetMs = parseInt(meta[2]!.trim(), 10) || 0; } continue; // metadata tag, not a lyric line } lines.push({ timeMs: null, text: line.trim() }); continue; } // Body = the line minus its `[..]` line stamps; still holds `<..>` words. const body = line.replace(TIMESTAMP, ""); const text = body.replace(WORD_TIMING, "").trim(); if (!text) continue; synced = true; // Word times are absolute, so they're only valid for a single occurrence; // a repeated-chorus line ([00:01][01:30]…) falls back to line-level fill. const words = stamps.length === 1 ? parseWords(body) : undefined; if (words) wordSynced = true; for (const m of stamps) { lines.push({ timeMs: toMs(m[1]!, m[2]!, m[3]), text, words }); } } if (synced) { lines.sort((a, b) => (a.timeMs ?? Infinity) - (b.timeMs ?? Infinity)); // Each synced line ends where the next one begins (for line-level pacing). for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) { if (lines[i]!.timeMs == null) continue; const next = lines[i + 1]; if (next?.timeMs != null) lines[i]!.endMs = next.timeMs; } } return { lines, synced, wordSynced, offsetMs }; }

nodes.name: activeLineIndex
nodes.signature: function activeLineIndex( lines: LyricLine[], positionMs: number, ): number
nodes.body_text: function activeLineIndex( lines: LyricLine[], positionMs: number, ): number { let lo = 0; let hi = lines.length - 1; let result = -1; while (lo <= hi) { const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1; const t = lines[mid]!.timeMs; if (t == null || t > positionMs) { hi = mid - 1; } else { result = mid; lo = mid + 1; } } return result; }

nodes.name: platform.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Platform helpers — window chrome, and the few places copy must name the OS. * * The window uses `titleBarStyle: "Overlay"` (see tauri.conf.json), which on * macOS draws the traffic-light buttons floating over our content's top-left * corner. We reserve a safe inset at the top of the chrome so nothing sits * under them — the desktop equivalent of a Flutter `SafeArea` top inset — and * make that strip draggable. Overlay is macOS-only; other platforms keep their * native title bar and need no inset. */ export const isMac = typeof navigator !== "undefined" && /Mac/i.test(navigator.userAgent); export const isWindows = typeof navigator !== "undefined" && /Win/i.test(navigator.userAgent); /** Which OS we're on, for copy that differs per platform (setup instructions, * what to call this machine). Everything that isn't macOS or Windows is * treated as Linux — the third target this app ships for. */ export const HOST_OS: HostOs = isMac ? "mac" : isWindows ? "windows" : "linux"; /** What to call this machine in UI copy. */ export const THIS_COMPUTER = HOST_OS === "mac" ? "this Mac" : HOST_OS === "windows" ? "this PC" : "this computer"; /** * Height (px) of the traffic-light zone reserved at the top of the window * chrome on macOS. Matches the standard macOS title-bar height so the buttons * clear the content below. Zero elsewhere. */ export const TITLEBAR_INSET = isMac ? 28 : 0;

nodes.name: reducedMotion.ts
nodes.body_text: /** * Whether the user asked for less motion. * * Read once at import, matching the existing call sites. The CSS blanket rule * in styles/index.css already collapses animation/transition timing; this is * for JS-driven motion that CSS can't reach. */ export const prefersReducedMotion: boolean = (() => { try { return window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches; } catch { return false; } })();

""; const rustIds = [...block.matchAll(/"([^"]+)"/g)].map((m) => m[1]); expect(rustIds).toEqual(SETTINGS_SECTIONS.map((s) => s.id)); }); });

nodes.body_text: /** * Canonical front-end types. * * These mirror the serde payloads in `crates/hm-core` exactly — same field * names (camelCase), same shapes. They are one contract expressed twice; when a * Rust type changes, change it here too. */ /** Number of graphic-EQ bands (ISO one-third-octave, 20 Hz–20 kHz). */ export const BAND_COUNT = 31; /** ISO one-third-octave nominal center frequencies (Hz), mirroring Rust. */ export const ISO_CENTERS_HZ: readonly number[] = [ 20, 25, 31.5, 40, 50, 63, 80, 100, 125, 160, 200, 250, 315, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1000, 1250, 1600, 2000, 2500, 3150, 4000, 5000, 6300, 8000, 10000, 12500, 16000, 20000, ]; /** On/off state for each virtual loudspeaker in the 3D Surround ring. */ /** Room reverb ("room effects"). Scalars are 0–1 except preDelay (ms). */ /** Convolution (impulse-response) stage. Heavy IR data lives engine-side. */ /** Multiband compander (10-band LR compressor/expander); global params. */ /** Tube-style analog saturation (4× oversampled). */ /** A built-in room reverb preset (mirrors the Hype mobile presets). */ export const ROOM_PRESETS: readonly RoomPreset[] = [ { id: "none", name: "None", roomSize: 0.0, decay: 0.0, damping: 0.0, preDelay: 0, diffusion: 0.0, wetDry: 0.0 }, { id: "small", name: "Small Room", roomSize: 0.2, decay: 0.25, damping: 0.6, preDelay: 3, diffusion: 0.5, wetDry: 0.25 }, { id: "medium", name: "Medium Room", roomSize: 0.4, decay: 0.4, damping: 0.45, preDelay: 8, diffusion: 0.55, wetDry: 0.3 }, { id: "large", name: "Large Room", roomSize: 0.6, decay: 0.55, damping: 0.35, preDelay: 15, diffusion: 0.6, wetDry: 0.35 }, { id: "hall", name: "Hall", roomSize: 0.75, decay: 0.65, damping: 0.3, preDelay: 25, diffusion: 0.65, wetDry: 0.4 }, { id: "cathedral", name: "Cathedral", roomSize: 0.9, decay: 0.8, damping: 0.5, preDelay: 40, diffusion: 0.7, wetDry: 0.4 }, { id: "plate", name: "Plate", roomSize: 0.35, decay: 0.5, damping: 0.1, preDelay: 2, diffusion: 0.8, wetDry: 0.35 }, { id: "studio", name: "Studio", roomSize: 0.15, decay: 0.2, damping: 0.65, preDelay: 2, diffusion: 0.4, wetDry: 0.2 }, { id: "chamber", name: "Chamber", roomSize: 0.45, decay: 0.45, damping: 0.35, preDelay: 12, diffusion: 0.55, wetDry: 0.3 }, { id: "arena", name: "Arena", roomSize: 1.0, decay: 0.9, damping: 0.55, preDelay: 60, diffusion: 0.65, wetDry: 0.35 }, { id: "concert", name: "Concert", roomSize: 0.8, decay: 0.7, damping: 0.35, preDelay: 35, diffusion: 0.65, wetDry: 0.4 }, ]; /** Queue-playback behaviour: gapless transitions + crossfade between tracks. */ /** How the macOS system-wide EQ tap selects which apps to process. */ /** Per-app selection for the system-wide EQ (mirrors `hm_core::SystemEqScope`). */ /** A named snapshot of the entire DSP enhancement chain. Mirrors `ChainPreset` in hm-core. */ /** A country in the Africa radio browser. */ /** A television channel from the world TV directory (iptv-org). The `url` is a * video stream (usually HLS) played by the native mpv window. */ /** A browsable TV category (iptv-org bucket). */ /** A country in the world TV browser. */ /** The server's license verdict (from the Management API). */ /** `GET /me/entitlements`, as returned by the `account_entitlements` command. */ /** The signed-in account + its current entitlement. */ /** One page of library tracks. `tracks` is the reachable subset; `scanned` is * the DB rows read before availability filtering, so the loader advances its * offset correctly even when an unplugged drive's rows are hidden. */ /** Now-playing metadata extracted from the decoded track (tags + cover art). */ /** How an output device is attached — drives the picker icon + speaker/headphone hint. */ /** A selectable system output device (from `audio_output_devices`). */ /** The error shape every Tauri command rejects with. */ /** One connected cloud account. The same provider can have several (e.g. two * Google accounts), so `id` — not `provider` — is the identity used to list, * stream, and cache. `label` is the account's email / display name. */ /** A folder or audio file inside a cloud account (browsed folder-by-folder). */ /** A flat account-wide audio listing. `fromCache` is true when it was served * from the on-disk cache (so the caller can refresh it in the background). */ /** A cloud track's embedded tags, read from the file's leading bytes. */ /* ---------------------------------------------------------- YouTube Music */ /** One of the signed-in account's playlists. */ /** One track inside a playlist. Unlike cloud files, YT Music hands us the tags * up front, so there's no metadata pass — the listing is already complete. */ /** One page of a song radio: similar tracks plus the token for the next page. * A missing token is rare — radio panels normally chain forever. */ /** Whether yt-dlp — which resolves every stream and download — is installed. * Playlists browse without it; only playback and downloads need it. */ /** A row of Explore categories ("Moods & moments", "Genres", …). */ /** One shelf on a category, search or artist page ("Songs", "Albums", …). */ /** What an {@link ExploreItem} is. Cards name a page to open; `song`/`video` * name something to play. */ /** A thing in Explore — browsable or playable. Unlike library tracks these are * never cached or merged into the library: Explore is YouTube's live catalog. */ /** A whole-library listing. `fromCache` mirrors {@link CloudAudioPage}: true * means it was served from the on-disk cache, so refresh it behind the UI. */ /** Progress of a download (to this machine or on to a phone), per `videoId`. */ /* ------------------------------------------------------------- Phone Link */ /** A phone discovered on the LAN, or one we've already paired with. */ /** One track in a paired phone's library. */ /** One headphone in the bundled AutoEQ index (mirrors `hm_core::AutoEqEntry`). */

nodes.name: useTrackArtwork.ts
nodes.body_text: import { useEffect, useState } from "react"; import { cloudTrackCover, libraryArtwork, linkArtwork } from "@/lib/ipc"; /** * Where a track's cover art comes from. Local files read embedded art by path; * phone tracks fetch it from the paired device; cloud tracks fetch it lazily * from the metadata cache (only the on-screen rows, so a big library never holds * thousands of covers in memory). YouTube Music tracks always arrive with their * thumbnail URL in `cover`, so they resolve with no fetch at all. */ /** * Lazily resolve a track's cover art (a `data:` URI), source-aware. Results * (including "no art" = `null`) are cached per track for the session and * in-flight requests de-duplicated, so scrolling a huge grid/list stays cheap. */ const cache = new Map<string, string | null>(); const inFlight = new Map<string, Promise<string | null>>(); // Bound the cache so covers don't accumulate unbounded as you scroll a huge // library over a session (each is a ~100 KB `data:` URI). A cap well above the // on-screen working set means back-and-forth scrolling still hits cache; only // long-gone rows are evicted (oldest-inserted first — a visible row was just // inserted, so it's never the one dropped). ~400 covers ≈ a few tens of MB max. const CACHE_CAP = 400; /** The track's cover art data URI, or `null` while loading / if it has none. */

nodes.name: ArtSource
nodes.body_text: interface ArtSource { /** Stable cache key (the track's uid). */ key: string; source: "local" | "phone" | "cloud" | "ytmusic"; /** Local file path. */ path?: string | null; /** Phone device + track ids. */ deviceId?: string; trackId?: string; /** Whether the phone reports embedded art (skip the fetch if false). */ hasArt?: boolean; /** Cloud account + file ids + name, to resolve the cover lazily on demand. */ cloudAccountId?: string; cloudFileId?: string; cloudName?: string; /** Already-resolved cover (a `data:` URI, or a YT Music thumbnail URL), e.g. * the now-playing track after decode — used directly, skipping any fetch. */ cover?: string | null; }

nodes.name: cacheSet
nodes.signature: function cacheSet(key: string, value: string | null): void
nodes.body_text: function cacheSet(key: string, value: string | null): void { cache.set(key, value); while (cache.size > CACHE_CAP) { const oldest = cache.keys().next().value; if (oldest === undefined) break; cache.delete(oldest); } }

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.body_text: function resolve(art: ArtSource): Promise<string | null> { // A cover already in hand (e.g. the now-playing track post-decode) wins. if (art.cover) return Promise.resolve(art.cover); if (art.source === "local" && art.path) { return libraryArtwork(art.path); } if (art.source === "phone" && art.hasArt && art.deviceId && art.trackId) { return linkArtwork(art.deviceId, art.trackId); } if (art.source === "cloud" && art.cloudAccountId && art.cloudFileId) { return cloudTrackCover( art.cloudAccountId, art.cloudFileId, art.cloudName ?? "", ); } return Promise.resolve(null); }

nodes.name: fetchArtwork
nodes.body_text: function fetchArtwork(art: ArtSource): Promise<string | null> { const existing = inFlight.get(art.key); if (existing) return existing; const p = resolve(art) .then((v) => v ?? null) .catch(() => null) .then((v) => { cacheSet(art.key, v); inFlight.delete(art.key); return v; }); inFlight.set(art.key, p); return p; }

nodes.name: useTrackArtwork
nodes.signature: function useTrackArtwork(art: ArtSource | null | undefined): string | null
nodes.body_text: function useTrackArtwork(art: ArtSource | null | undefined): string | null { const key = art?.key ?? null; const [cover, setCover] = useState<string | null>(() => key ? (cache.get(key) ?? null) : null, ); useEffect(() => { if (!art || !key) { setCover(null); return; } if (cache.has(key)) { setCover(cache.get(key)!); return; } // Defer slightly: rows scrolled straight past unmount before this fires, so // a fast scroll never kicks off hundreds of fetches. Cached/in-flight keys // resolve immediately via the dedup above. let active = true; const timer = window.setTimeout(() => { void fetchArtwork(art).then((v) => { if (active) setCover(v); }); }, 140); return () => { active = false; window.clearTimeout(timer); }; // Only re-resolve when the track changes (art content is stable per key). // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps }, [key]); return cover; }

Outside Tauri (unit tests, a plain browser) there is no * window to ask, and that context behaves like the main window. */ export const WINDOW_LABEL: string = (() => { try { return getCurrentWebviewWindow().label; } catch { return MAIN_WINDOW; } })(); export const isMainWindow = WINDOW_LABEL === MAIN_WINDOW; export const isSettingsWindow = WINDOW_LABEL === SETTINGS_WINDOW;

nodes.name: windowSync.test.ts
nodes.body_text: import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"; import { createStore, type StoreApi } from "zustand/vanilla"; import { applySynced, diffSynced, snapshotSynced, type SyncSpec } from "./windowSync"; /** * The Settings window and the main window are separate JS contexts. These * tests load one copy of `windowSync` per simulated window (each with its own * label) on an in-memory event bus that delivers asynchronously, like Tauri. */ const engineSpec: SyncSpec<Engine> = { keys: ["nowPlaying"], merge: { state: ["playback", "scope"] }, }; afterEach(() => { vi.doUnmock("@/lib/windowLabel"); vi.doUnmock("@tauri-apps/api/event"); }); describe("diff / snapshot / apply", () => { it("diffs only synced keys and only the listed fields of merge keys", () => { const prev = engine().getState(); const next: Engine = { ...prev, meters: 9, state: { ...prev.state, eq: [3, 3], playback: { gapless: false, crossfadeSecs: 0 } }, }; expect(diffSynced(prev, next, engineSpec)).toEqual({ state: { playback: { gapless: false, crossfadeSecs: 0 } }, }); expect(diffSynced(prev, { ...prev, meters: 1 }, engineSpec)).toBeNull(); }); it("snapshots every synced key and nothing else", () => { const s = engine({ scope: "only" }).getState(); expect(snapshotSynced(s, engineSpec)).toEqual({ nowPlaying: null, state: { playback: { gapless: true, crossfadeSecs: 0 }, scope: "only" }, }); }); it("merges merge keys into the receiver's object", () => { const s = engine({ eq: [5, 5] }).getState(); const out = applySynced(s, { state: { scope: "except" } }, engineSpec); expect(out.state).toEqual({ ...s.state, scope: "except" }); }); }); describe("two windows", () => { it("mirrors a change and never echoes it back", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const mainStore = engine(); await main.syncStore(mainStore, "engine", engineSpec); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); const settingsStore = engine(); await settings.syncStore(settingsStore, "engine", engineSpec); settingsStore.setState((s) => ({ state: { ...s.state, playback: { gapless: true, crossfadeSecs: 6 } }, })); await flush(); expect(mainStore.getState().state.playback.crossfadeSecs).toBe(6); const syncs = bus.sent.filter((m) => m.event === "hm://sync"); expect(syncs).toHaveLength(1); // main applied it without re-emitting expect(syncs[0]?.from).toBe("settings"); }); it("does not overwrite fields the receiver changed meanwhile, or unsynced ones", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const mainStore = engine(); await main.syncStore(mainStore, "engine", engineSpec); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); const settingsStore = engine(); await settings.syncStore(settingsStore, "engine", engineSpec); // Main drags the EQ (unsynced) and changes scope; Settings changes playback. mainStore.setState((s) => ({ state: { ...s.state, eq: [4, 4], scope: "only" } })); settingsStore.setState((s) => ({ state: { ...s.state, playback: { gapless: false, crossfadeSecs: 0 } }, })); await flush(); expect(mainStore.getState().state).toEqual({ eq: [4, 4], scope: "only", playback: { gapless: false, crossfadeSecs: 0 }, }); expect(settingsStore.getState().state.scope).toBe("only"); expect(settingsStore.getState().state.eq).toEqual([0, 0]); }); it("starts a new window from the other window's state, not its defaults", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const mainStore = engine({ scope: "except" }); mainStore.setState((s) => ({ nowPlaying: "Song", state: { ...s.state, playback: { gapless: false, crossfadeSecs: 8 } }, })); await main.syncStore(mainStore, "engine", engineSpec); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); const settingsStore = engine(); await settings.syncStore(settingsStore, "engine", engineSpec); await settings.requestSnapshot(); await flush(); expect(settingsStore.getState().nowPlaying).toBe("Song"); expect(settingsStore.getState().state.playback).toEqual({ gapless: false, crossfadeSecs: 8 }); expect(settingsStore.getState().state.scope).toBe("except"); // The snapshot went only to the window that asked. const snap = bus.sent.find((m) => (m.payload as { snapshot?: boolean })?.snapshot); expect(snap?.to).toBe("settings"); }); it("a late snapshot does not roll back what the new window already changed", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const mainStore = engine({ scope: "only" }); await main.syncStore(mainStore, "engine", engineSpec); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); const settingsStore = engine(); await settings.syncStore(settingsStore, "engine", engineSpec); // Not awaited: the user flips gapless in Settings before the snapshot lands. void settings.requestSnapshot(); settingsStore.setState((s) => ({ state: { ...s.state, playback: { gapless: false, crossfadeSecs: 0 } }, })); await flush(); expect(settingsStore.getState().state.playback.gapless).toBe(false); expect(settingsStore.getState().state.scope).toBe("only"); expect(mainStore.getState().state.playback.gapless).toBe(false); }); it("keeps stores with different names apart", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const a = createStore(() => ({ v: 1 })); await main.syncStore(a, "a", { keys: ["v"] }); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); const b = createStore(() => ({ v: 1 })); await settings.syncStore(b, "b", { keys: ["v"] }); b.setState({ v: 2 }); await flush(); expect(a.getState().v).toBe(1); }); it("stops syncing after the returned function runs", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const mainStore = createStore(() => ({ v: 1 })); const stop = await main.syncStore(mainStore, "s", { keys: ["v"] }); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); const settingsStore = createStore(() => ({ v: 1 })); await settings.syncStore(settingsStore, "s", { keys: ["v"] }); stop(); settingsStore.setState({ v: 3 }); await flush(); expect(mainStore.getState().v).toBe(1); }); }); describe("forwarding to the main window", () => { it("runs a forwarded action in main with its arguments", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const play = vi.fn(); await main.serveMainInvocations({ "engine.playCloudList": play }); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); settings.forwardToMain("engine.playCloudList", [[{ id: "x" }], 0]); await flush(); expect(play).toHaveBeenCalledWith([{ id: "x" }], 0); }); it("ignores unknown actions and survives a throwing or rejecting handler", async () => { const bus = new Bus(); const main = await loadWindow(bus, "main"); const ok = vi.fn(); await main.serveMainInvocations({ boom: () => { throw new Error("x"); }, reject: () => Promise.reject(new Error("y")), ok, }); const settings = await loadWindow(bus, "settings"); settings.forwardToMain("nope", []); settings.forwardToMain("boom", []); settings.forwardToMain("reject", []); settings.forwardToMain("ok", [1]); await flush(); expect(ok).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1); }); });

nodes.name: Listener
nodes.signature: type Listener = { label: string; event: string; cb: (e: { payload: unknown }) => void };
nodes.body_text: type Listener = { label: string; event: string; cb: (e: { payload: unknown }) => void };

nodes.name: Bus
nodes.body_text: class Bus { listeners: Listener[] = []; sent: { from: string; event: string; to?: string; payload: unknown }[] = []; api(label: string) { const deliver = (event: string, payload: unknown, to?: string) => { this.sent.push({ from: label, event, to, payload }); const targets = this.listeners.filter( (l) => l.event === event && (to === undefined || l.label === to), ); queueMicrotask(() => targets.forEach((l) => l.cb({ payload }))); }; return { emit: async (event: string, payload: unknown) => deliver(event, payload), emitTo: async (to: string, event: string, payload: unknown) => deliver(event, payload, to), listen: async (event: string, cb: Listener["cb"]) => { const l = { label, event, cb }; this.listeners.push(l); return () => { this.listeners = this.listeners.filter((x) => x !== l); }; }, }; } }

nodes.name: windowSync.ts
nodes.body_text: import { emit, emitTo, listen } from "@tauri-apps/api/event"; import type { StoreApi } from "zustand"; import { MAIN_WINDOW, WINDOW_LABEL } from "@/lib/windowLabel"; /** * Keeps chosen Zustand state identical in every app window. * * Each Tauri window is its own JS context with its own store instances, so the * Settings window and the main window would drift apart: a theme picked in * Settings wouldn't reach the main window until a relaunch, and a Settings * window opened with default engine state would send those defaults back to * Rust (`setPlayback` sends gapless and crossfade together). So: * * - a change to a synced key is emitted as just the changed keys, stamped with * the sender's label; other windows apply it without re-emitting; * - a window that opens asks the others for a snapshot, so it starts from their * live state rather than whatever localStorage held when its modules loaded; * - persistence stays where it was: the window where the user acted writes its * localStorage keys, receivers don't write again. * * Actions that drive the main window's player or library (start a queue, * re-sync the phone) must run there, not be mirrored: see {@link forwardToMain}. */ export const SYNC_EVENT = "hm://sync"; export const SYNC_REQUEST_EVENT = "hm://sync-request"; export const MAIN_INVOKE_EVENT = "hm://main-invoke"; /** The synced keys that differ between `prev` and `next`, or null if none. */ /** Every synced key of `state`, for a snapshot. */ /** The partial state that applies `patch` to `state` (merge keys merged in). */ /** Patch paths (`key` or `key.field`), to remember what changed locally. */ /** `patch` without the paths in `skip`; null if nothing is left. */ /** Set once this window has asked the others for a snapshot. */ let awaitingSnapshot = false; /** * Mirror `spec`'s keys of `store` across windows under `name`. Resolves once * the listeners are registered (call {@link requestSnapshot} after that). * Returns a function that stops syncing. */ /** * Ask the other windows for their synced state. Call once, after every * {@link syncStore} in this window has resolved. */ /** * Run `action` in the main window. For actions whose effects live in the main * window's stores (starting a queue that the now-playing bar shows, re-syncing * the phone library the Library view renders): mirroring their results would * be both incomplete and racy, so the main window does the work itself. */ /** In the main window: carry out actions other windows forward. */ /** Test-only: forget a pending snapshot request. */

nodes.name: Patch
nodes.body_text: type Patch = Record<string, unknown>;

nodes.name: SyncMessage
nodes.body_text: interface SyncMessage { store: string; from: string; /** A full snapshot answering a window that just opened, not a change. */ snapshot?: boolean; patch: Patch; }

nodes.name: SyncSpec
nodes.body_text: interface SyncSpec<S> { /** Top-level keys mirrored whole. Compared by identity, as Zustand sets do. */ keys?: readonly (keyof S & string)[]; /** * Object-valued keys mirrored field by field: only the listed fields are * compared and merged, so one window can't overwrite fields another window * changed in the meantime (the engine's `state`). */ merge?: { readonly [K in keyof S & string]?: readonly string[] }; }

nodes.name: Obj
nodes.body_text: type Obj = Record<string, unknown>;

nodes.name: asObj
nodes.body_text: asObj = (v: unknown): Obj => (v && typeof v === "object" ? (v as Obj) : {})

nodes.name: diffSynced
nodes.signature: function diffSynced<S extends object>(prev: S, next: S, spec: SyncSpec<S>): Patch | null
nodes.body_text: function diffSynced<S extends object>(prev: S, next: S, spec: SyncSpec<S>): Patch | null { const patch: Patch = {}; const p = prev as Obj; const n = next as Obj; for (const key of spec.keys ?? []) { if (!Object.is(p[key], n[key])) patch[key] = n[key]; } for (const [key, fields] of Object.entries(spec.merge ?? {}) as [string, readonly string[]][]) { if (Object.is(p[key], n[key])) continue; const before = asObj(p[key]); const after = asObj(n[key]); const changed: Obj = {}; for (const f of fields) { if (!Object.is(before[f], after[f])) changed[f] = after[f]; } if (Object.keys(changed).length) patch[key] = changed; } return Object.keys(patch).length ? patch : null; }

nodes.name: snapshotSynced
nodes.signature: function snapshotSynced<S extends object>(state: S, spec: SyncSpec<S>): Patch
nodes.body_text: function snapshotSynced<S extends object>(state: S, spec: SyncSpec<S>): Patch { const s = state as Obj; const patch: Patch = {}; for (const key of spec.keys ?? []) patch[key] = s[key]; for (const [key, fields] of Object.entries(spec.merge ?? {}) as [string, readonly string[]][]) { const value = asObj(s[key]); const picked: Obj = {}; for (const f of fields) picked[f] = value[f]; patch[key] = picked; } return patch; }

nodes.name: applySynced
nodes.signature: function applySynced<S extends object>(state: S, patch: Patch, spec: SyncSpec<S>): Partial<S>
nodes.body_text: function applySynced<S extends object>(state: S, patch: Patch, spec: SyncSpec<S>): Partial<S> { const s = state as Obj; const merge = (spec.merge ?? {}) as Record<string, readonly string[] | undefined>; const out: Obj = {}; for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(patch)) { out[key] = merge[key] ? { ...asObj(s[key]), ...asObj(value) } : value; } return out as Partial<S>; }

nodes.name: paths
nodes.signature: function paths(patch: Patch, spec: { merge?: object }): string[]
nodes.body_text: function paths(patch: Patch, spec: { merge?: object }): string[] { const merge = (spec.merge ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>; return Object.entries(patch).flatMap(([key, value]) => merge[key] ? Object.keys(asObj(value)).map((f) => `${key}.${f}`) : [key], ); }

nodes.name: without
nodes.signature: function without(patch: Patch, skip: ReadonlySet<string>, spec: { merge?: object }): Patch | null
nodes.body_text: function without(patch: Patch, skip: ReadonlySet<string>, spec: { merge?: object }): Patch | null { const merge = (spec.merge ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>; const out: Patch = {}; for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(patch)) { if (merge[key]) { const kept = Object.fromEntries( Object.entries(asObj(value)).filter(([f]) => !skip.has(`${key}.${f}`)), ); if (Object.keys(kept).length) out[key] = kept; } else if (!skip.has(key)) { out[key] = value; } } return Object.keys(out).length ? out : null; }

nodes.name: syncStore
nodes.signature: async function syncStore<S extends object>( store: StoreApi<S>, name: string, spec: SyncSpec<S>, ): Promise<() => void>
nodes.body_text: async function syncStore<S extends object>( store: StoreApi<S>, name: string, spec: SyncSpec<S>, ): Promise<() => void> { // Set while applying another window's change, so it isn't sent back. let applying = false; let snapshotApplied = false; // Paths the user changed here before the snapshot arrived; the snapshot must // not roll them back. const changedEarly = new Set<string>(); const unsubscribe = store.subscribe((next, prev) => { if (applying) return; const patch = diffSynced(prev, next, spec); if (!patch) return; if (awaitingSnapshot && !snapshotApplied) paths(patch, spec).forEach((p) => changedEarly.add(p)); const message: SyncMessage = { store: name, from: WINDOW_LABEL, patch }; void emit(SYNC_EVENT, message).catch(() => {}); }); const apply = (patch: Patch) => { applying = true; try { store.setState((state) => applySynced(state, patch, spec)); } finally { applying = false; } }; const unlistenSync = await listen<SyncMessage>(SYNC_EVENT, ({ payload }) => { if (payload.store !== name || payload.from === WINDOW_LABEL) return; if (payload.snapshot) { if (snapshotApplied) return; snapshotApplied = true; const patch = without(payload.patch, changedEarly, spec); if (patch) apply(patch); return; } apply(payload.patch); }); const unlistenRequest = await listen<{ from: string }>(SYNC_REQUEST_EVENT, ({ payload }) => { if (payload.from === WINDOW_LABEL) return; const message: SyncMessage = { store: name, from: WINDOW_LABEL, snapshot: true, patch: snapshotSynced(store.getState(), spec), }; void emitTo(payload.from, SYNC_EVENT, message).catch(() => {}); }); return () => { unsubscribe(); unlistenSync(); unlistenRequest(); }; }

nodes.name: apply
nodes.body_text: apply = (patch: Patch) => { applying = true; try { store.setState((state) => applySynced(state, patch, spec)); } finally { applying = false; } }

nodes.name: requestSnapshot
nodes.body_text: async function requestSnapshot(): Promise<void> { awaitingSnapshot = true; await emit(SYNC_REQUEST_EVENT, { from: WINDOW_LABEL }); }

nodes.name: MainInvocation

nodes.name: forwardToMain
nodes.signature: function forwardToMain(action: string, args: unknown[]): void
nodes.body_text: function forwardToMain(action: string, args: unknown[]): void { const message: MainInvocation = { action, args }; void emitTo(MAIN_WINDOW, MAIN_INVOKE_EVENT, message).catch(() => {}); }

nodes.name: serveMainInvocations
nodes.signature: function serveMainInvocations( handlers: Readonly<Record<string, (...args: never[]) => unknown>>, ): Promise<() => void>
nodes.body_text: function serveMainInvocations( handlers: Readonly<Record<string, (...args: never[]) => unknown>>, ): Promise<() => void> { return listen<MainInvocation>(MAIN_INVOKE_EVENT, ({ payload }) => { const handler = handlers[payload.action] as ((...args: unknown[]) => unknown) | undefined; if (!handler) return; try { void Promise.resolve(handler(...payload.args)).catch(() => {}); } catch { // A forwarded action failing must not take the listener down. } }); }

nodes.body_text: import { StrictMode } from "react"; import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client"; import { App } from "@/app/App"; import { SessionGate } from "@/app/SessionGate"; import { OnboardingGate } from "@/app/OnboardingGate"; import { IntroSplash } from "@/components/IntroSplash"; import { Providers } from "@/app/providers"; import { startMainWindowSync, startSettingsWindowSync } from "@/app/windowSyncSetup"; import { SettingsWindow } from "@/features/settings/window/SettingsWindow"; import { isSettingsWindow } from "@/lib/windowLabel"; import "@/styles/index.css"; const rootEl = document.getElementById("root"); if (!rootEl) { throw new Error("Root element #root not found in index.html"); } const root = createRoot(rootEl); /** Settings starts from the main window's live state, but never waits on it forever. */ const SETTINGS_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500; if (isSettingsWindow) { // The Settings window runs none of the main window's global effects // (Providers, gates, App): they would double-publish Hype Connect state, // re-drain open-files, re-resume system EQ and so on. await Promise.race([ startSettingsWindowSync().catch(() => {}), new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, SETTINGS_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS)), ]); root.render( <StrictMode> <SettingsWindow /> </StrictMode> ); } else { startMainWindowSync(); root.render( <StrictMode> <Providers> <OnboardingGate> <SessionGate> <App /> </SessionGate> </OnboardingGate> <IntroSplash /> </Providers> </StrictMode> ); }

nodes.body_text: import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"; import { itemMeta, radioItem, reconcileDuration, ytmusicItem } from "@/stores/engine"; import type { YtTrack } from "@/lib/types"; describe("ytmusicItem", () => { it("maps a track onto a ytmusic queue item", () => { expect(ytmusicItem(track())).toEqual({ id: "vid1", source: "ytmusic", title: "Song", artist: "Artist", album: "Album", durationSecs: 210, cover: "https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vid1/hq.jpg", ytTrack: track(), }); }); it("keys the item by videoId — that's what playback resolves with", () => { expect(ytmusicItem(track({ videoId: "abc" })).id).toBe("abc"); }); it("carries the thumbnail as the cover, so the card needs no art fetch", () => { expect(ytmusicItem(track({ thumbnail: "https://x/y.jpg" })).cover).toBe( "https://x/y.jpg", ); // No thumbnail must stay null (not undefined) — the Artwork gradient // fallback keys off a falsy cover. expect(ytmusicItem(track({ thumbnail: null })).cover).toBeNull(); }); it("passes null tags through rather than inventing placeholders", () => { const item = ytmusicItem(track({ artist: null, album: null, durationSecs: null })); expect(item.artist).toBeNull(); expect(item.album).toBeNull(); expect(item.durationSecs).toBeNull(); }); it("keeps the source payload so the queue can resolve the stream", () => { // startPlayback reads `ytTrack.videoId` off the queue, not `id`. expect(ytmusicItem(track()).ytTrack?.videoId).toBe("vid1"); }); }); describe("itemMeta", () => { /** The sidebar's now-playing card renders `nowPlayingMeta.cover`. This used to * hardcode null, so a YT Music track sat on its gradient forever: the engine * can only supply art it decodes from the file, and googlevideo streams a * bare DASH audio track with no embedded tags. The thumbnail was on the item * the whole time. */ it("carries the item's own cover", () => { expect(itemMeta(item()).cover).toBe("https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vid1/hq.jpg"); }); it("passes the item's tags through", () => { expect(itemMeta(item())).toEqual({ title: "Song", artist: "Artist", album: "Album", cover: "https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vid1/hq.jpg", }); }); /** A local file has no cover on the item — its art is decoded from the file * later, so null here is correct and must stay null (not undefined). */ it("is null when the item has no cover of its own", () => { expect(itemMeta({ ...item(), cover: null }).cover).toBeNull(); const { cover: _drop, ...noCover } = item(); expect(itemMeta(noCover).cover).toBeNull(); }); }); describe("radioItem", () => { it("is a ytmusic queue item marked auto-added — the queue UI badges it", () => { expect(radioItem(track())).toEqual({ ...ytmusicItem(track()), autoAdded: true }); }); }); describe("reconcileDuration", () => { /** The bug this exists to fix: a streamed track's engine-reported total * grows from ~1s as it downloads/decodes. Naively adopting it every tick * made the seek bar's total visibly count up on every streamed track. */ it("trusts the item's known duration while the engine's total is still a growing partial", () => { expect(reconcileDuration(210, 1, null)).toBe(210); expect(reconcileDuration(210, 90, null)).toBe(210); expect(reconcileDuration(210, 209, null)).toBe(210); }); it("adopts the engine's total once it reaches or exceeds the item's", () => { expect(reconcileDuration(210, 210, null)).toBe(210); expect(reconcileDuration(210, 211, null)).toBe(211); }); it("uses the engine's total when the item never had one (a local file, or unknown tags)", () => { expect(reconcileDuration(null, 180, null)).toBe(180); }); it("falls back to the previous duration when neither the item nor this tick's engine value has one", () => { expect(reconcileDuration(null, null, 180)).toBe(180); expect(reconcileDuration(null, null, null)).toBeNull(); }); it("keeps a settled duration if a later tick's engine value briefly drops out (item has none of its own)", () => { // Mirrors calling reconcileDuration tick-over-tick with the previous // return value threaded back in as `prevDuration`. const afterEngineReports = reconcileDuration(null, 180, null); expect(afterEngineReports).toBe(180); expect(reconcileDuration(null, null, afterEngineReports)).toBe(180); }); });

A queue is always built from a * single source (a library list, a phone's library, or one cloud folder), so * every item shares the same `source`. */ const defaultEngineState: EngineState = { power: true, masterVolume: 1, eq: { enabled: true, preGain: 0, bands: Array<number>(BAND_COUNT).fill(0) }, bass: { enabled: false, amount: 0, harmonics: false, adaptive: false }, spatializer: { enabled: false, amount: 0.5, mode: "crossfeed" }, surround3d: { enabled: false, intensity: 0.5, subwoofer: 0.25, speakers: { frontL: true, frontR: true, sideL: true, sideR: true, surroundL: true, surroundR: true, }, }, room: { enabled: false, roomSize: 0.4, decay: 0.4, damping: 0.45, preDelay: 8, diffusion: 0.55, wetDry: 0.3, activePresetId: null, }, convolver: { enabled: false, wetDry: 1.0, irGainDb: 0.0, irId: null, irName: null, irSeconds: 0.0, irTruncated: false, }, compander: { enabled: false, thresholdDb: -18.0, ratio: 2.5, kneeDb: 8.0, attackMs: 15.0, releaseMs: 45.0, makeupDb: 0.0, gateDb: -70.0, expanderRatio: 2.0, }, saturation: { enabled: false, drive: 0.3, mix: 1.0 }, script: { enabled: false, source: "" }, headphone: { enabled: false, preamp: 0, bands: [] }, output: { gainDb: 0, limiterEnabled: true, ceilingDb: -0.3 }, playback: { gapless: true, crossfadeSecs: 0, dataSaver: false, autoplay: true }, systemEqScope: { mode: "all", apps: [] }, activePresetId: null, activeProfileId: null, }; const idleMeters: MeterFrame = { peak: [0, 0], rms: [0, 0] }; // A single shared "no gain reduction" compander meter row. Re-used as a stable // reference across idle frames so the meter doesn't re-render 30×/s for zeros. const IDLE_COMPANDER_GR: number[] = new Array<number>(10).fill(0); /* --------------------------------------------------------------- queue items */ /** A radio pick: the same ytmusic item, marked auto-added. */ /** Extension hint from a cloud file name (e.g. "Song.flac" → "flac"), for the * demuxer. Returns undefined when there's no extension. */ /** The now-playing card's view of a queue item, before the engine has decoded * anything from the file itself. * * `cover` carries the item's own art when it has any. YT Music hands us a * thumbnail with the listing, and hardcoding null here meant the card waited * forever for art the engine could never supply: googlevideo streams a bare * DASH audio track with no embedded tags, so the sidebar sat on its gradient * while the very same cover showed in every list. Cloud items benefit too — a * preloaded cover shows immediately and saves the lazy fetch. Local files carry * none here and still get theirs decoded, exactly as before. */ /** The duration to show for the current track on this progress tick. * * A streamed track (cloud/phone/YouTube Music) reports a `durationSecs` off * `engine:progress` that *grows* as more of the file downloads/decodes — * it starts around a second and climbs toward the real length. Adopting * that number the moment it arrives (the old `p.durationSecs ?? s.durationSecs`) * made the seek bar's total visibly count up from 0:01 to 3:42 on every * streamed track, and made src-tauri re-publish OS media metadata each time * the number changed. * * `itemDuration` (the queue item's own known duration, when it has one) is * trusted instead for as long as the engine's own total hasn't caught up to * it — a growing partial, by definition, can only under-report the true * length. Once the engine's number reaches or exceeds the item's, it's * adopted (it may be more accurate — e.g. the item's duration came from a * tag estimate) and kept from then on even if the engine stops reporting * one (`engineDuration` going `null` again mid-track isn't expected, but * falls back to `prevDuration` rather than losing the value either way). */ /* ----------------------------------------------------------------- play order */ /** Fisher–Yates shuffle (in place). */ /** Build a play order over `len` items, keeping `start` first when shuffling. */ /** Next order position in `dir`, honouring repeat; null when there's nowhere to go. */ export const useEngineStore = create<EngineStore>((set, get) => { // Not part of rendered state: distinguishes user-stop from natural end. let userStopped = false; // Whether the engine is currently driving a multi-track gapless queue (true), // versus a single track / stream the store advances itself (false). Tags * only — never the ~100 KB base64 cover, so a 10k-track queue doesn't hold * ~1 GB of covers in memory; covers resolve lazily per visible queue row * (and via {@link fillNowPlayingCover} for the current track). Resolved * tags are batched and applied as one new queue array per flush. */ /** Replace the queue and start playing `index`. */ /** A new listening intent: the old radio session must not graft onto it. * Called by every path that replaces the queue — not just * `setQueueAndPlay` — so a session from before can't survive into an * unrelated queue (e.g. switching to an internet radio station or an * incoming cast while a YT Music radio session was live). Pending warmups * die with the session too: nothing from the old queue is worth warming, * and "radio-batch" in particular is never re-scheduled by `startPlayback` * (unlike "video"/"batch"), so it would otherwise leak into whatever * queue replaces this one. */ /** Extend the live queue in place: the current stream keeps running; the * new items only lengthen `queue` and `order`. Appended in listed order * even under shuffle — a radio is already a curated order. */ /** If the queue ran dry before a radio page landed, pick up where it ended. */ /** Run one radio fetch and append what it returns. Failures are silent — * the next track-advance retries via maybeExtendRadio; playback is never * interrupted for a queue that only might run out. */ /** Keep an endless queue endless — called on every track advance. */ /** Decide what to play when the current item ends naturally. */ return { state: defaultEngineState, meters: idleMeters, spectrum: [], companderGr: IDLE_COMPANDER_GR, metersLive: false, playing: false, paused: false, nowPlaying: null, nowPlayingMeta: null, currentTrackPath: null, currentYtVideoId: null, positionSecs: 0, durationSecs: null, seekable: false, buffering: false, queue: [], queueIndex: -1, order: [], orderPos: -1, shuffle: false, repeat: "off", resumeAt: null, restoreSession: (session) => { const cur = get(); if (cur.queue.length > 0 || cur.playing) return false; const qi = session.order[session.orderPos]; const item = qi === undefined ? undefined : session.queue[qi]; if (!item) return false; const live = item.source === "radio"; set({ queue: session.queue, order: session.order, orderPos: session.orderPos, queueIndex: qi!, shuffle: session.shuffle, repeat: session.repeat, nowPlaying: item.title, nowPlayingMeta: itemMeta(item), // "Is there something to play", not "is it playing": the bar shows the // track with a Play button. Nothing is loaded until that is pressed. playing: false, paused: true, resumeAt: live ? 0 : session.positionSecs, positionSecs: live ? 0 : session.positionSecs, durationSecs: item.durationSecs, // A known-length track can be scrubbed before it loads (it just moves // the resume point). seekable: !live && (item.durationSecs ?? 0) > 0, buffering: false, }); fillNowPlayingCover(item); return true; }, hydrate: (state) => set({ state }), setPower: (power) => { set((s) => ({ state: { ...s.state, power } })); void engineSetPower(power).catch(() => { }); }, setMasterVolume: (masterVolume) => { set((s) => ({ state: { ...s.state, masterVolume } })); nodes.name: QueueSource
nodes.body_text: type QueueSource = "local" | "phone" | "cloud" | "ytmusic" | "radio" | "cast";

nodes.name: RepeatMode
nodes.body_text: type RepeatMode = "off" | "all" | "one";

nodes.name: QueueItem
nodes.body_text: interface QueueItem { /** Stable id for highlight/dedup: local path | phone/cloud id | url. */ id: string; source: QueueSource; title: string; artist: string | null; album: string | null; durationSecs: number | null; /** Resolved cover (a `data:` URI), e.g. a cloud track's art once its tags * load. Local/phone items resolve art lazily from their path instead. */ cover?: string | null; // Exactly one payload is set, matching `source`: track?: LibraryTrack; device?: PhoneDevice; phoneTrack?: PhoneTrack; cloud?: CloudEntry; ytTrack?: YtTrack; radioUrl?: string; /** Queued by radio (Autoplay), not by the user — the queue UI badges these. */ autoAdded?: boolean; }

nodes.name: localItem
nodes.body_text: function localItem(track: LibraryTrack): QueueItem { return { id: track.path, source: "local", title: track.title, artist: track.artist, album: track.album, durationSecs: track.durationSecs, track, }; }

nodes.name: phoneItem
nodes.signature: function phoneItem(device: PhoneDevice, t: PhoneTrack): QueueItem
nodes.body_text: function phoneItem(device: PhoneDevice, t: PhoneTrack): QueueItem { return { id: t.id, source: "phone", title: t.title, artist: t.artist, album: t.album, durationSecs: t.durationMs != null ? t.durationMs / 1000 : null, device, phoneTrack: t, }; }

nodes.name: cloudItem
nodes.body_text: function cloudItem(file: CloudEntry): QueueItem { return { id: file.id, source: "cloud", title: file.name, artist: null, album: null, durationSecs: null, cloud: file, }; }

nodes.name: ytmusicItem
nodes.body_text: function ytmusicItem(t: YtTrack): QueueItem { return { id: t.videoId, source: "ytmusic", title: t.title, artist: t.artist, album: t.album, durationSecs: t.durationSecs, // The API hands us the thumbnail with the listing, so the card has its art // from the start — no lazy per-track cover fetch like cloud needs. cover: t.thumbnail, ytTrack: t, }; }

nodes.name: radioItem
nodes.body_text: function radioItem(t: YtTrack): QueueItem { return { ...ytmusicItem(t), autoAdded: true }; }

nodes.name: extFromName
nodes.body_text: function extFromName(name: string): string | undefined { const dot = name.lastIndexOf("."); return dot > 0 && dot < name.length - 1 ? name.slice(dot + 1).toLowerCase() : undefined; }

nodes.name: itemMeta
nodes.body_text: function itemMeta(item: QueueItem): TrackMeta { return { title: item.title, artist: item.artist, album: item.album, cover: item.cover ?? null, }; }

nodes.name: reconcileDuration
nodes.signature: function reconcileDuration( itemDuration: number | null, engineDuration: number | null, prevDuration: number | null, ): number | null
nodes.body_text: function reconcileDuration( itemDuration: number | null, engineDuration: number | null, prevDuration: number | null, ): number | null { if (itemDuration != null && (engineDuration == null || engineDuration < itemDuration)) { return itemDuration; } return engineDuration ?? prevDuration; }

nodes.name: shuffleInPlace
nodes.body_text: function shuffleInPlace<T>(arr: T[]): T[] { for (let i = arr.length - 1; i > 0; i--) { const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1)); [arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j]!, arr[i]!]; } return arr; }

nodes.name: buildOrder
nodes.signature: function buildOrder( len: number, shuffle: boolean, start: number, ): { order: number[]; orderPos: number }
nodes.body_text: function buildOrder( len: number, shuffle: boolean, start: number, ): { order: number[]; orderPos: number } { const identity = Array.from({ length: len }, (_, i) => i); if (!shuffle || len <= 1) return { order: identity, orderPos: start }; const rest = identity.filter((i) => i !== start); shuffleInPlace(rest); return { order: [start, ...rest], orderPos: 0 }; }

nodes.name: stepOrder
nodes.signature: function stepOrder( pos: number, len: number, repeat: RepeatMode, dir: 1 | -1, ): number | null
nodes.body_text: function stepOrder( pos: number, len: number, repeat: RepeatMode, dir: 1 | -1, ): number | null { if (len === 0 || pos < 0) return null; const n = pos + dir; if (n >= 0 && n < len) return n; if (repeat === "all") return ((n % len) + len) % len; return null; }

nodes.name: EngineStore
nodes.body_text: interface EngineStore { state: EngineState; meters: MeterFrame; spectrum: number[]; /** Per-band compander gain-reduction in dB (10 values, ≤0).
